questions.stem: A hospital microbiology laboratory tests a blood isolate of Staphylococcus aureus against doubling dilutions of an antibiotic. After 24 hours of incubation, the tubes containing 0.25, 0.5, and 1 microgram/mL are visibly cloudy, while the tubes containing 2, 4, and 8 micrograms/mL remain clear. Which of the following values should be reported as the minimum inhibitory concentration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 0.25 micrograms/mL

choices.label: B
choices.text: 1 microgram/mL

choices.label: C
choices.text: 1.5 micrograms/mL

choices.label: D
choices.text: 2 micrograms/mL

choices.label: E
choices.text: 8 micrograms/mL

explanation.summary: The MIC is the lowest antibiotic concentration at which there is no visible growth in the dilution series.
explanation.whyCorrect: In broth or tube dilution testing, a standard concentration of the organism is mixed with increasing concentrations of antibiotic and incubated for about 24 hours. Turbidity means the organism grew; a clear tube means growth was inhibited. The lowest concentration with no visible growth, 2 micrograms/mL here, is reported as the MIC.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This tube is cloudy, so the organism grew freely at this concentration.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is the highest concentration that still permitted growth, not the lowest that inhibited it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dilution panels use doubling concentrations, and this concentration was not tested.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Growth was inhibited here, but this is not the lowest inhibitory concentration.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: An attending asks a student on rounds to define the measurement that the microbiology laboratory uses to determine antibiotic susceptibility. Which of the following is the best definition of the minimum inhibitory concentration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The average drug concentration held across a dosing interval

choices.label: B
choices.text: The concentration at which the isolate is reported as resistant

choices.label: C
choices.text: The lowest antibiotic concentration that inhibits growth of the organism

choices.label: D
choices.text: The lowest concentration producing a 99.9% fall in colony count

choices.label: E
choices.text: The peak serum concentration reached after a standard dose

explanation.summary: MIC is the minimal antibiotic concentration required to inhibit growth of the organism in question.
explanation.whyCorrect: MIC is the measurement used in clinical and hospital practice to determine antibiotic susceptibility. It is the minimal concentration that inhibits growth of the bacterium, determined by incubating a standard inoculum with increasing drug concentrations and reading the lowest concentration without visible growth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Average exposure over an interval relates to the area under the concentration-time curve, not the MIC.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Resistance is assigned by comparing the MIC with a published breakpoint; it is not the definition of MIC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: That describes the minimum bactericidal concentration, which reflects killing rather than inhibition.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Peak concentration is a pharmacokinetic property of the drug and dose, not a measure of the organism.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A research laboratory wants to know whether a new agent kills bacteria or only halts their replication. Dilution tubes are incubated and then subcultured onto agar. Which of the following findings defines the minimum bactericidal concentration for this organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The concentration that equals one half of the peak serum level

choices.label: B
choices.text: The concentration that keeps drug above the MIC for the whole interval

choices.label: C
choices.text: The lowest concentration at which the isolate is reported susceptible

choices.label: D
choices.text: The lowest concentration causing a 99.9% fall in the original colony count

choices.label: E
choices.text: The lowest concentration that prevents visible turbidity in the broth

explanation.summary: MBC is the concentration that produces a 99.9% reduction in the original bacterial colony count, defined practically as inability to re-culture the bacteria.
explanation.whyCorrect: MBC is determined in the same type of dilution testing used for MIC. Rather than reading turbidity, the tubes are subcultured, and the concentration corresponding to a 99.9% reduction in the starting colony count, so that the organism can no longer be re-cultured, is the MBC.

whyWrongByChoice.A: MBC is a property of the organism-drug pair and is unrelated to half the peak serum level.
whyWrongByChoice.B: That describes the time-above-MIC pharmacodynamic parameter, not a laboratory endpoint.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Susceptible is an interpretation made by comparing the MIC with a breakpoint.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Absence of turbidity defines the MIC, which reflects inhibition of growth rather than cell death.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A student watches a technologist read a microdilution panel inoculated with a patient's isolate. Several wells are cloudy and several are clear. Cloudiness in a well indicates which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: That well was inoculated with no organism

choices.label: B
choices.text: The antibiotic has precipitated out of the broth

choices.label: C
choices.text: The concentration in that well exceeds the breakpoint

choices.label: D
choices.text: The organism grew at that drug concentration

choices.label: E
choices.text: The organism has been killed by the antibiotic

explanation.summary: Turbidity in a dilution well means bacterial growth; clearing means growth was inhibited.
explanation.whyCorrect: After roughly 24 hours of incubation, the mixtures are examined by eye and with computer assistance for cloudiness. Turbidity indicates that the bacterial organism grew at that concentration, so the MIC must lie at a higher concentration in the series.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Every well in the panel receives a standard concentration of the patient's organism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Precipitation is not what the reader is assessing; the panel is read for bacterial growth.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Wells above the breakpoint would be expected to be clear if the isolate is susceptible.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Killing would leave the well clear, and re-culture would be required to demonstrate it.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A clinician notices that an MIC of 2 micrograms/mL is reported as susceptible for one organism-drug pair but not for another. The cutoff MIC that separates these interpretations is closely monitored and published by a national organization. This cutoff is best termed which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The area under the concentration-time curve

choices.label: B
choices.text: The breakpoint for that organism-drug pair

choices.label: C
choices.text: The local resistance rate for that drug

choices.label: D
choices.text: The minimum bactericidal concentration

choices.label: E
choices.text: The peak-to-MIC ratio of the drug

explanation.summary: The breakpoint is the particular cutoff MIC, specific to each organism-antibiotic pair, at or below which the isolate is called susceptible.
explanation.whyCorrect: For each organism-antibiotic pair there is a particular cutoff MIC that is considered susceptible. That MIC is called the breakpoint, and it is closely monitored and published by a national organization so that laboratories interpret MIC values consistently.

whyWrongByChoice.A: AUC is a pharmacokinetic exposure measure, not an interpretive threshold.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Local resistance rates are aggregated in antibiograms and do not define susceptibility for one isolate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The MBC is a killing endpoint determined by subculture, not an interpretive cutoff.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cmax/MIC is a pharmacodynamic ratio that predicts efficacy of certain drugs.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A student notices that culture and sensitivity reports list MIC values but essentially never list MBC values. Which of the following best explains this practice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: MBC can be determined only after the patient completes therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: MBC cannot be measured for organisms that will grow in broth culture

choices.label: C
choices.text: MBC is hard to obtain and adds little value outside of research

choices.label: D
choices.text: MBC is identical to the MIC for nearly every antibacterial agent

choices.label: E
choices.text: MBC shifts too quickly during therapy to be reported reliably

explanation.summary: MBC is rarely obtained outside research because it is difficult to measure and has little clinical value.
explanation.whyCorrect: MICs can be calculated with commercially available assays that return results in about 24 hours. MBC is much more difficult to obtain and has little clinical value given the efficacy of bacteriostatic action, so MBC data are rarely acquired for patients outside of research purposes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nothing about the assay requires waiting until therapy is complete.
whyWrongByChoice.B: MBC is determined from the same broth dilution testing used to determine the MIC.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MBC usually exceeds the MIC, and the size of that gap is what separates cidal from static agents.
whyWrongByChoice.E: MBC is a property of the organism-drug pair measured in vitro, not a value that fluctuates hourly in the patient.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: Testing of a patient's isolate yields an MIC of 2 micrograms/mL and an MBC of 4 micrograms/mL for drug X. Based on this relationship, drug X is best classified against this organism as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bactericidal, because the MBC/MIC ratio is 4 or less

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bacteriostatic, because the MBC is higher than the MIC

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bacteriostatic, because the MBC/MIC ratio is above 4

choices.label: D
choices.text: Concentration dependent, because the MBC is measurable

choices.label: E
choices.text: Time dependent, because the two values are close together

explanation.summary: An MBC/MIC ratio of 4 or less defines a bactericidal agent.
explanation.whyCorrect: Whether a drug is considered bacteriostatic or bactericidal depends on the comparison of MIC to MBC. A ratio of MBC to MIC of 4 or less is classified as bactericidal; here the ratio is 4/2, or 2, so drug X is bactericidal against this isolate.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The MBC almost always exceeds the MIC; the size of the ratio, not its direction, is what matters.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The ratio here is 2, which is not above 4.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Concentration dependence is a pharmacodynamic property predicted by Cmax/MIC, not by the MBC/MIC ratio.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Time dependence refers to how long drug levels stay above the MIC and is not derived from the MBC.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A second agent is tested against the same isolate and yields an MIC of 0.5 micrograms/mL and an MBC of 8 micrograms/mL. Which of the following is the most accurate conclusion about this agent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is bactericidal, because its MBC/MIC ratio is 4 or less

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is bactericidal, because its MIC is lower than that of the first agent

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is bacteriostatic, because its MBC/MIC ratio is above 4

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the better therapeutic option, because its MIC is lower

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is time dependent, because its MBC is far above its MIC

explanation.summary: An MBC/MIC ratio greater than 4 defines a bacteriostatic agent.
explanation.whyCorrect: Here the ratio is 8 divided by 0.5, or 16, which is well above 4, so this agent is classified as bacteriostatic against this isolate. Bacteriostatic agents halt bacterial growth and replication, which lets an immunocompetent host clear the organism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The ratio is 16, not 4 or less.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A low MIC says nothing about whether the drug kills; the MBC/MIC relationship does.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A lower MIC does not make an antibiotic the better choice, and MICs should not be compared across drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Time dependence describes how drug concentration relates to the MIC over time, not the MBC/MIC gap.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: An otherwise healthy 22-year-old woman is treated with a bacteriostatic antibiotic for a skin infection and recovers completely. Which of the following best explains how a drug that does not kill bacteria cured her infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Halting bacterial growth let her immune system clear the organism

choices.label: B
choices.text: The drug lowered the organism's MIC below the published breakpoint

choices.label: C
choices.text: The drug raised the organism's MBC and cut the colony count by 99.9%

choices.label: D
choices.text: The drug reached a peak many times above the organism's MBC

choices.label: E
choices.text: The drug was converted to a bactericidal metabolite in the tissue

explanation.summary: Bacteriostatic agents stop bacterial growth and replication so that an immunocompetent host can clear the infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacteriostatic antibacterials halt the growth of bacteria. When bacterial growth and replication are halted, the immunocompetent host is able to clear the organism more easily, which makes these agents as effective as bactericidal agents for most infections.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Antibiotics do not lower an organism's MIC; the MIC is an inherent property of the organism-drug pair.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A 99.9% reduction in colony count defines the MBC and describes bactericidal, not bacteriostatic, action.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Exceeding the MBC would mean the drug is acting as a bactericidal agent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Conversion to a killing metabolite is not how bacteriostatic activity produces cure.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: Two agents are tested against the same isolate. For agent Y the MBC is only slightly higher than the MIC, whereas for agent Z the MBC is many times the MIC. Which of the following statements about agent Y is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It behaves more bactericidally than agent Z

choices.label: B
choices.text: It has a broader spectrum of activity than agent Z

choices.label: C
choices.text: It reaches higher tissue concentrations than agent Z

choices.label: D
choices.text: It requires less frequent dosing than agent Z

choices.label: E
choices.text: It selects for resistance more readily than agent Z

explanation.summary: As the MIC approaches the MBC, an agent is considered more bactericidal.
explanation.whyCorrect: Classification as bacteriostatic or bactericidal rests on the comparison of MIC to MBC. When the two values converge, only a little more drug is needed to kill than to inhibit, so the agent is considered more bactericidal; a wide gap indicates bacteriostatic behavior.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Spectrum reflects which organisms an agent covers, which these two values do not describe.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tissue penetration is a pharmacokinetic property and cannot be inferred from MIC and MBC values.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dosing frequency follows the pharmacodynamic parameter, such as time above MIC, not the MBC/MIC ratio.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nothing about a narrow MBC/MIC gap implies greater selection for resistance.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man is admitted with streptococcal endocarditis, and the team deliberately selects a bactericidal rather than a bacteriostatic regimen. Bactericidal therapy is generally preferred in which of the following pairs of infections?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cellulitis and otitis media

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cystitis and pharyngitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Endocarditis and meningitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gastroenteritis and conjunctivitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sinusitis and bronchitis

explanation.summary: For most infections static and cidal agents perform similarly, but bactericidal drugs are preferred for endocarditis and meningitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Outcomes with appropriate bacteriostatic and bactericidal therapy are similar for most infections. Certain infections are the exception, because the immune system cannot act effectively at that anatomic location; endocarditis and meningitis are the classic settings in which bactericidal drugs are preferred.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Skin and middle ear infections in an immunocompetent host do not require cidal therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: These are ordinary infections in which appropriately chosen static or cidal therapy performs similarly.
whyWrongByChoice.D: These infections are not the settings in which killing rather than inhibition is required.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neither site poses the immune access problem that drives a cidal requirement.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman admitted with a severe bloodstream infection has been on chronic immunosuppressive therapy for rheumatoid arthritis. Her condition improved initially but the infection is not resolving completely. Which of the following considerations most strongly favors choosing a bactericidal agent for her?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bactericidal agents are dosed once daily and improve adherence

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bactericidal agents are less often reported as intermediate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bactericidal agents have lower MICs than bacteriostatic agents

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bactericidal agents reach higher concentrations in every tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Her suppressed immune system cannot clear merely inhibited organisms

explanation.summary: Bacteriostatic therapy depends on a functioning immune system, so bactericidal agents are preferred in immunosuppressed patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacteriostatic agents work by halting growth so the host can clear the pathogen. In an immunosuppressed patient the immune system cannot take care of the pathogen once growth has been halted, so bactericidal agents are often preferred in these patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dosing frequency follows the pharmacodynamic parameter, and many cidal drugs are dosed several times daily.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intermediate is an interpretive category based on MIC and is unrelated to cidal or static class.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MIC values depend on the organism-drug pair and do not track with cidal versus static classification.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tissue penetration varies by drug and site and is not a property of bactericidal agents as a group.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: The culture and sensitivity report for that same immunosuppressed 55-year-old woman lists the antibiotic she is currently receiving as intermediate against the organism isolated from her blood. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change to an antibiotic the organism is reported susceptible to

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continue the current drug and add a second intermediate agent

choices.label: C
choices.text: Continue the current drug but extend the planned duration

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repeat the blood culture in 48 hours before changing anything

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stop antibiotics and observe, since she improved at first

explanation.summary: An intermediate result means coverage is not reliable, so therapy should be changed to an agent reported as susceptible.
explanation.whyCorrect: The culture and sensitivity report classifies each antibiotic as susceptible, intermediate, or resistant for that isolate. Intermediate coverage against the bacteria in her blood is a reason her infection is not resolving, so choosing another antibiotic to which the organism is susceptible is the best course of action.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Stacking a second unreliable agent does not correct the underlying coverage problem.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A longer course of a drug with intermediate activity does not make that drug adequate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Waiting delays effective therapy when the report already identifies a better option.
whyWrongByChoice.E: She has an incompletely treated bloodstream infection and is immunosuppressed; stopping therapy is unsafe.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A patient with bacterial meningitis has an isolate whose lowest reported MIC belongs to an antibiotic known to penetrate the central nervous system poorly. Which of the following principles best explains why this agent may still be a poor choice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A low MIC shows the drug is bacteriostatic rather than bactericidal

choices.label: B
choices.text: MIC values are valid only for organisms grown from blood cultures

choices.label: C
choices.text: MIC values fall steadily as the duration of therapy increases

choices.label: D
choices.text: Published breakpoints apply only to drugs given intravenously

choices.label: E
choices.text: The drug must reach adequate concentration at the site of infection

explanation.summary: Having the lowest MIC does not make an antibiotic the best choice, because drugs reach different concentrations at different body sites.
explanation.whyCorrect: Different antibiotics achieve different concentrations in different places in the body, such as the central nervous system versus the bladder. An agent with a very low MIC that cannot reach the infected compartment will not treat the infection, which is why site of infection governs the choice.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cidal versus static classification comes from the MBC/MIC comparison, not from a low MIC.
whyWrongByChoice.B: MIC testing is performed on isolates from any patient sample, not only blood.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The MIC is a property of the organism-drug pair and does not drift downward with treatment time.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Breakpoints are set for organism-drug pairs and are not restricted to intravenous agents.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A resident ranks five antibiotics reported for a single isolate from lowest to highest MIC and proposes treating with the drug at the top of the list. Which of the following is the most important flaw in this approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: MIC results are reported only as susceptible, intermediate, or resistant

choices.label: B
choices.text: MICs are measured at concentrations far above those reached in serum

choices.label: C
choices.text: MICs differ so much between laboratories that none can be compared

choices.label: D
choices.text: MICs for one organism should not be compared across different drugs

choices.label: E
choices.text: MICs measure killing of bacteria rather than inhibition of growth

explanation.summary: MIC values for one organism should not be compared between different antibiotics when selecting therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Just because an antibiotic has the lowest MIC for a pathogen does not mean it is the best choice. Because different drugs achieve different concentrations at different sites, MICs for a single organism generally should not be compared across different drugs in selecting therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Reports give both the numeric MIC and its interpretation, so the numbers are indeed available.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The dilution series is designed around clinically relevant concentrations and breakpoints.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Testing is standardized and breakpoints are published nationally, so results are reproducible.
whyWrongByChoice.E: MIC measures inhibition of growth; killing is measured by the MBC.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: The activity of a certain antibiotic against microorganisms correlates with the duration of time that its concentration remains above the MIC. This property is best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacteriostatic activity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Concentration-dependent activity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Post-antibiotic effect

choices.label: D
choices.text: Synergistic activity

choices.label: E
choices.text: Time-dependent activity

explanation.summary: Antibiotics whose efficacy tracks with T > MIC are called time-dependent agents.
explanation.whyCorrect: For certain antibiotics, activity against microorganisms correlates with the duration of time that the drug concentration remains above the MIC. These agents are described as time dependent, and practically they require more frequent dosing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bacteriostatic refers to inhibiting growth and is determined by the MBC/MIC comparison.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Concentration dependence means efficacy tracks with the peak-to-MIC ratio instead.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A post-antibiotic effect describes suppression persisting after levels fall, which is not what is defined here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Synergy describes two drugs acting together, not one drug's exposure over time.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A patient is started on a beta-lactam whose antibacterial activity is predicted by T > MIC. Which of the following dosing strategies best matches this pharmacodynamic property?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A loading dose with no further doses given

choices.label: B
choices.text: A single large dose given once each week

choices.label: C
choices.text: Alternating doses given every other day

choices.label: D
choices.text: One large dose daily to maximize the peak

choices.label: E
choices.text: Smaller doses given three or four times daily

explanation.summary: Time-dependent antibiotics require frequent dosing to keep concentrations above the MIC.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antibiotics in the time-dependent category are effective in proportion to how long their concentration stays above the MIC. Practically, this means they require more frequent dosing, such as three or four times daily, rather than large widely spaced doses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A loading dose alone cannot maintain concentrations above the MIC over a course of therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Weekly dosing would leave concentrations below the MIC for nearly the entire interval.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Every-other-day dosing leaves long periods of subtherapeutic concentration.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Maximizing the peak is the strategy for concentration-dependent drugs predicted by Cmax/MIC.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: For some antibiotics the efficacy of therapy is determined by the ratio of the peak drug concentration to the MIC. Agents with this property are described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacteriostatic agents

choices.label: B
choices.text: Breakpoint-dependent agents

choices.label: C
choices.text: Concentration-dependent agents

choices.label: D
choices.text: Narrow-spectrum agents

choices.label: E
choices.text: Time-dependent agents

explanation.summary: When the Cmax/MIC ratio predicts efficacy, the antibiotic is concentration dependent.
explanation.whyCorrect: For some antibiotics, the ratio of the peak concentration of drug over the MIC determines efficacy. These agents are referred to as concentration dependent, and clinically they are often dosed once daily using larger doses to drive the peak well above the MIC.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bacteriostatic describes inhibition of growth and comes from the MBC/MIC comparison.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Breakpoints are interpretive MIC cutoffs and do not define a pharmacodynamic class.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Spectrum describes which organisms are covered and is unrelated to this ratio.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Time-dependent agents are defined by how long levels stay above the MIC, not by the peak.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with a gram-negative bloodstream infection is prescribed an aminoglycoside as a single large daily dose rather than in divided doses. Which of the following best explains this regimen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Its activity depends on an MBC/MIC ratio above 4

choices.label: B
choices.text: Its activity depends on halting bacterial replication

choices.label: C
choices.text: Its activity depends on the peak relative to the MIC

choices.label: D
choices.text: Its activity depends on the published breakpoint

choices.label: E
choices.text: Its activity depends on time spent above the MIC

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides are concentration-dependent bactericidal drugs predicted by Cmax/MIC, so they are given as large once-daily doses.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycosides are grouped with the fluoroquinolones, metronidazole, and daptomycin as bactericidal agents whose predictive parameter is Cmax/MIC. Concentration-dependent antibiotics are often dosed once daily and rely on larger doses to push the peak well above the MIC.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An MBC/MIC ratio above 4 would make the drug bacteriostatic, which aminoglycosides are not.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aminoglycosides kill bacteria rather than simply halting replication.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The breakpoint is an interpretive cutoff and does not dictate the dosing interval.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Time above MIC predicts activity for beta-lactams, which need frequent dosing instead.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: For vancomycin, the best predictor of antibacterial activity is the ratio of which of the following to the MIC?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The area under the concentration-time curve

choices.label: B
choices.text: The dosing interval in hours

choices.label: C
choices.text: The minimum bactericidal concentration

choices.label: D
choices.text: The peak serum concentration

choices.label: E
choices.text: The trough serum concentration

explanation.summary: Vancomycin activity is predicted by the AUC/MIC ratio.
explanation.whyCorrect: For some antibiotics the best predictor of activity is the ratio of the area under the concentration-time curve to the MIC. Vancomycin, a slowly bactericidal agent, falls into this AUC/MIC category, as do the macrolides, tetracyclines, and linezolid.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The dosing interval is a regimen feature, not a predictive PK/PD parameter.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MBC is a laboratory killing endpoint, not an exposure measure used in PK/PD ratios.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cmax/MIC predicts activity for fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, metronidazole, and daptomycin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The trough alone is not the pharmacodynamic parameter used to predict activity.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man with cellulitis is admitted and started on a penicillin. This class of antibiotics is best characterized by which of the following pairs of properties?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bactericidal activity predicted by AUC / MIC

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bactericidal activity predicted by Cmax / MIC

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bactericidal activity predicted by Time > MIC

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bacteriostatic activity predicted by AUC / MIC

choices.label: E
choices.text: Bacteriostatic activity predicted by Time > MIC

explanation.summary: Penicillins are bactericidal agents whose predictive PK/PD parameter is time above the MIC.
explanation.whyCorrect: Penicillins, along with cephalosporins, carbapenems, and monobactams, are bactericidal and have Time > MIC as their predictive PK/PD parameter. That is why these agents are typically given at frequent intervals rather than as a single large daily dose.

whyWrongByChoice.A: AUC/MIC with bactericidal activity describes vancomycin, which kills slowly.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cmax/MIC applies to fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, metronidazole, and daptomycin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: AUC/MIC with bacteriostatic activity describes macrolides, tetracyclines, and linezolid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Penicillins kill bacteria rather than merely inhibiting their growth.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A patient with a resistant gram-negative infection is switched from cefepime to meropenem, and aztreonam is considered as an alternative. Cephalosporins, carbapenems, and monobactams share which of the following predictive PK/PD parameters?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AUC / MIC

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cmax / MIC

choices.label: C
choices.text: MBC / MIC

choices.label: D
choices.text: Time > MIC

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trough / MIC

explanation.summary: All of the beta-lactam families are bactericidal with Time > MIC as the predictive parameter.
explanation.whyCorrect: Penicillins, cephalosporins, carbapenems, and monobactams are grouped together as bactericidal agents whose activity is predicted by the time that the concentration stays above the MIC. Switching between agents within these families therefore does not change the need for frequent dosing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: AUC/MIC characterizes vancomycin as well as macrolides, tetracyclines, and linezolid.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cmax/MIC characterizes fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, metronidazole, and daptomycin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MBC/MIC is the laboratory ratio used to classify an agent as cidal or static.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trough relative to MIC is not one of the predictive parameters used for these agents.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman with a methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia is treated with vancomycin, which is noted to kill this organism slowly. Which of the following pairs correctly characterizes vancomycin?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bactericidal and rapid, with activity predicted by Cmax / MIC

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bactericidal and rapid, with activity predicted by Time > MIC

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bactericidal but slow, with activity predicted by AUC / MIC

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bacteriostatic, with activity predicted by Cmax / MIC

choices.label: E
choices.text: Bacteriostatic, with activity predicted by Time > MIC

explanation.summary: Vancomycin is a slowly bactericidal agent whose activity is predicted by AUC/MIC.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vancomycin occupies its own row among the common antibacterials: it is bactericidal, but slowly so, and its predictive PK/PD parameter is the ratio of the area under the concentration-time curve to the MIC rather than peak or time above MIC.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cmax/MIC applies to the rapidly bactericidal concentration-dependent agents, not vancomycin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Time > MIC is the parameter for the beta-lactam families.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vancomycin kills bacteria and is not classified as bacteriostatic.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neither half of this pairing applies to vancomycin.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman with pyelonephritis is treated with levofloxacin given once daily. Fluoroquinolones are bactericidal, and their antibacterial activity is best predicted by which of the following parameters?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AUC / MBC

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cmax / MIC

choices.label: C
choices.text: MBC / MIC

choices.label: D
choices.text: Time > MIC

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trough / MIC

explanation.summary: Fluoroquinolones are concentration-dependent bactericidal agents predicted by Cmax/MIC.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fluoroquinolones are grouped with aminoglycosides, metronidazole, and daptomycin as bactericidal agents whose predictive parameter is Cmax/MIC. Because efficacy depends on how far the peak exceeds the MIC, these drugs are often given once daily in larger doses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: PK/PD ratios are constructed against the MIC, not the MBC.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MBC/MIC classifies an agent as bactericidal or bacteriostatic; it does not predict dosing efficacy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Time above MIC predicts activity for penicillins, cephalosporins, carbapenems, and monobactams.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trough relative to MIC is not among the predictive parameters described for these drugs.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: Metronidazole and daptomycin are grouped with the aminoglycosides and fluoroquinolones when antibacterials are organized by pharmacodynamics. This grouping reflects which of the following shared characteristics?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bactericidal activity predicted by AUC / MIC

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bactericidal activity predicted by Cmax / MIC

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bactericidal activity predicted by Time > MIC

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bacteriostatic activity predicted by AUC / MIC

choices.label: E
choices.text: Bacteriostatic activity predicted by Time > MIC

explanation.summary: Fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, metronidazole, and daptomycin are all bactericidal, concentration-dependent agents.
explanation.whyCorrect: These four are listed together because they share both features: they kill bacteria as their primary action, and their efficacy is predicted by the ratio of peak concentration to MIC. Concentration-dependent agents are therefore given in larger, less frequent doses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bactericidal with AUC/MIC describes vancomycin, which kills slowly.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bactericidal with Time > MIC describes the beta-lactam families.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bacteriostatic AUC/MIC describes macrolides, tetracyclines, and linezolid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: No common class is bacteriostatic with Time > MIC as its parameter.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man with atypical pneumonia is treated with a macrolide, which is a bacteriostatic antibacterial. Which of the following agents shares that same classification?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Daptomycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gentamicin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Linezolid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Meropenem

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Macrolides, tetracyclines, and linezolid are the bacteriostatic agents among the common antibacterials.
explanation.whyCorrect: Macrolides are listed with tetracyclines and linezolid as bacteriostatic agents, all predicted by AUC/MIC. These drugs halt bacterial growth, and an immunocompetent host then clears the organism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Daptomycin is bactericidal with a Cmax/MIC parameter.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gentamicin is an aminoglycoside and is bactericidal and concentration dependent.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Meropenem is a carbapenem and is bactericidal with Time > MIC as its parameter.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin is bactericidal, though slowly, with an AUC/MIC parameter.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: Tetracyclines and linezolid halt bacterial replication rather than killing the organism outright. The antibacterial activity of these agents is best predicted by which of the following parameters?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AUC / MIC

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cmax / MIC

choices.label: C
choices.text: MBC / MIC

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peak-to-trough ratio

choices.label: E
choices.text: Time > MIC

explanation.summary: The bacteriostatic macrolides, tetracyclines, and linezolid are predicted by AUC/MIC.
explanation.whyCorrect: Macrolides, tetracyclines, and linezolid are grouped as bacteriostatic agents whose predictive PK/PD parameter is the ratio of the area under the concentration-time curve to the MIC, meaning that total drug exposure over the interval drives their effect.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cmax/MIC applies to fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, metronidazole, and daptomycin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MBC/MIC is a laboratory ratio used to classify agents as cidal or static.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The peak-to-trough ratio is not one of the predictive parameters used for these drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Time above MIC is the parameter for the bactericidal beta-lactam families.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man arrives in the emergency department with suspected acute bacterial meningitis. Antibiotics are administered immediately, before any culture or susceptibility result is available. This approach is best termed which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Definitive therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Empiric therapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prophylactic therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Suppressive therapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Synergistic therapy

explanation.summary: Empiric therapy is best-guess treatment started before culture and susceptibility results are known.
explanation.whyCorrect: When cultures have not yet identified the cause of an infection and treatment cannot wait, empiric therapy is started to cover the likely and most dangerous culprits. Acute bacterial meningitis is the classic setting in which minutes matter.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Definitive therapy is the regimen chosen after the culture and sensitivity report is available.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Prophylaxis is given to prevent infection in a patient who is not already infected.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Suppressive therapy aims to hold a chronic infection in check rather than treat an acute one.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Synergy describes two drugs whose combined effect exceeds the sum of their individual effects.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: For that same 70-year-old man with suspected bacterial meningitis, which of the following best justifies starting antibiotics rather than waiting for the microbiology laboratory?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibiotics given after cultures are drawn cannot penetrate the CNS

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cultures cannot identify any organism once antibiotics have started

choices.label: C
choices.text: Empiric regimens are narrower and therefore safer than definitive ones

choices.label: D
choices.text: MIC testing is inaccurate when performed on cerebrospinal fluid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Susceptibility testing takes about 24 hours or longer, and delay is dangerous

explanation.summary: MIC and identification testing take at least a day, and some infections cannot tolerate that delay.
explanation.whyCorrect: MIC, or sensitivity, testing takes about 24 hours or longer, and some cultures take days to return species identification or susceptibility results. In conditions such as acute bacterial meningitis, minutes really do matter, so best-guess coverage of the likely and most dangerous pathogens is started first.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Penetration into the central nervous system is a property of the drug, not of when cultures were drawn.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cultures obtained before antibiotics are still processed and reported normally.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Empiric regimens are broader than definitive therapy, which is why de-escalation follows.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Susceptibility testing is performed on isolates from any patient sample, including cerebrospinal fluid.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man who injects drugs and shares needles presents with a thigh abscess and has had several emergency department visits in the past month. The wound is sampled and sent for culture and sensitivity. Which of the following should most influence the antibiotic he is given before those results return?

choices.label: A
choices.text: His response to oral antibiotics given in childhood

choices.label: B
choices.text: His risk for MRSA together with local antibiogram resistance rates

choices.label: C
choices.text: The MBC of each candidate drug against staphylococci

choices.label: D
choices.text: The number of colonies reported on the initial Gram stain

choices.label: E
choices.text: The time each drug stays above its own MBC

explanation.summary: Empiric choice is driven by the likely pathogen given the patient's risk factors plus local resistance data.
explanation.whyCorrect: Injection drug use with shared needles and repeated healthcare contact substantially raises concern for a resistant organism, most notably MRSA. That risk, combined with the resistance rates shown in the local antibiogram, determines the empiric regimen while the culture and sensitivity result is pending.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Remote childhood antibiotic exposure does not predict the organism or its resistance pattern here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MBC values are rarely obtained clinically and have little value in choosing therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A colony count on Gram stain does not identify the organism or its susceptibility.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pharmacodynamic parameters are constructed against the MIC and guide dosing, not organism coverage.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A hospitalist must choose empiric therapy for a patient with a suspected intra-abdominal infection. Which of the following sets of considerations should guide that choice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cost of the drug, its route of administration, and the patient's insurance

choices.label: B
choices.text: The likely source, the flora normally found there, and local resistance rates

choices.label: C
choices.text: The MBC/MIC ratio, the drug half-life, and the degree of protein binding

choices.label: D
choices.text: The number of isolates in the antibiogram and the age of the patient

choices.label: E
choices.text: The white blood cell count, the temperature, and the heart rate at admission

explanation.summary: Empiric therapy requires knowing the disease process and probable source, the pathogens usually found there, and local resistance rates.
explanation.whyCorrect: Choosing empiric therapy requires an understanding of the patient's disease process and potential sources of infection, consideration of the most common pathogens, meaning the normal flora, based on the source of infection, and knowledge of local resistance rates from surveillance data and antibiograms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: These practical issues may affect the final prescription but do not determine microbiologic coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: These pharmacologic details inform dosing rather than selection of empiric coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The raw isolate count in an antibiogram is not what guides therapy; percent susceptibility is.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vital signs and white count indicate severity, not which organism is likely or which drug covers it.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A hospital publishes a periodic report listing each commonly isolated organism along with the percentage of those isolates susceptible to each antimicrobial drug. Which of the following best names that report?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A breakpoint table

choices.label: B
choices.text: A culture and sensitivity report

choices.label: C
choices.text: A minimum inhibitory concentration panel

choices.label: D
choices.text: A therapeutic drug monitoring chart

choices.label: E
choices.text: An antibiogram

explanation.summary: An antibiogram is a profile of how susceptible specific microorganisms are to a range of antimicrobial drugs.
explanation.whyCorrect: An antibiogram is built from aggregate culture and sensitivity data for a hospital or healthcare system and shows the percentage of organisms tested that are susceptible to each antimicrobial drug. It is a crucial tool for choosing empiric therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Breakpoints are the MIC cutoffs used to interpret an individual result.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A culture and sensitivity report covers one patient's isolate, not aggregate data.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An MIC panel is the dilution series used in the laboratory for a single isolate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Therapeutic drug monitoring tracks drug levels in an individual patient.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A pharmacist is assembling an institution's antibiogram for distribution to clinicians. Which of the following does such a document typically contain?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Individual MIC values for every patient isolate collected

choices.label: B
choices.text: Percent susceptibility by organism over roughly six months to a year

choices.label: C
choices.text: Recommended doses and intervals for each antimicrobial listed

choices.label: D
choices.text: The MBC/MIC ratio for each organism and antimicrobial pair

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treatment outcomes for patients infected with each organism

explanation.summary: Antibiograms report percent susceptibility by organism over a defined time frame, usually six months or one year.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antibiograms include the percentages of organisms tested that are susceptible to a particular antimicrobial drug, data drawn from a defined time frame that is usually one year or six months, and information about which antimicrobials are more or less effective for different organisms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Individual MIC values belong on each patient's culture and sensitivity report, not the aggregate table.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dosing recommendations come from pharmacology references rather than the susceptibility profile.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MBC data are rarely obtained at all and are not part of an antibiogram.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antibiograms report susceptibility, not patient treatment outcomes.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A culture and sensitivity report returns identifying the organism isolated from a patient's wound, followed by a column of antibiotics each marked S, I, or R. These letters convey which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The MBC of each antibiotic against the isolate

choices.label: B
choices.text: The percentage of local isolates susceptible to each agent

choices.label: C
choices.text: The rank of the antibiotics by their tissue penetration

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whether each agent is bactericidal, intermediate, or bacteriostatic

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whether the isolate is susceptible, intermediate, or resistant to each agent

explanation.summary: A culture and sensitivity report gives patient-specific susceptibility, reported as susceptible, intermediate, or resistant.
explanation.whyCorrect: The report identifies the organism and lists antibiotics with an interpretation of susceptible (S), intermediate (I), or resistant (R), derived from MIC testing of that patient's isolate. It gives the clinician patient-specific information about which agents will treat the infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: MBC is rarely determined and is not reported on clinical culture and sensitivity reports.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aggregate percent susceptibility appears in the antibiogram, not in one patient's report.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tissue penetration is a pharmacokinetic property that the laboratory does not report.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cidal versus static classification is a drug property and is not what S, I, and R denote.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A physician who moves to a hospital in another state finds that an empiric regimen she used successfully for years now frequently fails. Which of the following best explains why she should consult her new institution's antibiogram?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibiograms list entirely different organisms in different regions

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bacteria alter their MBC/MIC ratio when they move between regions

choices.label: C
choices.text: Breakpoints are set independently by each hospital laboratory

choices.label: D
choices.text: MIC testing methods differ substantially from state to state

choices.label: E
choices.text: Resistance rates vary widely between regions and individual facilities

explanation.summary: Resistance patterns differ by region and facility, which is why local antibiogram data guide empiric therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Different regions have variations in bacterial resistance rates and infection rates, and antibiograms can be specific to a facility, city, county, region, state, country, or the globe. Because resistance can vary widely between areas, the local antibiogram is a crucial tool in choosing empiric antibiotic therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The same common pathogens appear across regions; their susceptibility percentages differ.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An organism's MBC/MIC relationship is an intrinsic property and does not change with geography.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Breakpoints are closely monitored and published by a national organization rather than set locally.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Susceptibility testing is standardized; it is the resistance rates, not the methods, that differ.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: Three days after broad empiric therapy was begun for a wound infection, the culture and sensitivity report identifies a common gram-positive organism susceptible to several oral agents, and the patient is called and switched to one of them. This adjusted regimen is best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Definitive therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Empiric therapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prophylactic therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Suppressive therapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Synergistic therapy

explanation.summary: Therapy chosen using the culture and sensitivity report, after empiric coverage, is definitive therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: The culture and sensitivity report gives patient-specific information on the organism and which antibiotics will treat it. Applying clinical judgment to that report to select the best agent moves the patient from best-guess empiric therapy to definitive therapy, often allowing de-escalation to a narrower oral drug.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Empiric therapy is the best-guess regimen given before these results were available.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Prophylaxis is given to prevent infection, not to treat an established one.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Suppressive therapy holds a chronic infection in check rather than treating it to cure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Synergy refers to combining agents for greater than additive effect, which did not occur here.

questions.topicName: Principles of Antibacterial Drugs

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with community-acquired pneumonia is started on intravenous ceftriaxone. The drug kills the bacteria by interfering with assembly of the bacterial cell wall. Which of the following reactions is most directly blocked by this antibiotic?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activation of bacterial autolytic enzymes in the wall

choices.label: B
choices.text: Addition of the NAM-NAG unit to the growing glycan chain

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cross-linking of peptidoglycan chains by transpeptidase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Synthesis of the D-alanyl-D-alanine terminus of the peptide

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transfer of N-acetylmuramic acid onto the bactoprenol carrier

explanation.summary: Cephalosporins are beta-lactams that inhibit the transpeptidation reaction that cross-links peptidoglycan.
explanation.whyCorrect: The beta-lactam ring binds covalently to the active site of penicillin-binding proteins, the transpeptidases that cross-link adjacent peptidoglycan chains. With cross-linking blocked, peptidoglycan synthesis halts and the wall loses the rigidity that protects the cell from rupture. The organism then dies from loss of cell wall integrity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Activation of autolytic enzymes is one of the mechanisms attributed to the penicillins.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blocking addition of the NAM-NAG unit to the growing peptidoglycan chain is the mechanism of vancomycin, not of cephalosporins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cephalosporins mimic the D-alanyl-D-alanine terminus rather than preventing the cell from making it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Preventing NAM from joining bactoprenol is the mechanism of bacitracin.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: A student is grouping antibiotics by shared chemical structure and places the cephalosporins in the same structural class as the penicillins. Which structural feature accounts for this grouping?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A beta-lactam ring

choices.label: B
choices.text: A four-ring naphthacene nucleus

choices.label: C
choices.text: A glycopeptide backbone

choices.label: D
choices.text: A macrolide lactone ring

choices.label: E
choices.text: An aminocyclitol sugar core

explanation.summary: Cephalosporins are beta-lactam antibiotics, the same structural class as the penicillins.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cephalosporins carry the four-membered beta-lactam ring, and it is this ring that binds the penicillin-binding proteins. Because penicillins share the same ring, the two drug families are grouped together and also share cross-reactivity in allergic patients.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A four-ring naphthacene nucleus describes the tetracyclines, which are not beta-lactams.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A glycopeptide backbone describes vancomycin, which acts on the wall by a different mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A macrolide lactone ring defines the macrolides, which are protein synthesis inhibitors rather than cell wall agents.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An aminocyclitol sugar core describes the aminoglycosides, which bind the ribosome.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: Cephalosporins bind covalently to the active site of penicillin-binding proteins. This binding occurs because the antibiotic is a structural analog of which bacterial substrate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bactoprenol

choices.label: B
choices.text: D-alanyl-D-alanine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lipoteichoic acid

choices.label: D
choices.text: N-acetylglucosamine

choices.label: E
choices.text: N-acetylmuramic acid

explanation.summary: Beta-lactams mimic the D-Ala-D-Ala terminus of the peptidoglycan side chain.
explanation.whyCorrect: The amino-acid peptide on N-acetylmuramic acid terminates in D-alanyl-D-alanine, which is the natural substrate of the penicillin-binding protein. Cephalosporins resemble this dipeptide closely enough to enter the active site and bind it covalently, which permanently disables the enzyme.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bactoprenol is the lipid carrier that ferries wall subunits across the membrane and is the target of bacitracin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lipoteichoic acid is a gram-positive wall component that plays no part in transpeptidation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: N-acetylglucosamine is a sugar of the glycan backbone, not the substrate recognized by the transpeptidase active site.
whyWrongByChoice.E: N-acetylmuramic acid is the sugar that anchors the peptide, but the enzyme acts on the peptide terminus rather than the sugar.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: In a growing bacterium, a penicillin-binding protein removes the terminal alanine from a peptide side chain of peptidoglycan. What is the direct consequence of this reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A cross-link forms with a nearby peptide, giving the wall rigidity

choices.label: B
choices.text: A new N-acetylglucosamine subunit is added to the glycan backbone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Autolytic enzymes are released into the periplasmic space

choices.label: D
choices.text: The peptide side chain is transferred onto the bactoprenol carrier

choices.label: E
choices.text: The plasma membrane is depolarized and loses its barrier function

explanation.summary: Removal of the terminal D-alanine by penicillin-binding protein creates the peptide cross-link that stiffens the wall.
explanation.whyCorrect: The peptide attached to N-acetylmuramic acid ends in D-alanyl-D-alanine. The penicillin-binding protein cleaves off the terminal alanine and uses the energy of that bond to join the peptide to a neighbor, producing the cross-linked mesh that gives the cell wall its rigidity. Cephalosporins stop this exact step.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Adding sugar subunits to the glycan backbone is a separate polymerization step that precedes cross-linking.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Autolysin release is a downstream event of penicillin action, not the direct product of this reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Transfer of wall subunits onto bactoprenol happens during transport, not during transpeptidation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Membrane depolarization is not a consequence of transpeptidase activity, which acts outside the membrane.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: Peptidoglycan is a cross-linked polymer of polysaccharide and peptide. The polysaccharide portion is built from which pair of sugars?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glucose and galactose, the halves of dietary lactose

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glucuronic acid and iduronic acid of host glycosaminoglycans

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mannose and fucose from glycoproteins and fungal walls

choices.label: D
choices.text: N-acetylglucosamine and N-acetylmuramic acid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ribose and deoxyribose, the nucleic acid pentoses

explanation.summary: The peptidoglycan glycan strand alternates N-acetylglucosamine (NAG) and N-acetylmuramic acid (NAM).
explanation.whyCorrect: The bacterial cell wall is made of peptidoglycan, a cross-linked polymer of polysaccharides and peptides. The polysaccharide is an alternating chain of NAG and NAM, and the amino-acid peptide hangs off the NAM sugar. Recognizing these two sugars is the starting point for understanding where each wall-active antibiotic acts.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glucose and galactose are dietary and storage sugars and are not the repeating units of peptidoglycan.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Glucuronic and iduronic acids are components of host glycosaminoglycans, not of the bacterial wall.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mannose and fucose appear in glycoproteins and fungal walls rather than in peptidoglycan.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ribose and deoxyribose are nucleic acid sugars and have no role in wall structure.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: Within the peptidoglycan polymer, the short amino-acid peptide that is later cross-linked is attached to which component?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The bactoprenol carrier lipid

choices.label: B
choices.text: The lipopolysaccharide core of the outer membrane

choices.label: C
choices.text: The N-acetylglucosamine sugar

choices.label: D
choices.text: The N-acetylmuramic acid sugar

choices.label: E
choices.text: The phospholipid head of the plasma membrane

explanation.summary: The cross-linking peptide is linked to N-acetylmuramic acid and terminates in D-alanyl-D-alanine.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the glycan strand the amino-acid peptide is attached specifically to the NAM sugar, and that peptide ends in D-alanyl-D-alanine. The penicillin-binding protein grabs this terminus to build the cross-link, which is why beta-lactams that mimic D-Ala-D-Ala can block the reaction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bactoprenol transports subunits across the membrane but is not the anchor for the finished peptide.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lipopolysaccharide is an outer membrane molecule of gram-negative bacteria and is separate from peptidoglycan.
whyWrongByChoice.C: N-acetylglucosamine alternates with NAM in the backbone but does not carry the peptide side chain.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The peptide is part of the wall polymer outside the membrane and is not attached to membrane phospholipid.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: A researcher adds a cephalosporin to two flasks of the same organism: one in log-phase growth and one held in a nutrient-free buffer in which the cells are not dividing. Killing occurs only in the log-phase flask. Which property best explains this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The drug binds ribosomes only while translation is ongoing

choices.label: B
choices.text: The drug is bacteriostatic and requires host immunity to kill

choices.label: C
choices.text: The drug is degraded by proteases released in stationary phase

choices.label: D
choices.text: The drug kills only cells that are actively synthesizing cell wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: The drug requires an oxygen-dependent transporter for uptake

explanation.summary: Like penicillins, cephalosporins kill only bacteria that are actively growing and building cell wall.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cephalosporins work by stopping the transpeptidation step of new peptidoglycan synthesis. A cell that is not growing is not laying down new wall, so there is no vulnerable reaction to block and the organism survives exposure. Actively dividing cells, by contrast, cannot complete their wall and die.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cephalosporins act on the cell wall and have no ribosomal target.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Most cephalosporins are bactericidal rather than bacteriostatic, so this misstates the class.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Protease degradation of the drug is not the described property of cephalosporins; beta-lactamases, not proteases, are the relevant resistance enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oxygen-dependent uptake describes aminoglycoside entry, not cephalosporin activity.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: Most cephalosporins are best classified as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bactericidal disruptors of the cell membrane

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bactericidal inhibitors of cell wall synthesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bactericidal inhibitors of DNA gyrase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bacteriostatic inhibitors of folate synthesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Bacteriostatic inhibitors of protein synthesis

explanation.summary: Cephalosporins are bactericidal cell wall synthesis inhibitors.
explanation.whyCorrect: By blocking transpeptidation, cephalosporins halt peptidoglycan synthesis, and the cell dies from loss of wall integrity rather than merely stopping its growth. This killing action places most members of the class among the bactericidal antibiotics.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cephalosporins act on the wall rather than dissolving the cell membrane.
whyWrongByChoice.C: DNA gyrase is the target of the fluoroquinolones, not of beta-lactams.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Folate synthesis inhibition describes sulfonamides and trimethoprim.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cephalosporins do not act on the ribosome and are not bacteriostatic.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: After individual peptidoglycan chains have been assembled, transpeptidase enzymes act on them. What does this step accomplish?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It adds teichoic acid side chains to the glycan strands

choices.label: B
choices.text: It anchors the wall to the outer membrane through lipoprotein

choices.label: C
choices.text: It cleaves the wall so that daughter cells can separate

choices.label: D
choices.text: It exports the completed glycan strands across the membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: It joins chains through peptides to form a rigid multilayered network

explanation.summary: Transpeptidases cross-link peptidoglycan chains so that multiple layers form a rigid network.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once the chains of peptidoglycan are constructed, enzymes called transpeptidases link them to one another through their peptide side chains. This allows multiple layers to develop in the cell wall, producing the rigid network that withstands internal pressure. Cephalosporins inhibit precisely this enzyme.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Teichoic acid addition is a distinct biosynthetic process not carried out by transpeptidases.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lipoprotein anchoring of the outer membrane is a separate gram-negative feature unrelated to transpeptidation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cleaving the wall for cell separation is the job of autolysins, which break bonds rather than form them.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Export of glycan strands across the membrane occurs on the bactoprenol carrier before cross-linking.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: An antibiotic blocks the addition of the NAM-NAG unit to the growing peptidoglycan chain rather than inhibiting the transpeptidation reaction. Which drug acts in this way?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bacitracin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cefazolin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Penicillin G

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Vancomycin stops the NAM-NAG unit from being added to the growing peptidoglycan chain.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vancomycin acts one step earlier in wall synthesis than the beta-lactams do, preventing the disaccharide subunit from being incorporated into the elongating glycan strand. Because it does not bind penicillin-binding proteins, its mechanism is a classic contrast to that of the cephalosporins.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aztreonam works by binding penicillin-binding protein 3.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bacitracin prevents N-acetylmuramic acid from joining bactoprenol.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cefazolin is a cephalosporin and inhibits the transpeptidase cross-linking step.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Penicillin G blocks cross-linking and also activates autolytic enzymes.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: An antibiotic exerts its effect by preventing N-acetylmuramic acid from joining bactoprenol. Which drug has this mechanism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bacitracin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cefepime

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ceftriaxone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Bacitracin blocks the transfer of NAM onto the bactoprenol lipid carrier.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacitracin interferes with the lipid carrier step that moves wall precursors across the membrane, so subunits never reach the growing chain. This is upstream of both the vancomycin step and the transpeptidation step targeted by cephalosporins.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aztreonam binds penicillin-binding protein 3.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cefepime is a cephalosporin and acts at the transpeptidation step.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ceftriaxone is a cephalosporin and inhibits peptidoglycan cross-linking.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin prevents the NAM-NAG unit from being added to the growing chain.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: Which antibiotic exerts its antibacterial effect specifically by binding penicillin-binding protein 3?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bacitracin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cefoxitin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ceftaroline

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Binding to penicillin-binding protein 3 is the mechanism attributed to aztreonam.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aztreonam is singled out as the agent whose action is described as binding penicillin-binding protein 3. Cephalosporins bind penicillin-binding proteins as well, but their described mechanism is inhibition of the transpeptidase cross-linking reaction rather than this specific PBP.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Bacitracin prevents NAM from joining bactoprenol.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cefoxitin is a second-generation cephalosporin that inhibits peptidoglycan cross-linking.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ceftaroline is a fifth-generation cephalosporin and works at the transpeptidation step.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin blocks addition of the NAM-NAG unit to the growing chain.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: Activation of bacterial autolytic enzymes is one of the mechanisms attributed to which of the following drugs or drug classes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycosides

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bacitracin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Penicillins

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Autolytic enzyme activation is a penicillin mechanism, not a cephalosporin mechanism.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although penicillins and cephalosporins share the beta-lactam ring, activation of the bacterium's own autolysins is described as one of the ways penicillins exert their effect. Cephalosporins are defined by inhibition of the transpeptidase that cross-links peptidoglycan.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aminoglycosides act on the bacterial ribosome and are notable instead for nephrotoxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aztreonam acts by binding penicillin-binding protein 3.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bacitracin prevents NAM from joining bactoprenol.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin blocks addition of the NAM-NAG unit to the growing peptidoglycan chain.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: Into how many generations are the cephalosporins divided?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Five

choices.label: B
choices.text: Four

choices.label: C
choices.text: Six

choices.label: D
choices.text: Three

choices.label: E
choices.text: Two

explanation.summary: Cephalosporins are grouped into five generations.
explanation.whyCorrect: The class is divided into five groups, or generations, based on effectiveness against different types of bacterial infections. The fourth generation contains cefepime alone and the fifth contains ceftaroline alone, which makes the upper end of the list easy to anchor.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Four omits the fifth generation, the group with anti-MRSA activity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Six exceeds the number of generations described for this class.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Three stops short of the generations containing cefepime and ceftaroline.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Two understates the classification; the class extends well past a gram-positive and gram-negative split.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: Cephalosporin generations are assigned on the basis of which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The antibacterial spectrum of activity

choices.label: B
choices.text: The number of rings in the drug molecule

choices.label: C
choices.text: The ratio of renal to hepatic clearance

choices.label: D
choices.text: The route of administration available for the drug

choices.label: E
choices.text: The serum half-life of the drug

explanation.summary: Generations are defined by antibacterial spectrum of activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cephalosporin generations have been classified according to which organisms the drugs cover, and that spectrum shifts from predominantly gram-positive toward gram-negative as the generation number rises. Knowing a drug's generation therefore predicts the kinds of bacteria it can treat.

whyWrongByChoice.B: All cephalosporins share the same core beta-lactam structure, so ring count does not separate them.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clearance route is a pharmacokinetic property and is not used to group the generations.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Route does not define generation; oral and intravenous agents appear within the same generation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Half-life varies among agents but is not the basis for assigning a generation.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: Compared with the later generations, first-generation cephalosporins have their principal activity against which group of organisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anaerobic spirochetes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cell-wall-deficient mycoplasmas

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram-negative rods

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gram-positive cocci

choices.label: E
choices.text: Intracellular mycobacteria

explanation.summary: First-generation cephalosporins primarily cover gram-positive cocci.
explanation.whyCorrect: The spectrum of activity varies across the generations, with the first generation concentrated on gram-positive cocci. Later generations progressively extend coverage toward gram-negative organisms, which is why cefazolin and cephalexin are used for skin and soft tissue infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Spirochetes are not the organisms targeted by first-generation agents.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mycoplasmas lack a cell wall entirely, so no cephalosporin can act against them.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gram-negative rods are covered progressively better by the later generations, not the first.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mycobacteria are treated with antimycobacterial regimens, not cephalosporins.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: As one moves from first-generation toward later-generation cephalosporins, the spectrum of activity changes in which way?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It becomes restricted to anaerobes

choices.label: B
choices.text: It broadens to include gram-negative organisms

choices.label: C
choices.text: It loses all activity against cocci

choices.label: D
choices.text: It narrows to gram-positive cocci alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: It shifts from bacteria to fungi

explanation.summary: Later cephalosporin generations expand coverage from gram-positive toward gram-negative organisms.
explanation.whyCorrect: First-generation agents primarily cover gram-positive cocci, and each successive generation extends the spectrum further into gram-negative territory, with the most advanced agents covering both. This trend is the single most useful thing to remember when choosing among the generations.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No generation becomes restricted to anaerobes; anaerobic coverage is only one feature of certain agents.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Later generations do not abandon coverage of cocci; the fifth generation even adds MRSA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Narrowing to gram-positive cocci describes the first generation, the starting point rather than the trend.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cephalosporins are antibacterial agents and never acquire antifungal activity.

questions.topicName: Cephalosporins

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes resistance to beta-lactamase among the cephalosporins?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It falls with each successive generation

choices.label: B
choices.text: It increases as the spectrum extends toward gram-negative organisms

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is greatest among the agents whose activity is mainly gram-positive

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is identical across all five generations

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is present only in the orally administered agents

explanation.summary: Beta-lactamase resistance rises as cephalosporin coverage moves toward gram-negative organisms.
explanation.whyCorrect: Along the gram-positive to gram-negative axis that orders the generations, beta-lactamase resistance is low at the gram-positive end and high at the gram-negative end. The agents developed later were designed to survive the beta-lactamases produced by gram-negative bacteria.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The trend runs in the opposite direction, rising rather than falling with later generations.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The gram-positive end of the spectrum is where beta-lactamase resistance is lowest.
