whyWrongByChoice.D: Reduced porin permeability applies to gram-negative rods such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa, not to staphylococci.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Alteration of the D-Ala-D-Ala terminus is the basis of vancomycin resistance.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: An intensive care isolate of Pseudomonas aeruginosa shows reduced susceptibility to a penicillin. Assays detect no beta-lactamase, and the drug that does reach the target still binds it normally. Which of the following best accounts for the reduced susceptibility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Altered porins in the outer membrane impede drug entry

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autolysins in this organism are constitutively repressed

choices.label: C
choices.text: Peptidoglycan cross-links form without any transpeptidase

choices.label: D
choices.text: The organism lacks peptidoglycan in its cell wall entirely

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thiazolidine ring hydrolysis inactivates the drug in transit

explanation.summary: Changed porin structure in gram-negative rods such as P. aeruginosa impedes penicillin access to PBPs.
explanation.whyCorrect: A minor mechanism of resistance is a change in porin structure in the outer cell wall membrane of some gram-negative rods, exemplified by Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Altered porins impede access of penicillins to the penicillin-binding proteins, so less drug reaches an otherwise normal target.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Autolysins are predominantly a gram-positive feature and their regulation is not the resistance mechanism described for this organism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cross-linking requires transpeptidase; bacteria do not bypass the enzyme to build their wall.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Both gram-positive and gram-negative organisms possess peptidoglycan in their cell walls.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Beta-lactamases cleave the beta-lactam ring, and beta-lactamase has been excluded here; hydrolysis of the thiazolidine ring is not a resistance mechanism.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: Several penicillins are marketed in fixed combinations with a partner drug whose only purpose is to protect the beta-lactam ring from enzymatic cleavage. Which of the following is such a beta-lactamase inhibitor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cloxacillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Probenecid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tazobactam

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ticarcillin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Tazobactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor co-formulated with a penicillin to protect the beta-lactam ring.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beta-lactamase inhibitors were developed and co-formulated with penicillins to protect the beta-lactam ring from cleavage. Examples include clavulanate, sulbactam, tazobactam, avibactam, and vaborbactam. Tazobactam is the partner in piperacillin/tazobactam.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cloxacillin is an antistaphylococcal penicillin that resists beta-lactamase but does not inhibit the enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Probenecid raises penicillin concentrations by blocking transport out of the CSF; it does not inhibit beta-lactamase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ticarcillin is itself a penicillin available in parenteral formulation, not an enzyme inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin is a glycopeptide antibiotic and is unrelated to beta-lactamase inhibition.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: A urinary isolate is resistant to amoxicillin alone but fully susceptible to amoxicillin/clavulanate. Which of the following best describes what clavulanate contributes to this combination?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It binds penicillin-binding proteins that amoxicillin misses

choices.label: B
choices.text: It blocks renal tubular secretion of amoxicillin

choices.label: C
choices.text: It inactivates the beta-lactamase that cleaves amoxicillin

choices.label: D
choices.text: It increases amoxicillin absorption from the small bowel

choices.label: E
choices.text: It opens porin channels to admit more amoxicillin

explanation.summary: Clavulanate is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects the amoxicillin beta-lactam ring.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beta-lactamase cleaves the beta-lactam ring and abolishes antimicrobial activity. Clavulanate is a beta-lactamase inhibitor co-formulated with the aminopenicillin to protect that ring, which extends activity against some beta-lactamase-producing organisms. This is exactly the strategy used when an organism proves resistant to amoxicillin alone.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clavulanate does not supply antibacterial activity of its own by binding PBPs; it protects the partner drug.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blocking renal tubular secretion to raise drug levels is the action of probenecid, not clavulanate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aminopenicillins already have increased stability to gastric acid; clavulanate is not added as an absorption enhancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Porin changes are a resistance mechanism in gram-negative rods and are not reversed by clavulanate.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: Alteration of the D-Ala-D-Ala building block of the peptidoglycan precursor is the basis of bacterial resistance to which of the following antibiotics?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ampicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nafcillin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Penicillin G

choices.label: D
choices.text: Piperacillin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Changing the D-Ala-D-Ala terminus confers vancomycin resistance, not penicillin resistance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Changes in the D-Ala-D-Ala building block of the peptidoglycan precursor are the basis of the mechanism of resistance to vancomycin. Penicillins are affected by a different set of mechanisms: beta-lactamase production as the major one, with PBP mutations and porin changes as minor ones.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ampicillin resistance is chiefly driven by beta-lactamase production, which is why it is paired with sulbactam.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Resistance to nafcillin, an antistaphylococcal penicillin, arises through altered penicillin-binding proteins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Penicillin G resistance reflects beta-lactamase production or, in S. pneumoniae, altered PBPs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Piperacillin resistance is countered with tazobactam, again pointing to beta-lactamase rather than a precursor change.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: Penicillin G and penicillin V share a spectrum of activity that sets them apart from the other penicillin subgroups. Which of the following best characterizes that spectrum?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activity restricted to anaerobic organisms of the colon and mouth

choices.label: B
choices.text: Equal activity against gram-positive and gram-negative organisms

choices.label: C
choices.text: Greatest activity against gram-negative rods, and beta-lactamase stable

choices.label: D
choices.text: Greatest activity against gram-positive organisms, and beta-lactamase labile

choices.label: E
choices.text: Greatest activity against Pseudomonas and other resistant rods

explanation.summary: The natural penicillins act best on gram-positive organisms and are hydrolyzed by beta-lactamases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Penicillin G and penicillin V have the greatest activity against gram-positive organisms, including gram-positive cocci and gram-positive rods. They have little activity against gram-negative rods, and they are susceptible to hydrolysis by beta-lactamases.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An anaerobe-only spectrum is not how these agents are classified.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Balanced gram-positive and gram-negative coverage does not describe penicillin G or V.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This reverses both features: the natural penicillins are weak against gram-negative rods and are beta-lactamase labile.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antipseudomonal activity belongs to piperacillin/tazobactam, not to the natural penicillins.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man has a serious bloodstream infection with methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus. Which of the following penicillins is the agent of choice for this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ampicillin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nafcillin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Penicillin V

choices.label: E
choices.text: Piperacillin

explanation.summary: Nafcillin, an antistaphylococcal penicillin, is the drug of choice for serious S. aureus infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nafcillin is the drug of choice for serious Staphylococcus aureus infections. It belongs to the antistaphylococcal penicillins, which are resistant to staphylococcal beta-lactamases and are therefore active against staphylococci and streptococci, although their overall spectrum is limited.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin is an aminopenicillin without resistance to staphylococcal beta-lactamases.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ampicillin is not the drug of choice for serious S. aureus infection; that distinction belongs to nafcillin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Penicillin V is hydrolyzed by staphylococcal beta-lactamases and is used for gram-positive infections such as streptococcal pharyngitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Piperacillin is chosen for serious Pseudomonas infection, typically with tazobactam.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: Oxacillin and cloxacillin belong to a penicillin subgroup defined by one shared property. Which of the following best describes that subgroup?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Broad activity that includes Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections

choices.label: B
choices.text: Greater gram-negative coverage than any other penicillin class

choices.label: C
choices.text: Improved gastric acid stability with enterohepatic recycling

choices.label: D
choices.text: Resistance to staphylococcal beta-lactamases, with limited spectrum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Routine coformulation with clavulanate to extend the spectrum

explanation.summary: Nafcillin, oxacillin, and cloxacillin are antistaphylococcal penicillins: beta-lactamase resistant but narrow.
explanation.whyCorrect: The antistaphylococcal penicillins are resistant to staphylococcal beta-lactamases. Hence they are active against staphylococci and streptococci, but they have a limited spectrum of activity. Nafcillin, oxacillin, and cloxacillin are the examples of this class.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antipseudomonal coverage belongs to piperacillin/tazobactam, a different subgroup.
whyWrongByChoice.B: These agents have a limited spectrum and are not the class with the greatest gram-negative coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acid stability and enterohepatic recycling describe the aminopenicillins, not oxacillin and cloxacillin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Coformulation with clavulanate or sulbactam characterizes the aminopenicillins.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: Ampicillin and amoxicillin are frequently supplied as combination products so that they retain activity against some beta-lactamase-producing organisms. Which of the following correctly pairs an aminopenicillin with its usual partner agent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin and clavulanate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nafcillin and clavulanate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oxacillin and clavulanate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Penicillin V and tazobactam

choices.label: E
choices.text: Piperacillin and sulbactam

explanation.summary: Aminopenicillins are paired with clavulanate or sulbactam: amoxicillin/clavulanate and ampicillin/sulbactam.
explanation.whyCorrect: The aminopenicillins are coformulated with beta-lactamase inhibitors such as clavulanate or sulbactam, which extend their activity against some beta-lactamase-producing organisms. The standard products are amoxicillin/clavulanate and ampicillin/sulbactam.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Nafcillin is an antistaphylococcal penicillin that already resists staphylococcal beta-lactamases and is not sold with clavulanate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oxacillin belongs to the antistaphylococcal group and is not coformulated with clavulanate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Penicillin V is a natural penicillin and is not supplied with a beta-lactamase inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Piperacillin is paired with tazobactam, and it is an antipseudomonal rather than an aminopenicillin.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: A neutropenic patient develops a serious Pseudomonas aeruginosa bloodstream infection. The penicillin selected is a derivative of ampicillin with a broader spectrum than the aminopenicillins, supplied together with a beta-lactamase inhibitor. Which of the following is that combination?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin/clavulanate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ampicillin/sulbactam

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nafcillin/clavulanate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxacillin/sulbactam

choices.label: E
choices.text: Piperacillin/tazobactam

explanation.summary: Piperacillin/tazobactam is the antipseudomonal penicillin combination.
explanation.whyCorrect: Piperacillin is a derivative of ampicillin with a broader spectrum of activity than the aminopenicillins. The antipseudomonal penicillins retain the antibacterial spectrum of penicillin and have improved activity against gram-positive and gram-negative organisms. Coformulation as piperacillin/tazobactam gives activity against serious Pseudomonal infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin/clavulanate is likewise an aminopenicillin combination without antipseudomonal activity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ampicillin/sulbactam is an aminopenicillin combination and is not the antipseudomonal agent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nafcillin is an antistaphylococcal penicillin and is not marketed with clavulanate or used for Pseudomonas.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oxacillin is antistaphylococcal, with a limited spectrum that does not cover Pseudomonas.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: The natural penicillin is broken down industrially to yield a nucleus that then serves as the precursor for manufacturing the semisynthetic penicillins. Which of the following is that nucleus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 6-Aminopenicillanic acid

choices.label: B
choices.text: 7-Aminocephalosporanic acid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Benzylpenicilloyl polylysine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Clavulanic acid

choices.label: E
choices.text: N-Acetylmuramic acid pentapeptide

explanation.summary: Penicillin G is degraded to 6-aminopenicillanic acid, the precursor of the semisynthetic penicillins.
explanation.whyCorrect: Penicillin G, the natural penicillin, is broken down to make 6-aminopenicillanic acid, which is used as a precursor to make other semisynthetic penicillins. Modifications to this structure, principally at the R side chain, generated the antistaphylococcal, amino-, and antipseudomonal penicillin subgroups.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A cephalosporin nucleus is not the precursor described for making the semisynthetic penicillins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Benzylpenicilloyl material relates to penicillin degradation products that drive hypersensitivity, not to drug manufacture.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clavulanic acid is a beta-lactamase inhibitor, not the scaffold from which penicillins are built.
whyWrongByChoice.E: N-acetylmuramic acid pentapeptide is a bacterial cell wall component, not a drug precursor.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: Hypersensitivity to penicillin is directed not at the intact drug but at products of its degradation, which then provoke an antibody response. Which of the following metabolites is the principal antigenic material responsible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 6-Aminopenicillanic acid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Benzylpenicilloyl derivatives

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clavulanate-protein adducts

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tazobactam breakdown products

choices.label: E
choices.text: The intact thiazolidine ring

explanation.summary: Benzylpenicilloyl derivatives are the degradation products that drive penicillin hypersensitivity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Penicillin is degraded into several metabolites including benzylpenicilloyl derivatives. An immune response can be elicited by antibodies made to these metabolites, and it is the antibody class involved that determines which hypersensitivity reaction occurs: IgE for immediate reactions and IgG for the hemolytic and immune complex reactions.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 6-Aminopenicillanic acid is the manufacturing precursor for semisynthetic penicillins, not the antigenic metabolite.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clavulanate is a beta-lactamase inhibitor added to protect the drug and is not the described antigen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tazobactam is an inhibitor partner drug; its breakdown is not identified as the antigen in penicillin allergy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The intact thiazolidine ring is a structural element of the drug rather than a degradation product.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: Eight minutes after receiving an intravenous penicillin, a 34-year-old woman develops urticaria, wheezing, bronchoconstriction, and hypotension. Which of the following events is most directly responsible for her presentation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deposition of antibody-antigen complexes in small vessels

choices.label: B
choices.text: IgE-triggered mast cell degranulation with histamine release

choices.label: C
choices.text: IgG binding to penicillin adsorbed onto red blood cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Release of bacterial toxins from organisms killed by the drug

choices.label: E
choices.text: T-cell-mediated injury of the renal tubulointerstitium

explanation.summary: Immediate penicillin reactions are type 1, IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: A type 1 or immediate hypersensitivity reaction usually occurs within 2 to 20 minutes of drug administration. IgE antibodies on mast cells contact the antigen, which is the penicillin metabolite, and this triggers immediate mast cell degranulation releasing mediators including histamine. The result is the classic allergy picture of bronchoconstriction, urticaria, hypotension, and wheezing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Immune complex deposition produces a serum sickness-like syndrome 1 to 3 weeks after therapy starts, not within minutes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IgG against penicillin adsorbed on red cells causes Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia, a type 2 reaction over a longer course.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Toxin release from killed organisms describes the Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction, a flu-like syndrome without urticaria and hypotension of this type.
whyWrongByChoice.E: T-cell-mediated interstitial nephritis presents with fever, eosinophilia, rash, and hematuria rather than acute bronchospasm.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: A patient receiving increased doses of intravenous penicillin over several weeks develops anemia with a positive direct Coombs test. The anemia resolves after the drug is stopped. Which of the following best explains this reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delayed T-cell hypersensitivity against tubular epithelium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct oxidative injury of erythrocyte membrane proteins

choices.label: C
choices.text: IgE-mediated degranulation of mast cells and basophils

choices.label: D
choices.text: IgG reacting with penicillin adsorbed onto red blood cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Immune complex deposition with complement activation

explanation.summary: Penicillin can cause a type 2, Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia via IgG against drug adsorbed on red cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Type 2 hypersensitivity is also seen with penicillins, in which IgG reacts with penicillin adsorbed on red blood cells. This can lead to Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia and usually occurs in a small percentage of patients receiving increased doses of IV penicillin for a prolonged period of time. The anemia is usually reversible upon drug termination.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Delayed T-cell hypersensitivity is believed to underlie drug-induced tubular interstitial nephritis, not hemolysis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The mechanism described for penicillin-associated hemolysis is antibody-mediated rather than direct oxidative damage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation is the type 1 reaction and produces urticaria and wheezing within minutes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Immune complex deposition causes the serum sickness-like syndrome with lymphadenopathy and arthralgia.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: Twelve days after beginning penicillin therapy, a patient develops urticaria, diffuse lymphadenopathy, and arthralgia. Which of the following best describes the underlying mechanism of this syndrome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Circulating antibody-antigen complexes depositing in tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cytotoxic antibody directed against circulating red cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Delayed T-cell infiltration of the renal interstitium

choices.label: D
choices.text: IgE on mast cells binding drug metabolites directly

choices.label: E
choices.text: Toxin release from spirochetes killed by the antibiotic

explanation.summary: Serum sickness-like syndrome after penicillin is a type 3, immune complex reaction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Type 3 hypersensitivity to penicillin results from circulating antibody-antigen complexes that deposit in the skin, kidneys, and blood vessels and cause tissue damage through complement activation. This serum sickness-like syndrome, the prototype immune complex disease, can occur 1 to 3 weeks after the start of penicillin therapy and manifests as urticaria, diffuse lymphadenopathy, and arthralgia.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cytotoxic antibody against red cells causes Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia rather than lymphadenopathy and arthralgia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Renal interstitial T-cell infiltration produces fever, eosinophilia, rash, and hematuria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: IgE-mediated reactions appear within 2 to 20 minutes of administration, not after roughly two weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Toxin release from killed spirochetes is the Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction, a brief flu-like syndrome.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: A patient who has been taking a penicillin for 10 days develops fever, a rash, peripheral eosinophilia, and hematuria, with a rising serum creatinine. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibiotic-associated pseudomembranous colitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Drug-induced tubular interstitial nephritis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum sickness-like syndrome

explanation.summary: Fever, eosinophilia, rash, and hematuria on a penicillin point to drug-induced tubular interstitial nephritis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Type 4 hypersensitivity reactions can occur with penicillin exposure and are believed to be the mechanism by which penicillin causes drug-induced tubular interstitial nephritis. The classic presentation is fever, eosinophilia, rash, and hematuria, which is blood in the urine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pseudomembranous colitis produces diarrhea and colonic pseudomembranes, not this renal and eosinophilic picture.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia causes anemia after prolonged high-dose IV penicillin, without rash and hematuria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Jarisch-Herxheimer is a brief flu-like reaction after treating a spirochete infection, with no renal findings.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serum sickness-like syndrome presents with urticaria, diffuse lymphadenopathy, and arthralgia rather than hematuria and rising creatinine.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man lists a penicillin allergy on his chart but has never been skin tested, and the label is now limiting his antibiotic options. Which of the following statements about reported penicillin allergy is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About half of reported allergies are confirmed by skin testing

choices.label: B
choices.text: Beta-lactams are a rare cause of drug-induced anaphylaxis overall

choices.label: C
choices.text: More than 90% of those reporting allergy lack IgE sensitivity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Patients with confirmed IgE allergy tolerate no other beta-lactams

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reported penicillin allergy affects roughly 40% of all patients

explanation.summary: Most reported penicillin allergy is not IgE-mediated, and most confirmed allergic patients still tolerate other beta-lactams.
explanation.whyCorrect: Penicillin allergy is reported by up to 10% of patients, yet more than 90% of those with a reported penicillin allergy do not exhibit IgE-mediated sensitivity when skin testing is performed. The discrepancy arises from inappropriate labeling as allergic or from resolution of an earlier allergy over time. Among patients with confirmed IgE-mediated allergy, studies indicate 97% will tolerate other beta-lactams.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Confirmation on skin testing is far lower than half; more than 90% of reported allergies are not IgE-mediated.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Despite the reassuring statistics on labeling, beta-lactam drugs remain among the leading causes of drug-induced anaphylaxis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Among those with confirmed IgE-mediated penicillin allergy, 97% tolerate other beta-lactams.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Penicillin allergy is reported by up to about 10% of patients, not 40%.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: Six hours after receiving penicillin G for syphilis, a patient develops fever, chills, and headache that resolve without further treatment or change in therapy. Which of the following best explains this reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A direct pyrogenic effect of the penicillin molecule itself

choices.label: B
choices.text: A serum sickness-like immune complex reaction to the drug

choices.label: C
choices.text: An IgE-mediated immediate hypersensitivity to the drug

choices.label: D
choices.text: Release of toxins from spirochetes killed by the drug

choices.label: E
choices.text: Superinfection of the bowel by Clostridioides difficile

explanation.summary: The Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction is a flu-like syndrome from toxins released by killed spirochetes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction occurs in patients being treated with penicillin G for a spirochete infection, usually syphilis caused by Treponema pallidum. It is a flu-like syndrome of fever, chills, and headache produced by the release of toxins from the bacteria that the antibiotic has killed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fever is attributed to toxins released by dying organisms rather than to a pyrogenic property of the drug.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The serum sickness-like syndrome develops 1 to 3 weeks into therapy with urticaria, lymphadenopathy, and arthralgia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immediate IgE reactions occur within 2 to 20 minutes and cause urticaria, wheezing, and hypotension.
whyWrongByChoice.E: C difficile superinfection causes diarrhea and colitis, not an isolated brief flu-like syndrome.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: Ten days after finishing a course of amoxicillin for sinusitis, a 60-year-old woman has profuse watery diarrhea. Colonoscopy shows red inflamed mucosa with adherent areas of white exudate, and necrosis of the mucosal surface is present beneath them. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clostridioides difficile

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pseudomonas aeruginosa

choices.label: C
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treponema pallidum

explanation.summary: Antibiotic-associated pseudomembranous colitis after a penicillin is caused by Clostridioides difficile.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antibiotic-associated colitis, or pseudomembranous colitis, is caused by Clostridioides difficile and may occur during or immediately after penicillin therapy. It is more common with amoxicillin because that drug is so frequently used. Broad-spectrum coverage changes normal bowel flora and allows overgrowth of C difficile, which produces a spore that survives even though the organism is sensitive to ampicillin. Colonoscopy shows red inflamed mucosa with white exudate, the pseudomembranes, with necrosis of the mucosal surface underneath.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is treated with piperacillin/tazobactam and is discussed for porin-based resistance, not for pseudomembranes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Staphylococcus aureus is the organism for which nafcillin is the drug of choice, and it is not the cause of this colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae causes pneumonia and is relevant to PBP-mediated penicillin resistance, not to antibiotic-associated colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Treponema pallidum is the spirochete of syphilis and is linked to the Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: A 17-year-old with sore throat, fever, and posterior cervical lymphadenopathy is given amoxicillin for presumed streptococcal pharyngitis and develops a diffuse maculopapular eruption of small flat discolored spots and papules. A monospot test is positive. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation of the rash?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A nonallergic rash typical of aminopenicillins in mononucleosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: A serum sickness-like reaction from immune complex deposits

choices.label: C
choices.text: A toxin-mediated reaction from rapidly killed streptococci

choices.label: D
choices.text: An early sign of drug-induced tubular interstitial nephritis

choices.label: E
choices.text: An IgE-mediated allergy that precludes all future beta-lactams

explanation.summary: Ampicillin and amoxicillin cause a nonallergic maculopapular rash, especially in infectious mononucleosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ampicillin and amoxicillin, the more commonly used of the two, have been found to cause a maculopapular skin rash consisting of small, flat, discolored spots and papules that does not appear to be an allergic reaction. Patients who have infectious mononucleosis are at increased risk of developing such a rash, which fits this patient's positive monospot.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A serum sickness-like reaction appears 1 to 3 weeks into therapy with urticaria, lymphadenopathy, and arthralgia rather than this maculopapular rash.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Toxin release from killed organisms describes the Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction seen with spirochete infections treated with penicillin G.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Interstitial nephritis presents with fever, eosinophilia, rash, and hematuria, and the urinary findings are absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This eruption is specifically described as not appearing to be an allergic reaction, so it does not establish IgE-mediated allergy.

questions.topicName: Penicillins

questions.stem: A 5-year-old child is brought in for 3 days of right ear pain, irritability, and low-grade fever. Otoscopy shows a red, bulging tympanic membrane with decreased mobility on pneumatic otoscopy. Acute otitis media is diagnosed and antibiotic therapy is indicated. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line agent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cefuroxime

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nafcillin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral vancomycin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topical bacitracin

explanation.summary: Amoxicillin, with or without clavulanic acid, is the first-line antibiotic for acute otitis media.
explanation.whyCorrect: Otitis media is typically caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae and susceptible Gram-negative bacteria. Amoxicillin is a broad-spectrum penicillin with good Gram-positive and Gram-negative coverage, which matches those organisms. It is listed as the first-line agent for otitis media, given with or without clavulanic acid.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cefuroxime is a second-generation cephalosporin with very limited Gram-positive coverage and is not the first-line choice here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nafcillin is an antistaphylococcal penicillin aimed at Staphylococcus aureus and is not used for otitis media.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oral vancomycin is not absorbed and acts only in the gut; it is reserved for C. difficile infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bacitracin is a topical agent for minor skin wounds and has no role in middle ear infection.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: An 8-year-old girl has fever, sore throat, and tender anterior cervical nodes. A throat culture grows Streptococcus pyogenes. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ceftaroline

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cefuroxime

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nafcillin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Penicillin VK

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Oral penicillin (Penicillin VK) is the first-line agent for streptococcal pharyngitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Penicillins have Gram-positive cocci coverage, and oral penicillin VK remains a useful first-line agent for many streptococcal infections. Pharyngitis due to Strep species is listed with oral penicillins as the first-line antibiotic.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftaroline is reserved for MRSA and is not used for routine streptococcal pharyngitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cefuroxime is a second-generation cephalosporin and is not the first-line treatment for pharyngitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Streptococcus species are resistant to nafcillin, which was developed against staphylococci.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin does cover Gram-positive bacteria but is not first-line for pharyngitis.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man is scheduled for an elective open hernia repair. The surgical team wants an intravenous agent given before incision to cover Gram-positive cocci from the skin, with rapid bioavailability and peak tissue levels at the time of the incision. Which of the following is the most appropriate agent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bacitracin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cefazolin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ceftriaxone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cephalexin

explanation.summary: Cefazolin is the first-generation cephalosporin used intravenously for surgical prophylaxis through the skin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cefazolin is a first-generation cephalosporin given IV, so it is effective against the Gram-positive skin flora and reaches peak tissue levels rapidly at the time of incision. Surgical prophylaxis of procedures through the skin is listed with cefazolin as the first-line agent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin is an oral broad-spectrum penicillin and does not provide rapid IV tissue levels.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bacitracin is a topical agent and cannot provide systemic prophylaxis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ceftriaxone is a third-generation agent whose value is extended Gram-negative coverage, not skin prophylaxis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cephalexin is also a first-generation cephalosporin but is oral, so it is not used for surgical prophylaxis.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman has a warm, tender, erythematous plaque on her lower leg after a minor abrasion. There is no abscess, no fever, and no risk factors for resistant organisms. She will be treated as an outpatient with an oral agent. Which of the following is the most appropriate choice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cefoxitin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ceftazidime

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cephalexin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral vancomycin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Piperacillin-tazobactam

explanation.summary: Uncomplicated skin and soft tissue infections, typically due to Gram-positive cocci, are treated with a first-generation cephalosporin such as cephalexin.
explanation.whyCorrect: First-generation cephalosporins are primarily effective against Gram-positive bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus species, which are the usual causes of uncomplicated cellulitis. Cephalexin is the oral first-generation agent listed as first-line for these infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cefoxitin is a second-generation agent valued for Bacteroides coverage, not routine cellulitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ceftazidime is a third-generation agent used for extended Gram-negative coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oral vancomycin is not absorbed from the gut and cannot treat a skin infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Piperacillin-tazobactam is a broad intravenous agent used when Pseudomonas coverage is needed.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A 62-year-old hemodialysis patient has fever and rigors. Blood cultures grow methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cefazolin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cefepime

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nafcillin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Penicillin G

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Vancomycin is one of the few antibiotics effective against MRSA and is first-line for MRSA infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vancomycin is effective against most Gram-positive organisms and is specifically one of the few agents that works against MRSA. MRSA infections are listed with vancomycin and ceftaroline as first-line treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cefazolin is a first-generation cephalosporin with good Gram-positive coverage but does not cover MRSA.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cefepime retains good Gram-positive coverage except MRSA, so it would fail here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Methicillin-resistant strains are by definition not susceptible to antistaphylococcal penicillins such as nafcillin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Penicillin G has limited activity because many staphylococci have developed resistance to penicillin.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man develops profuse watery diarrhea one week after completing a course of antibiotics. Stool testing confirms Clostridium difficile infection. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacitracin, topical

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ceftriaxone, intravenous

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nafcillin, intravenous

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vancomycin, intravenous

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin, oral

explanation.summary: Oral vancomycin is the drug of choice for Clostridium difficile infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vancomycin is one of the few antibiotics used to treat C. difficile infection, and the oral formulation is the drug of choice. Because oral vancomycin is not absorbed, it stays in the gut where the infection resides and acts essentially as a topical treatment there.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bacitracin is a topical skin preparation and cannot treat a colonic infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ceftriaxone does not treat C. difficile; broad cephalosporin use is the kind of exposure that precedes it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nafcillin is an antistaphylococcal penicillin and has no role in C. difficile infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Intravenous vancomycin does not cross into the gastric mucosa, so it would be ineffective for C. difficile.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A hospitalized patient with confirmed Clostridium difficile colitis is started on intravenous vancomycin. After several days the diarrhea is unchanged. Which of the following best explains the treatment failure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: C. difficile is a Gram-negative rod outside the drug's spectrum

choices.label: B
choices.text: C. difficile produces a β-lactamase that inactivates vancomycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: IV vancomycin does not cross into the infected gastric mucosa

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral vancomycin is absorbed systemically while the IV form is not

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin has no intrinsic activity against C. difficile organisms

explanation.summary: IV vancomycin has excellent systemic bioavailability but does not reach the gut mucosa, so it fails in C. difficile infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: An intravenous drug has essentially complete bioavailability and treats systemic infection well, but vancomycin given IV does not cross into the gastric mucosa. Because C. difficile resides primarily in that mucosa, the drug never reaches the organism, and only the oral formulation, which acts topically in the gut, is effective.

whyWrongByChoice.A: C. difficile is a Gram-positive organism, and vancomycin covers most Gram-positive organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Vancomycin is not a β-lactam, so β-lactamase production is not the issue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The relationship is reversed: oral vancomycin is essentially not absorbed at all.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin is in fact one of the few antibiotics active against C. difficile.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A patient with C. difficile colitis is prescribed vancomycin capsules by mouth. Which property of oral vancomycin makes this route appropriate for this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is absorbed and then concentrated into the bile

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is activated by first-pass hepatic metabolism

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is not absorbed, so it acts topically in the gut

choices.label: D
choices.text: It reaches high serum levels after an oral dose

choices.label: E
choices.text: It requires gastric acid to convert to its active form

explanation.summary: Oral vancomycin has essentially zero bioavailability, so it stays in the gut and acts as a topical treatment.
explanation.whyCorrect: When vancomycin is given orally it is not readily absorbed across the gastric mucosa, so its bioavailability is essentially zero. That failure of absorption is exactly what makes it useful: the drug remains at high concentration where C. difficile lives, acting as a local, topical therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Biliary concentration is not the mechanism by which oral vancomycin reaches the colon.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Vancomycin is not a prodrug requiring hepatic activation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oral vancomycin produces almost no serum levels; IV dosing is required for systemic infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin does not need gastric acid to become active.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: Which generation of cephalosporins includes an agent with reliable activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fifth generation

choices.label: B
choices.text: First generation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fourth generation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Second generation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Third generation

explanation.summary: Fifth-generation cephalosporins, such as ceftaroline, are the ones active against MRSA.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ceftaroline is the fifth-generation cephalosporin and is notable for activity against MRSA while maintaining broad-spectrum activity against Gram-negative bacteria. No earlier generation covers MRSA.

whyWrongByChoice.B: First-generation agents such as cefazolin and cephalexin cover Gram-positive organisms but explicitly not MRSA.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fourth-generation cefepime retains good Gram-positive coverage except for MRSA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Second-generation agents have very limited Gram-positive coverage and no MRSA activity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Third-generation agents extend Gram-negative coverage to Neisseria but do not cover MRSA.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A hospitalized patient with a suspected Gram-negative infection is switched from ceftriaxone to cefepime. Which of the following best describes cefepime?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A fifth-generation agent with activity against MRSA

choices.label: B
choices.text: A first-generation agent with mainly Gram-positive activity

choices.label: C
choices.text: A fourth-generation agent with broader Gram-negative activity

choices.label: D
choices.text: A second-generation agent that also covers Bacteroides species

choices.label: E
choices.text: An antipseudomonal penicillin with anaerobic coverage

explanation.summary: Cefepime is a fourth-generation cephalosporin: good Gram-positive coverage except MRSA, with increased Gram-negative coverage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fourth-generation cephalosporins such as cefepime retain good Gram-positive coverage, with the exception of MRSA, while providing increased Gram-negative coverage compared with third-generation agents. That extra Gram-negative reach is the reason for switching from ceftriaxone.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fifth-generation agent active against MRSA is ceftaroline; cefepime does not cover MRSA.
whyWrongByChoice.B: First-generation agents are cefazolin and cephalexin, not cefepime.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The cephalosporins that cover Bacteroides are the second-generation agents cefoxitin and cefotetan.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Piperacillin-tazobactam, not cefepime, is the antipseudomonal penicillin with anaerobic coverage.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man has dysuria and a purulent urethral discharge, and testing is positive for Neisseria gonorrhoeae. A cephalosporin whose Gram-negative spectrum extends to Neisseria species is selected. Which of the following agents was chosen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacitracin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cefazolin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ceftriaxone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cephalexin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nafcillin

explanation.summary: Third-generation cephalosporins such as ceftriaxone extend Gram-negative coverage to Neisseria meningitidis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ceftriaxone is a third-generation cephalosporin with a broad spectrum against Gram-positive bacteria and Gram-negative coverage extended beyond the first and second generations. That extended coverage specifically includes Neisseria meningitidis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bacitracin is a topical agent active against Gram-positive skin organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cefazolin is a first-generation agent with limited activity against Gram-negative bacteria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cephalexin is the oral first-generation agent and also has limited Gram-negative activity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nafcillin is an antistaphylococcal penicillin directed at Staphylococcus aureus.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A patient is started on cefuroxime. Which of the following best describes this agent's generation and spectrum?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fifth generation, with reliable activity against MRSA isolates

choices.label: B
choices.text: First generation, with coverage aimed mainly at Gram-positives

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fourth generation, with the broadest Gram-negative coverage

choices.label: D
choices.text: Second generation, with limited Gram-positive activity

choices.label: E
choices.text: Third generation, with coverage extended to Neisseria species

explanation.summary: Cefuroxime is a second-generation cephalosporin with very limited Gram-positive coverage and better Gram-negative activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Second-generation cephalosporins such as cefuroxime, cefoxitin, and cefotetan have very limited Gram-positive coverage and are more effective against Gram-negative bacteria than the first-generation agents.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftaroline is the fifth-generation agent with MRSA activity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The first-generation agents are cefazolin and cephalexin, which are primarily Gram-positive drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cefepime is the fourth-generation agent with the widest Gram-negative reach.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ceftriaxone and ceftazidime are the third-generation agents whose coverage includes Neisseria.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A surgeon wants a single cephalosporin for an abdominal procedure in which useful activity against Bacteroides species is required. Which of the following agents best meets this requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cefazolin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cefepime

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cefoxitin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ceftaroline

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ceftriaxone

explanation.summary: Cefoxitin and cefotetan are the two second-generation cephalosporins that cover Bacteroides species.
explanation.whyCorrect: As a class, cephalosporins do not cover Bacteroides species well. The stated exceptions are two second-generation agents, cefoxitin and cefotetan, which is why cefoxitin is the appropriate choice when anaerobic Bacteroides coverage is needed from a cephalosporin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cefazolin is a first-generation agent aimed at Gram-positive skin flora.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cefepime is a fourth-generation agent whose advantage is Gram-negative reach, not anaerobes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ceftaroline is the fifth-generation agent notable for MRSA activity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ceftriaxone is a third-generation agent and does not cover Bacteroides well.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A patient receiving ceftriaxone for a suspected Gram-positive bloodstream infection fails to improve, and blood cultures grow Enterococcus species. Which of the following best explains this outcome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ceftriaxone covers only Gram-negative organisms

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ceftriaxone does not reach adequate levels in the bloodstream

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enterococci are Gram-negative rods outside the drug's spectrum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enterococci secrete a β-lactamase that destroys ceftriaxone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Enterococcus species are intrinsically resistant to cephalosporins

explanation.summary: Enterococcus species are intrinsically resistant to cephalosporins despite being Gram-positive cocci.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although many cephalosporins cover Gram-positive cocci, Enterococcus species are known for intrinsic resistance to this entire drug class. Choosing a cephalosporin for a known or suspected enterococcal infection therefore predicts failure regardless of generation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftriaxone has broad activity against Gram-positive bacteria as well as Gram-negatives.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ceftriaxone is an intravenous agent that achieves good systemic levels.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Enterococci are Gram-positive cocci, not Gram-negative rods.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The failure is intrinsic class resistance, not an acquired β-lactamase in this teaching.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: Nafcillin belongs to which of the following drug classes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antipseudomonal penicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antistaphylococcal penicillin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fourth-generation cephalosporin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Glycopeptide antibiotic

choices.label: E
choices.text: Third-generation cephalosporin

explanation.summary: Nafcillin, like oxacillin, is an antistaphylococcal penicillin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antistaphylococcal penicillins, nafcillin and oxacillin, were developed specifically to overcome staphylococcal resistance to penicillin. Susceptible strains of Staphylococcus aureus respond to them, although MRSA strains do not.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Piperacillin-tazobactam is the antipseudomonal penicillin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cefepime is the fourth-generation cephalosporin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vancomycin, not nafcillin, is the non-β-lactam agent in this group.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ceftriaxone is an example of a third-generation cephalosporin.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man with a deep wound infection is started on nafcillin. He fails to improve, and the wound culture is reported as methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. Which of the following best explains the failure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Methicillin-resistant strains are not susceptible to nafcillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nafcillin covers only Gram-negative rods and atypical organisms

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nafcillin is available only as a topical preparation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nafcillin is inactive against all staphylococcal species

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nafcillin requires a β-lactamase inhibitor to be active

explanation.summary: MRSA is the key example of resistance to the antistaphylococcal penicillins.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nafcillin and oxacillin were designed to overcome staphylococcal resistance, and ordinary Staphylococcus aureus strains are susceptible. Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is the most important example of an organism that has developed resistance to this drug class, so nafcillin predictably fails.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Nafcillin is a Gram-positive agent directed at staphylococci.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nafcillin is a systemic agent; bacitracin is the topical drug in this brick.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus strains do respond to nafcillin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nafcillin is used alone; tazobactam is the β-lactamase inhibitor paired with piperacillin.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man in the intensive care unit develops a ventilator-associated pneumonia, and respiratory cultures grow Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Which of the following penicillins is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin-clavulanate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nafcillin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oxacillin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Penicillin VK

choices.label: E
choices.text: Piperacillin-tazobactam

explanation.summary: Piperacillin-tazobactam is the antipseudomonal penicillin and is particularly effective against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
explanation.whyCorrect: Piperacillin-tazobactam provides broad-spectrum coverage against Gram-positive, Gram-negative, and anaerobic organisms. Because its coverage specifically includes Pseudomonas aeruginosa, it is called an antipseudomonal penicillin and is the correct choice here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin-clavulanate is a broad-spectrum penicillin but does not reach Pseudomonas.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nafcillin is an antistaphylococcal penicillin with no Pseudomonas activity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oxacillin is the other antistaphylococcal penicillin and is likewise inactive here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Penicillin VK is the oral penicillin used for streptococcal infections.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A patient with an intra-abdominal infection receives piperacillin-tazobactam. Which of the following best describes the contribution of the tazobactam component?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It extends piperacillin's activity to the atypical organisms

choices.label: B
choices.text: It improves the oral absorption of piperacillin

choices.label: C
choices.text: It inhibits β-lactamase and protects piperacillin from degradation

choices.label: D
choices.text: It lets piperacillin bind an additional bacterial target

choices.label: E
choices.text: It prolongs piperacillin's half-life by blocking renal clearance

explanation.summary: Tazobactam is a β-lactamase inhibitor that shields piperacillin from bacterial β-lactamase enzymes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The addition of tazobactam, a β-lactamase inhibitor, enhances the efficacy of piperacillin by protecting it from degradation by β-lactamase enzymes produced by certain bacteria. That protection is what allows the combination to retain very broad coverage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The combination's breadth comes from piperacillin's own spectrum plus enzyme protection, not atypical coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Piperacillin-tazobactam is an intravenous combination, so oral absorption is not the issue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tazobactam inhibits an enzyme; it does not add a new bacterial binding target.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tazobactam's role is enzymatic protection, not alteration of renal clearance.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A parent asks about the over-the-counter triple antibiotic ointment she applies to her child's scraped knee. The bacitracin it contains is used for which of the following purposes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intravenous therapy for MRSA bacteremia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oral therapy for Clostridium difficile colitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral treatment of streptococcal pharyngitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Systemic coverage of Pseudomonas aeruginosa

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topical prevention of infection in minor skin wounds

explanation.summary: Bacitracin is a topical agent used on minor cuts, scrapes, and burns.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacitracin inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis and is effective against Gram-positive bacteria including Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus species. This makes it useful as a topical treatment for skin infections caused by minor cuts, scrapes, or burns, and it is a key component of triple antibiotic ointments.

whyWrongByChoice.A: MRSA bacteremia is treated with vancomycin or ceftaroline.
whyWrongByChoice.B: C. difficile colitis is treated with oral vancomycin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oral penicillins are the first-line agents for streptococcal pharyngitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pseudomonas requires a systemic antipseudomonal agent such as piperacillin-tazobactam.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: Bacitracin exerts its antibacterial effect by which of the following mechanisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disruption of bacterial folate synthesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inhibition of bacterial cell wall synthesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibition of bacterial DNA gyrase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibition of bacterial protein synthesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibition of bacterial RNA polymerase

explanation.summary: Bacitracin works by inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacitracin is effective against Gram-positive bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus species, and it works by inhibiting cell wall synthesis. That shared mechanism places it alongside the β-lactams and vancomycin as a cell wall agent, though it is used topically.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bacitracin does not interfere with folate metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: DNA gyrase inhibition is not the mechanism of bacitracin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Protein synthesis inhibition is not how bacitracin acts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bacitracin does not target RNA polymerase.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A hospital laboratory reports an isolate as VRE. This designation refers to which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterococcus that has developed resistance to vancomycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enterococcus that is resistant to bacitracin and vancomycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enterococcus that is resistant to β-lactams but not vancomycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus that has become resistant to vancomycin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus that is resistant to both penicillin and vancomycin

explanation.summary: VRE stands for vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus refers to strains of Enterococcus bacteria that have developed resistance to vancomycin. This matters because vancomycin is otherwise one of the few reliable agents against most Gram-positive organisms.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Bacitracin resistance is not part of the VRE definition.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The defining resistance in VRE is to vancomycin itself.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The organism in VRE is Enterococcus, not Staphylococcus aureus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus is not the organism named in this abbreviation.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A patient is given vancomycin alone as empiric therapy. Blood cultures then grow a Gram-negative rod. Which of the following best explains why this regimen was inadequate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Vancomycin covers only strictly anaerobic organisms

choices.label: B
choices.text: Vancomycin does not have good Gram-negative coverage

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vancomycin is active only against Enterococcus species

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vancomycin is effective only when given by mouth

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin is inactivated by bacterial β-lactamases

explanation.summary: Vancomycin covers most Gram-positive organisms but lacks good Gram-negative coverage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vancomycin is effective against most Gram-positive organisms, including MRSA, but it does not have good Gram-negative coverage. A Gram-negative rod bacteremia therefore requires an agent with Gram-negative activity, such as a later-generation cephalosporin or piperacillin-tazobactam.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Vancomycin's spectrum is defined by Gram stain class, not by oxygen requirement.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vancomycin covers most Gram-positive organisms, not only enterococci.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Intravenous vancomycin is the route used for systemic infection; oral dosing is not absorbed.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin is not a β-lactam and is not a substrate for β-lactamases.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: Compared with penicillin G, the broad-spectrum penicillins amoxicillin and ampicillin are best described as having which of the following properties?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activity available only by the intravenous route

choices.label: B
choices.text: Activity developed specifically to treat MRSA

choices.label: C
choices.text: Activity restricted to Gram-positive cocci

choices.label: D
choices.text: Good Gram-positive and Gram-negative coverage

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reliable activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa

explanation.summary: Amoxicillin and ampicillin are broad-spectrum penicillins with both Gram-positive and Gram-negative coverage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Broad-spectrum penicillins such as amoxicillin and ampicillin have good Gram-positive and Gram-negative coverage, which is what separates them from the narrower penicillins. That combined coverage is why amoxicillin is first-line for otitis media, an infection due to Strep pneumoniae and susceptible Gram-negative bacteria.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin is widely used as an oral agent.
whyWrongByChoice.B: MRSA is covered by vancomycin and ceftaroline, not by broad-spectrum penicillins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Restriction to Gram-positive cocci describes penicillin VK and penicillin G.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pseudomonas coverage belongs to the antipseudomonal penicillin piperacillin-tazobactam.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: Which of the following antibiotics is NOT a β-lactam?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cefepime

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ceftriaxone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Piperacillin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: The β-lactams are the penicillins, cephalosporins, monobactams, and carbapenems; vancomycin is a separate class.
explanation.whyCorrect: β-lactams include the penicillins (amoxicillin and piperacillin-tazobactam among them), the cephalosporins of all five generations, the monobactams, and the carbapenems. Vancomycin is discussed alongside these agents as a cell wall inhibitor but is not a β-lactam.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin is a broad-spectrum penicillin and therefore a β-lactam.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cefepime is a fourth-generation cephalosporin and therefore a β-lactam.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ceftriaxone is a third-generation cephalosporin and therefore a β-lactam.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Piperacillin is a penicillin, paired with the β-lactamase inhibitor tazobactam.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman is admitted with a skin and soft tissue infection and started on cefazolin. Wound cultures return methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. Which of the following is the expected problem with continuing cefazolin?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cefazolin covers only anaerobic organisms

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cefazolin does not cover MRSA

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cefazolin has no Gram-positive activity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cefazolin is inactive against all staphylococci

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cefazolin must be given orally to be effective

explanation.summary: First-generation cephalosporins have good Gram-positive coverage but explicitly do not cover MRSA.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cefazolin and cephalexin are first-generation cephalosporins that are primarily effective against Gram-positive bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus species. Despite that good Gram-positive coverage, they do not cover MRSA, so therapy must change to vancomycin or ceftaroline.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cefazolin is not an anaerobic agent; cefoxitin and cefotetan are the cephalosporins with Bacteroides coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cefazolin has strong Gram-positive coverage; the gap is specifically MRSA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus is well covered by cefazolin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cefazolin is the intravenous first-generation agent; cephalexin is the oral one.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: Moving from first-generation through fourth-generation cephalosporins, which of the following best summarizes the change in spectrum of activity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anaerobic coverage increases with each successive generation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both Gram-positive and Gram-negative coverage steadily decrease

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coverage becomes progressively limited to atypical organisms

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gram-negative coverage increases while Gram-positive coverage narrows

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gram-positive coverage increases while Gram-negative coverage falls

explanation.summary: Across the first four cephalosporin generations, Gram-negative coverage broadens while Gram-positive coverage narrows.
explanation.whyCorrect: First-generation agents are primarily Gram-positive drugs with limited Gram-negative activity. Second-generation agents have very limited Gram-positive coverage and are more effective against Gram-negatives, third-generation agents extend Gram-negative reach further to include Neisseria, and fourth-generation cefepime has the most Gram-negative coverage of the four.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anaerobic Bacteroides coverage is confined to two second-generation agents, cefoxitin and cefotetan.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gram-negative coverage clearly expands rather than declining.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Atypical organism coverage is not a feature of the cephalosporin generations.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This reverses the trend; Gram-negative coverage is what grows across generations.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: Cefazolin and cephalexin are both first-generation cephalosporins. Which of the following statements best distinguishes them in practice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cefazolin is a second-generation agent and cephalexin is first

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cefazolin is given intravenously while cephalexin is oral

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cefazolin lacks Gram-positive activity while cephalexin has it

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cephalexin covers MRSA while cefazolin does not

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cephalexin covers Pseudomonas while cefazolin does not

explanation.summary: Both are first-generation cephalosporins; cephalexin is the oral agent and cefazolin the intravenous one.
explanation.whyCorrect: First-generation cephalosporins are cephalexin, given by mouth, and cefazolin, given intravenously. The route drives their indications: cephalexin is used for outpatient uncomplicated skin and soft tissue infections, and cefazolin is the IV agent for surgical prophylaxis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both drugs are first-generation cephalosporins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Both agents have good Gram-positive coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neither first-generation agent covers MRSA.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neither agent covers Pseudomonas; that requires piperacillin-tazobactam.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: Cefepime is best matched to which of the following drug classes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antipseudomonal penicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antistaphylococcal penicillin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fifth-generation cephalosporin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fourth-generation cephalosporin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Third-generation cephalosporin

explanation.summary: Cefepime is the fourth-generation cephalosporin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cefepime is classified as a fourth-generation cephalosporin. It retains good Gram-positive coverage except against MRSA and has increased Gram-negative coverage compared with the third-generation agents.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Piperacillin-tazobactam is the antipseudomonal penicillin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nafcillin and oxacillin are the antistaphylococcal penicillins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ceftaroline is the fifth-generation cephalosporin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ceftriaxone and ceftazidime are third-generation cephalosporins.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: Piperacillin-tazobactam is classified as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antipseudomonal penicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antistaphylococcal penicillin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fifth-generation cephalosporin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Glycopeptide antibiotic

choices.label: E
choices.text: Second-generation cephalosporin

explanation.summary: Piperacillin-tazobactam is the antipseudomonal penicillin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Piperacillin-tazobactam is a penicillin combined with a β-lactamase inhibitor that gives very broad coverage, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa. That Pseudomonas activity is the reason it is called an anti-pseudomonal penicillin.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Nafcillin and oxacillin are the antistaphylococcal penicillins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ceftaroline is the fifth-generation cephalosporin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vancomycin is the non-β-lactam agent in this group.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cefuroxime, cefoxitin, and cefotetan are the second-generation cephalosporins.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy with acute otitis media is started on amoxicillin. This empiric choice is aimed primarily at which of the following organisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clostridium difficile and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neisseria meningitidis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Bacteroides fragilis species

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae and susceptible Gram-negatives

explanation.summary: Otitis media is typically caused by Strep pneumoniae and susceptible Gram-negative bacteria, which amoxicillin covers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute otitis media is typically due to Streptococcus pneumoniae and susceptible Gram-negative bacteria. Amoxicillin is a broad-spectrum penicillin with good Gram-positive and Gram-negative coverage, which is exactly why it, with or without clavulanic acid, is the first-line agent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: C. difficile is treated with oral vancomycin, and enterococci are not the usual otitis media pathogens.
whyWrongByChoice.B: MRSA is not covered by amoxicillin and would require vancomycin or ceftaroline.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neisseria coverage is the province of third-generation cephalosporins such as ceftriaxone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pseudomonas and Bacteroides require an antipseudomonal penicillin or cefoxitin/cefotetan, not amoxicillin.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A 5-year-old with acute otitis media needs an antibiotic, and the clinician wants a first-line option other than amoxicillin alone. Which of the following is the most appropriate alternative?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin-clavulanate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bacitracin ointment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ceftaroline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nafcillin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral vancomycin

explanation.summary: Amoxicillin with clavulanic acid is the other typical first-line choice for acute otitis media.
explanation.whyCorrect: When antibiotics are indicated for otitis media, the typical choices to cover Strep and susceptible Gram-negative bacteria are amoxicillin or amoxicillin-clavulanate. Adding clavulanic acid preserves the same first-line role while protecting the penicillin from β-lactamase.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Bacitracin ointment is a topical agent for minor skin wounds.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ceftaroline is reserved for MRSA infections.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nafcillin targets Staphylococcus aureus and is not used for otitis media.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oral vancomycin is not absorbed and treats only C. difficile in the gut.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: The parents of a 5-year-old treated with amoxicillin for otitis media call on day 3 to say the ear pain has resolved and ask whether they can stop the antibiotic. Which of the following is the most appropriate advice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complete the full prescribed course even though symptoms improved

choices.label: B
choices.text: Double the dose today and then stop the antibiotic tomorrow

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stop the amoxicillin and begin oral vancomycin instead

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stop the antibiotic now that the symptoms have resolved

choices.label: E
choices.text: Switch to a topical antibiotic ointment for the remaining days

explanation.summary: The full antibiotic course should be completed even after symptoms improve.
explanation.whyCorrect: It is important to complete the full course of antibiotics, even when symptoms improve before the medication is finished. Pain and fever can be managed in the meantime with acetaminophen or ibuprofen while the course is completed.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Dose doubling with early discontinuation is not part of the treatment plan.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oral vancomycin is not absorbed and is used only for C. difficile infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stopping early at symptom resolution is precisely what the counseling advises against.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Topical bacitracin treats minor skin wounds and cannot treat a middle ear infection.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: Ceftazidime and ceftriaxone share which of the following classifications?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antistaphylococcal penicillins

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fifth-generation cephalosporins

choices.label: C
choices.text: First-generation cephalosporins

choices.label: D
choices.text: Second-generation cephalosporins

choices.label: E
choices.text: Third-generation cephalosporins

explanation.summary: Ceftriaxone and ceftazidime are the third-generation cephalosporins.
explanation.whyCorrect: Third-generation cephalosporins, such as ceftriaxone and ceftazidime, have a broad spectrum against Gram-positive bacteria and Gram-negative coverage extended beyond the first and second generations, including Neisseria meningitidis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nafcillin and oxacillin are the antistaphylococcal penicillins.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ceftaroline is the fifth-generation agent with MRSA activity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cefazolin and cephalexin are the first-generation agents.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cefuroxime, cefoxitin, and cefotetan are the second-generation agents.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man has a serious MRSA infection, but vancomycin cannot be used. Which of the following agents retains activity against MRSA?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cefazolin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cefepime

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ceftaroline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ceftriaxone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nafcillin

explanation.summary: Ceftaroline is the alternative to vancomycin for MRSA infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ceftaroline is a fifth-generation cephalosporin notable for activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus while maintaining broad-spectrum activity against Gram-negative bacteria. MRSA infections are listed as treatable with vancomycin or ceftaroline.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cefazolin is a first-generation cephalosporin and does not cover MRSA.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cefepime retains good Gram-positive coverage but explicitly not against MRSA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ceftriaxone is a third-generation agent with no MRSA coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: MRSA strains are by definition not susceptible to antistaphylococcal penicillins such as nafcillin.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications 1 – β-lactams and Vancomycin

questions.stem: A patient has a Staphylococcus aureus wound infection, and the team notes that plain penicillin would likely fail despite staphylococci being Gram-positive cocci. Which of the following best explains this?

choices.label: A
