whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin has no gram-negative coverage at all.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: An Escherichia coli isolate from a hospitalized patient is resistant to ampicillin, amoxicillin-clavulanate, and several cephalosporins but remains susceptible to meropenem. Which of the following best explains this resistance pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The organism grows only under anaerobic conditions

choices.label: B
choices.text: The organism has acquired a thick polysaccharide capsule

choices.label: C
choices.text: The organism has lost its peptidoglycan cell wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: The organism has mutated its 30S ribosomal subunit

choices.label: E
choices.text: The organism produces extended-spectrum β-lactamase enzymes

explanation.summary: ESBL producers make enzymes that degrade β-lactam antibiotics, leaving carbapenems as the reliable option.
explanation.whyCorrect: Extended-spectrum β-lactamase producing bacteria secrete β-lactamase enzymes that degrade other β-lactam antibiotics, which explains resistance across penicillins and cephalosporins. Carbapenems combine broad-spectrum activity with resistance to these enzymes, so they remain active. That is why carbapenems are the most reliable therapy for ESBL infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: E. coli is a facultative organism, and anaerobic growth does not explain β-lactam degradation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A capsule impairs phagocytosis but does not selectively inactivate β-lactam antibiotics.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Loss of the cell wall is not a feature of E. coli and would not spare carbapenem activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A 30S mutation would affect aminoglycosides and tetracyclines, not β-lactams.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: Carbapenems are often summarized as covering essentially all gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria. Which of the following organisms is the important gram-positive exception to that rule?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Beta-lactamase-producing Haemophilus influenzae

choices.label: B
choices.text: ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae

choices.label: C
choices.text: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Penicillin-susceptible Streptococcus pneumoniae

explanation.summary: Carbapenems cover a wide range of gram-positive and gram-negative organisms except MRSA.
explanation.whyCorrect: The shorthand for carbapenems is that they cover all gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, but MRSA is the explicit gram-positive exclusion. Anti-MRSA therapy must be added when that organism is suspected or isolated. The rest of the gram-positive and gram-negative spectrum is broad.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Haemophilus influenzae is a gram-negative organism covered by carbapenems, not the exception.
whyWrongByChoice.B: ESBL-producing Klebsiella is precisely the organism carbapenems treat most reliably.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methicillin-susceptible S. aureus is a gram-positive organism well within the carbapenem spectrum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus pneumoniae is covered by the broad gram-positive activity of carbapenems.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: An antimicrobial stewardship team restricts carbapenem use to infections that are hard to treat. For which of the following is carbapenem therapy the most appropriate choice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute otitis media in a healthy 4-year-old child

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hospital-acquired pneumonia caused by an ESBL organism

choices.label: C
choices.text: Non-purulent cellulitis of the leg in a healthy adult

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptococcal pharyngitis in a healthy adolescent

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uncomplicated bacterial sinusitis in a healthy adult

explanation.summary: Carbapenems are reserved for complicated infections such as intra-abdominal infection, urinary tract infection, and hospital-acquired pneumonia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Carbapenems are valuable in complicated infections including intra-abdominal infections, urinary tract infections, and hospital-acquired pneumonia, especially when ESBL-producing organisms are involved. These infections are hard to treat, and carbapenems are always reserved for them. Routine community infections should be treated with narrower agents.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Otitis media is treated with an aminopenicillin, typically amoxicillin with or without clavulanate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Non-purulent cellulitis is treated with agents directed at S. pyogenes and S. aureus, such as a first-generation cephalosporin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Streptococcal pharyngitis responds to narrow gram-positive therapy and does not warrant a carbapenem.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sinusitis is treated with amoxicillin/clavulanate, not with a reserved broad-spectrum agent.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 61-year-old ventilated patient develops pneumonia and is started on ertapenem. Fever persists, and respiratory cultures grow Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Which of the following best explains the failure of therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ertapenem is active only against gram-positive organisms

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ertapenem is degraded by all extended-spectrum β-lactamases

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ertapenem is inactivated by pulmonary surfactant

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ertapenem lacks activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ertapenem must be combined with cilastatin to be active

explanation.summary: Ertapenem is the carbapenem that does not cover Pseudomonas, Enterococci, or Acinetobacter.
explanation.whyCorrect: Carbapenems as a class cover most gram-negative bacteria, but ertapenem is the important exception: it has no coverage against Pseudomonas, Enterococci, or Acinetobacter. The mnemonic is that ErtAPenem does not cover PEA. A different carbapenem or an antipseudomonal agent is required here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ertapenem is a broad-spectrum agent with extensive gram-negative activity; it is not gram-positive only.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Carbapenems are notable for resisting β-lactamase enzymes, which is why they work against ESBL producers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Surfactant inactivation is not a property of carbapenems and does not explain the gap.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cilastatin is paired with imipenem, not ertapenem, and it is not required for antibacterial activity.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 74-year-old woman with an intra-abdominal abscess is treated with ertapenem but remains febrile. Operative cultures grow Enterococcus faecalis. Which of the following is the most likely reason for the poor response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ertapenem does not cover Enterobacter species

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ertapenem does not cover enterococci

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ertapenem does not cover Escherichia coli

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ertapenem does not cover Klebsiella species

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ertapenem does not cover Proteus species

explanation.summary: Enterococci are one of the three organisms ertapenem fails to cover.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ertapenem's coverage gaps are Pseudomonas, Enterococci, and Acinetobacter, captured by the mnemonic that ErtAPenem does not cover PEA. An enterococcal isolate therefore requires a different agent, such as an aminopenicillin. The rest of its gram-negative spectrum is broad.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterobacter species are covered; only Enterococcus, Pseudomonas, and Acinetobacter are the gaps.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Escherichia coli is well covered by carbapenems, including ertapenem.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Klebsiella, including ESBL-producing strains, is covered by carbapenems.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Proteus falls within the broad gram-negative coverage of carbapenems.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A resident choosing among carbapenems recalls that ertapenem has three notable coverage gaps. Which of the following groups of organisms is NOT covered by ertapenem?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterobacter species, Serratia marcescens, and Morganella morganii

choices.label: B
choices.text: Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Proteus mirabilis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pseudomonas, Enterococci, and Acinetobacter

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Moraxella catarrhalis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pyogenes, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Escherichia coli

explanation.summary: ErtAPenem does not cover PEA: Pseudomonas, Enterococci, and Acinetobacter.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ertapenem is the carbapenem exception, lacking activity against Pseudomonas, Enterococci, and Acinetobacter. The PEA mnemonic exists precisely because the rest of the carbapenem class does cover these gram-negative organisms. Recognizing the gap prevents treatment failure in ICU infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterobacter, Serratia, and Morganella are gram-negative organisms covered by carbapenems.
whyWrongByChoice.B: These Enterobacteriaceae are covered by ertapenem.
whyWrongByChoice.D: These respiratory organisms fall within carbapenem coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: These gram-positive cocci and E. coli are within the carbapenem spectrum; only MRSA is excluded.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 58-year-old intensive care unit patient develops pneumonia caused by Acinetobacter baumannii. Which of the following agents has activity against this organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ertapenem

choices.label: C
choices.text: Linezolid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nafcillin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Doxycycline's gram-negative spectrum includes Acinetobacter, which ertapenem does not cover.
explanation.whyCorrect: Doxycycline has wide gram-negative coverage that specifically includes Acinetobacter, along with Legionella, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and Haemophilus influenzae. Ertapenem is the carbapenem that explicitly lacks Acinetobacter activity. The remaining options are gram-positive agents.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ertapenem does not cover Acinetobacter, along with Pseudomonas and Enterococci.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Linezolid is a gram-positive agent and has no activity against Acinetobacter.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nafcillin is an antistaphylococcal penicillin without meaningful gram-negative activity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin covers gram-positive organisms only.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman with a serious infection caused by a gram-negative bacillus is treated with aztreonam. Which of the following best describes the primary use of monobactams?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Treatment of aerobic gram-negative bacillary infections

choices.label: B
choices.text: Treatment of anaerobic intra-abdominal infections

choices.label: C
choices.text: Treatment of atypical pneumonia caused by Mycoplasma

choices.label: D
choices.text: Treatment of enterococcal urinary tract infections

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treatment of MRSA skin and soft tissue infections

explanation.summary: Monobactams are used for infections caused by aerobic gram-negative bacilli.
explanation.whyCorrect: Monobactams are effective against aerobic gram-negative bacteria and are highly resistant to the β-lactamases those organisms produce. Unlike penicillins, they do not treat gram-positive bacteria or anaerobes. Their niche is therefore gram-negative bacillary infection.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Monobactams do not cover anaerobes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Atypical pathogens such as Mycoplasma are treated with doxycycline, not with a monobactam.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Enterococcus is a gram-positive organism and is not covered by monobactams.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Monobactams have no gram-positive activity, so MRSA is entirely outside their spectrum.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: Aztreonam is selected for a patient with a gram-negative bacillary infection partly because it is unlikely to disrupt the patient's normal microbiota. Which property of monobactams best explains this advantage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are active against gram-positive cocci but spare anaerobes

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are given only topically and are not absorbed systemically

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are rapidly degraded by β-lactamases in the gut lumen

choices.label: D
choices.text: They bind the 30S ribosome instead of the bacterial cell wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: They lack activity against gram-positive bacteria and anaerobes

explanation.summary: Because monobactams spare gram-positives and anaerobes, they treat gram-negative bacilli without disrupting the microbiota.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unlike penicillins, monobactams do not treat gram-positive bacteria or anaerobes. Since the normal microbiota is dominated by those organisms, aztreonam can target gram-negative bacilli while leaving the patient's flora largely intact. This narrow spectrum is presented as an advantage, not a drawback.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Monobactams do not cover gram-positive cocci at all, so this reverses their spectrum.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aztreonam is a systemic agent, not a topical one.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Monobactams are notable for a high level of resistance to β-lactamases produced by gram-negative organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Monobactams are β-lactams acting on the cell wall; 30S binding describes aminoglycosides and tetracyclines.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man receiving nafcillin for a staphylococcal wound infection develops Escherichia coli bacteremia that does not respond to the nafcillin. Which of the following best explains this observation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antistaphylococcal penicillins are active only against anaerobic organisms

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antistaphylococcal penicillins are destroyed by hepatic first-pass metabolism

choices.label: C
choices.text: Antistaphylococcal penicillins are not effective against many gram-negative bacteria

choices.label: D
choices.text: Antistaphylococcal penicillins inhibit protein synthesis rather than the cell wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Antistaphylococcal penicillins require a β-lactamase inhibitor to have any activity

explanation.summary: Penicillins and antistaphylococcal penicillins such as nafcillin and oxacillin are not effective against many gram-negative bacteria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nafcillin and oxacillin are aimed at staphylococci and are not effective against many gram-negative bacteria. Gram-negative resistance to these agents is largely due to β-lactamase enzymes and efflux pumps. A gram-negative bacteremia therefore requires a different class entirely.

whyWrongByChoice.A: They act against aerobic gram-positive cocci such as S. aureus, not exclusively anaerobes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: First-pass metabolism does not explain the intrinsic gram-negative gap of these agents.
whyWrongByChoice.D: These drugs are β-lactams that act on cell wall synthesis, not protein synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antistaphylococcal penicillins are themselves stable against staphylococcal penicillinase; the issue is spectrum, not inhibitor pairing.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: Most gram-negative bacilli are resistant to penicillin and to antistaphylococcal penicillins such as oxacillin. Which of the following mechanisms most commonly accounts for this resistance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Capsule formation and biofilm production

choices.label: B
choices.text: Porin overexpression and increased drug uptake

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ribosomal methylation and altered 50S binding sites

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thickened peptidoglycan and spore formation

choices.label: E
choices.text: β-lactamase expression and efflux pumps

explanation.summary: Gram-negative resistance to penicillins develops through β-lactamase enzymes and efflux pumps.
explanation.whyCorrect: In most cases, bacterial resistance to penicillins and antistaphylococcal penicillins has developed through expression of β-lactamase enzymes and efflux pumps. The enzymes destroy the drug and the pumps expel it before it reaches its target. This is why β-lactamase inhibitors are added to extend these agents into gram-negative territory.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Capsules and biofilms hinder host defenses but are not the described mechanism of β-lactam resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Increased drug uptake would make the organism more susceptible, not resistant.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ribosomal changes affect protein synthesis inhibitors, not cell-wall active β-lactams.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Spore formation and peptidoglycan thickness are not the mechanisms cited for gram-negative penicillin resistance.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: Gentamicin is being considered for a hospitalized patient with a serious infection. Against which of the following groups of organisms are aminoglycosides primarily effective?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aerobic gram-negative bacilli

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anaerobic gram-negative bacilli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Atypical intracellular pathogens

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gram-positive cocci in clusters

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spirochetes and rickettsial organisms

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides are potent agents directed primarily at aerobic gram-negative bacteria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycosides are potent antibiotics with a broad spectrum that is primarily effective against aerobic gram-negative bacteria, especially the Enterobacteriaceae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. They have limited gram-positive activity and no useful activity against anaerobes or atypicals. Oxygen-dependent uptake underlies the aerobic requirement.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Aminoglycosides are not effective against anaerobic bacteria.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Atypical pathogens are outside the aminoglycoside spectrum and are treated with doxycycline.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Activity against gram-positive cocci is limited, which is why aminoglycosides are used synergistically there.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Spirochetes such as the agent of Lyme disease and rickettsial organisms are treated with doxycycline.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man with extensive burns develops bacteremia with Pseudomonas aeruginosa. In addition to an antipseudomonal β-lactam, which of the following classes is effective against this organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycosides

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antistaphylococcal penicillins

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycopeptides

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxazolidinones

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tetracyclines

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides are effective against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
explanation.whyCorrect: In addition to covering Enterobacteriaceae, aminoglycosides are effective against Pseudomonas aeruginosa. This makes them a common companion to an antipseudomonal β-lactam in severe gram-negative infection. Their weakness is gram-positive organisms, anaerobes, and atypicals.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Nafcillin and oxacillin are not effective against many gram-negative bacteria, including Pseudomonas.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vancomycin and other glycopeptides have no gram-negative coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Linezolid and related oxazolidinones cover gram-positive organisms only.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tetracyclines are not effective against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A hospitalized patient has a gram-negative infection, and the team asks which organism could be treated with an aminoglycoside used by itself. Which of the following pathogens is the best answer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clostridioides difficile

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mycoplasma pneumoniae

choices.label: C
choices.text: Proteus mirabilis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Staphylococcus epidermidis

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides can be used alone against aerobic gram-negative Enterobacteriaceae such as Proteus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycosides are particularly effective against members of the Enterobacteriaceae family, including Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterobacter, Providencia, Proteus, Morganella, and Serratia. Proteus mirabilis therefore can be covered by an aminoglycoside used by itself. For gram-positive organisms they must be combined with another agent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clostridioides difficile is an anaerobe, and aminoglycosides are not effective against anaerobic bacteria.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mycoplasma is an atypical pathogen, and aminoglycosides are not effective against atypicals.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Staphylococcus aureus is gram-positive and would not be treated with an aminoglycoside alone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Staphylococcus epidermidis is gram-positive, where aminoglycoside activity is limited and synergy is required.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: An aminoglycoside is added to a regimen for a serious gram-positive infection rather than being used alone. Which of the following best explains this practice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycosides are active only against β-lactamase-producing strains

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aminoglycosides are inactivated by gastric acid in fasting patients

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aminoglycosides cannot be administered intravenously in adults

choices.label: D
choices.text: Aminoglycosides have limited activity against gram-positive bacteria

choices.label: E
choices.text: Aminoglycosides work only when the organism is growing anaerobically

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides have limited gram-positive activity and are used synergistically with other antibiotics for those infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although aminoglycosides are potent against aerobic gram-negative bacteria, they have limited activity against gram-positive organisms. For gram-positive infections they are typically used synergistically with other antibiotics rather than as monotherapy. The partner drug supplies the primary gram-positive activity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Their activity is not limited to β-lactamase-producing organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aminoglycosides are given parenterally, and gastric inactivation is not the reason for combination therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aminoglycosides are routinely given intravenously.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Aminoglycosides require aerobic conditions and are not effective against anaerobic bacteria.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman has an intra-abdominal abscess from which anaerobic organisms are recovered. Gentamicin alone is unlikely to be adequate therapy. Which of the following explains this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycosides are degraded by extended-spectrum β-lactamases

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aminoglycosides are not effective against anaerobic bacteria

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aminoglycosides are not effective against Enterobacteriaceae

choices.label: D
choices.text: Aminoglycosides are not effective against Proteus species

choices.label: E
choices.text: Aminoglycosides are not effective against Pseudomonas aeruginosa

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides have no useful activity against anaerobes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycosides are effective primarily against aerobic gram-negative organisms and are not effective against anaerobic bacteria or atypical pathogens. An abscess containing anaerobes therefore needs different or additional coverage. Broad agents such as piperacillin-tazobactam or a carbapenem are used for complicated intra-abdominal infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aminoglycosides are not β-lactams and are not the target of β-lactamase enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Enterobacteriaceae are a core part of the aminoglycoside spectrum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Proteus is among the Enterobacteriaceae that aminoglycosides cover.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Aminoglycosides are effective against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man has a subacute community-acquired pneumonia, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae is suspected. Gentamicin would be an inappropriate choice for which of the following reasons?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycosides are inactive against aerobic gram-negatives

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aminoglycosides are inactive against atypical pathogens

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aminoglycosides are inactive against Escherichia coli

choices.label: D
choices.text: Aminoglycosides are inactive against Klebsiella pneumoniae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Aminoglycosides are inactive against Serratia species

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides do not cover atypical pathogens such as Mycoplasma pneumoniae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycosides are not effective against anaerobic bacteria or atypical pathogens. Mycoplasma pneumoniae is an atypical organism, so doxycycline is the agent commonly used instead. Aminoglycoside strength lies with aerobic gram-negative bacilli.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aerobic gram-negative organisms are precisely what aminoglycosides target best.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Escherichia coli is covered by aminoglycosides.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Klebsiella pneumoniae is specifically within the aminoglycoside spectrum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serratia is one of the Enterobacteriaceae aminoglycosides cover.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man has a purulent skin and soft tissue infection, and community-acquired MRSA is suspected. An oral agent is needed. Which of the following is the most appropriate choice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ampicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: C
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gentamicin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Piperacillin-tazobactam

explanation.summary: Doxycycline is often used for skin and soft tissue infections because its gram-positive coverage includes MRSA.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tetracyclines are effective against gram-positive organisms including Staphylococcus aureus, and that coverage extends to MRSA. Many skin and soft tissue infections, purulent or non-purulent, are treated with doxycycline for this reason. It is also convenient as an oral agent in the outpatient setting.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aminopenicillins cover gram-positives except MRSA, so ampicillin would miss the suspected organism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aztreonam treats aerobic gram-negative bacteria only and has no gram-positive activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aminoglycosides have limited gram-positive activity and are not used alone for staphylococcal skin infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Piperacillin-tazobactam has broad coverage but explicitly excludes MRSA, and it is not an oral agent.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man has a bloodstream infection caused by vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE). Which of the following classes retains activity against this organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycosides

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aminopenicillins

choices.label: C
choices.text: Antistaphylococcal penicillins

choices.label: D
choices.text: Monobactams

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tetracyclines

explanation.summary: Tetracyclines cover gram-positive organisms including MRSA and VRE.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tetracyclines have broad gram-positive activity that includes Staphylococcus (including MRSA), Streptococcus, and Enterococcus (including VRE). That unusual reach is what distinguishes them from the β-lactams in this setting. Their gram-negative coverage through doxycycline is broad as well.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aminoglycosides have limited gram-positive activity and are not used alone against enterococci.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aminopenicillins cover Enterococcus generally, but a vancomycin-resistant strain is not within the tetracycline-specific coverage described here and requires an agent credited with VRE activity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nafcillin and oxacillin are aimed at methicillin-susceptible staphylococci, not enterococci.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Monobactams have no gram-positive activity whatsoever.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man has pneumonia caused by Legionella. Which of the following agents covers this organism as well as Acinetobacter, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and Haemophilus influenzae?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: B
choices.text: Linezolid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nafcillin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxacillin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Doxycycline has wide gram-negative coverage including Acinetobacter, Legionella, N. gonorrhoeae, and H. influenzae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Doxycycline's gram-negative spectrum specifically includes Acinetobacter, Legionella, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and Haemophilus influenzae. Combined with its gram-positive and atypical coverage, this makes it a versatile agent for respiratory infection. The other options are gram-positive agents only.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Linezolid covers gram-positive organisms only.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nafcillin is not effective against many gram-negative bacteria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oxacillin, like nafcillin, is an antistaphylococcal penicillin without gram-negative activity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin has no gram-negative coverage.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 28-year-old hiker has fever, headache, myalgias, and a petechial rash that began on the wrists and ankles. Rocky Mountain spotted fever due to a rickettsial organism is diagnosed. Which of the following is the first-line treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ampicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: C
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gentamicin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Doxycycline is first-line therapy for rickettsial infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Doxycycline is commonly used for atypical pathogens including Rickettsiae, and it is the first-line treatment for rickettsial disease. β-lactams and glycopeptides have no activity against these intracellular organisms. Prompt doxycycline is standard.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aminopenicillins do not treat rickettsial organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aztreonam covers aerobic gram-negative bacilli only.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aminoglycosides are not effective against atypical pathogens.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin covers gram-positive organisms and has no role in rickettsial infection.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man develops an expanding annular rash several days after a tick bite, and Lyme disease is diagnosed. Which of the following is the first-line treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gentamicin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Meropenem

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nafcillin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Doxycycline is the first-line treatment for Lyme disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Doxycycline is the first-line treatment for both Rickettsiae and Lyme disease. Its broad activity against atypical and intracellular organisms is what makes it effective here. The β-lactams listed do not target these pathogens.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Aminoglycosides are not effective against atypical pathogens.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Carbapenems are reserved for complicated gram-negative infections, not tick-borne illness.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nafcillin is an antistaphylococcal penicillin and does not treat Lyme disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin is a gram-positive agent with no role in Lyme disease.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy has a 3-day history of redness, swelling, warmth, and tenderness of the right lower leg. There is no drainage or pus and no history of trauma. Examination shows erythematous, edematous, warm skin with well-demarcated borders, and he has a low-grade fever. Which of the following pairs of organisms most likely caused this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae

choices.label: B
choices.text: Listeria monocytogenes and Enterococcus faecalis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Chlamydia trachomatis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pyogenes and Staphylococcus aureus

explanation.summary: Non-purulent cellulitis is typically attributed to Streptococcus pyogenes and Staphylococcus aureus.
explanation.whyCorrect: The well-demarcated erythema, warmth, and swelling without drainage describe non-purulent cellulitis, which is typically attributed to S. pyogenes (Group A Streptococcus) and S. aureus. These gram-positive skin organisms can be covered with a first-generation cephalosporin such as oral cephalexin, with oxacillin as an alternative. Supportive care includes rest, elevation, and analgesics.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterobacteriaceae cause urinary and intra-abdominal infections rather than typical cellulitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Listeria causes meningitis in neonates and older adults, and Enterococcus is a urinary and intra-abdominal pathogen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Atypical pathogens cause pneumonia and genital infection, not cellulitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: These resistant gram-negative organisms are hospital-associated and are not the usual cause of community cellulitis.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman is treated for a Chlamydia trachomatis infection. Which of the following agents is commonly used against this and other atypical pathogens such as Mycoplasma pneumoniae?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: B
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gentamicin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nafcillin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Doxycycline is very commonly used to treat atypical pathogens such as Mycoplasma, Chlamydia, and Rickettsiae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Doxycycline is used both inpatient and outpatient and is very common in treating atypical pathogens, including Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Chlamydia trachomatis, and Rickettsiae. These organisms are not reached by cell-wall active agents. Doxycycline is also commonly used for respiratory infections such as community-acquired pneumonia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aztreonam covers aerobic gram-negative bacilli only.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aminoglycosides are not effective against atypical pathogens.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nafcillin targets staphylococci and does not treat atypical organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin is a gram-positive agent with no atypical coverage.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man is admitted with fever, headache, photophobia, and neck stiffness. Empiric therapy for bacterial meningitis is started to cover Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and Haemophilus influenzae. Which of the following regimens is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin with tobramycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aztreonam with linezolid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ceftriaxone with or without vancomycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Doxycycline with gentamicin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nafcillin with oral vancomycin

explanation.summary: In adults, ceftriaxone with or without vancomycin covers the common causes of bacterial meningitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The common bacterial causes of meningitis are Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and Haemophilus influenzae. In adults, the combination of ceftriaxone with or without vancomycin provides coverage against these organisms. Ampicillin is added when Listeria must also be covered.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin plus an aminoglycoside does not reliably cover the three classic meningitis pathogens.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aztreonam misses gram-positive organisms and linezolid misses gram-negatives; the pair is not standard here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neither doxycycline nor gentamicin is the standard empiric regimen for these meningitis pathogens.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nafcillin lacks gram-negative coverage, and oral vancomycin is not absorbed and acts only in the gut.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man is admitted with bacterial meningitis. Because of his age, Listeria monocytogenes must be covered in addition to the usual pathogens. Which of the following should be added to ceftriaxone and vancomycin?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ampicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: C
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Linezolid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nafcillin

explanation.summary: Ampicillin is added for Listeria coverage in neonates, patients over 50, and immunocompromised patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: Listeria monocytogenes occurs at a higher rate in neonates under 1 month, patients over 50, and immunocompromised patients. Ampicillin provides effective treatment for Listeria, so in patients above 50 it is given along with ceftriaxone and vancomycin. In neonates, gentamicin with cefepime or cefotaxime is another option.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Aztreonam covers aerobic gram-negative bacilli only and would not treat a gram-positive rod.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxycycline is used for atypical and tick-borne pathogens, not for Listeria coverage in meningitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Linezolid is not the agent used to add Listeria coverage in this setting.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nafcillin is directed at staphylococci and is not the agent used for Listeria.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications – 2: β-lactams and 30S Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man is admitted with an acute pyogenic infection in which the causative organism is multiplying rapidly. The team selects a protein synthesis inhibitor. Under which condition are protein synthesis inhibitors most effective?

choices.label: A
choices.text: When host phagocytes have already engulfed most of the organisms

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the bacteria are actively dividing during acute infection

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the infection has become chronic and walled off by fibrosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: When the organism has formed a mature biofilm on a foreign body

choices.label: E
choices.text: When the organisms have entered a dormant, non-replicating state

explanation.summary: Protein synthesis inhibitors work best during the acute stage of infection, when bacteria are actively dividing.
explanation.whyCorrect: Protein synthesis inhibitors act on the bacterial ribosome, so their effect depends on ongoing translation. Actively dividing organisms are synthesizing protein at a high rate and are therefore maximally susceptible. This is why these drugs are most effective during the acute stage of an infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Phagocytosis is a host clearance mechanism and is not the condition that determines protein synthesis inhibitor efficacy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A chronic, walled-off focus contains slowly metabolizing organisms and is the opposite of the acute stage favored here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Biofilm organisms are metabolically slowed and shielded, which reduces rather than enhances the effect of these agents.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Dormant, non-replicating organisms are translating minimally, so ribosome-directed drugs have little to act on.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A student is learning bacterial translation and notes that the ribosome contains three defined positions where individual amino acids are loaded and bonded, designated A, P, and E. Which set of names corresponds to these three letters?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acceptor, peptidyl, and elongation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Activation, polymerase, and extension

choices.label: C
choices.text: Anchor, priming, and exchange

choices.label: D
choices.text: Anticodon, primer, and editing

choices.label: E
choices.text: Attachment, processing, and excision

explanation.summary: The three ribosomal sites are A (acceptor), P (peptidyl), and E (elongation).
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacterial ribosomes contain three sites important for peptide synthesis: A = acceptor, P = peptidyl, and E = elongation. Individual amino acids are loaded and bonded at these positions. Protein synthesis inhibitors act by interacting with these sites or with other parts of the ribosomal subunits.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Activation, polymerase, and extension describe other biochemical concepts, not the A, P, and E positions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Anchor, priming, and exchange do not correspond to any of the three defined ribosomal sites.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Anticodon, primer, and editing are not the names given to the three ribosomal sites.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Attachment, processing, and excision are unrelated to the acceptor, peptidyl, and elongation sites.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: An investigator studies an antibiotic whose target lies within the small subunit of the bacterial ribosome. That subunit is built from a single ribosomal RNA molecule together with 21 associated proteins. Which ribosomal RNA is present in this subunit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 5S ribosomal RNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: 16S ribosomal RNA

choices.label: C
choices.text: 18S ribosomal RNA

choices.label: D
choices.text: 23S ribosomal RNA

choices.label: E
choices.text: 28S ribosomal RNA

explanation.summary: The prokaryotic 30S subunit is composed of 16S rRNA plus 21 other proteins.
explanation.whyCorrect: The small ribosomal subunit in bacteria is the 30S subunit, and it is made up of 16S rRNA and 21 additional proteins. Aminoglycosides act at the 30S subunit and specifically target this 16S rRNA. Enzymatic modification of aminoglycosides prevents their interaction with the 16S rRNA.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 5S rRNA is a component of the large 50S subunit, not the small subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 18S rRNA is a eukaryotic ribosomal RNA and is not part of the bacterial small subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 23S rRNA belongs to the 50S subunit and carries peptidyl transferase activity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 28S rRNA is a eukaryotic ribosomal RNA and is not found in bacterial ribosomes.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: The large subunit of the 70S bacterial ribosome is responsible for forming the peptide bond between successive amino acids during protein synthesis. Which ribosomal RNA molecules compose this subunit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 16S rRNA and 23S rRNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: 16S rRNA and 5S rRNA

choices.label: C
choices.text: 18S rRNA and 28S rRNA

choices.label: D
choices.text: 23S rRNA and 28S rRNA

choices.label: E
choices.text: 23S rRNA and 5S rRNA

explanation.summary: The 50S subunit is composed of 23S rRNA and 5S rRNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: In prokaryotes the large subunit is the 50S subunit, composed of 23S rRNA and 5S rRNA. It is the subunit important for forming the peptide bond between amino acids in protein synthesis. The 23S rRNA within it contains peptidyl transferase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 16S rRNA belongs to the small subunit, so this pairing spans two different subunits.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 16S rRNA is a component of the 30S small subunit, not of the large subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 18S and 28S rRNA are eukaryotic ribosomal RNAs and are absent from bacterial ribosomes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 28S rRNA is eukaryotic, so it cannot be part of the bacterial 50S subunit.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A bacterial mutant binds incoming charged tRNAs normally but cannot join successive amino acids into a growing polypeptide chain. The defect maps to the ribosomal RNA that carries peptidyl transferase activity. Which molecule is defective?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The 16S rRNA of the 30S subunit

choices.label: B
choices.text: The 23S rRNA of the 50S subunit

choices.label: C
choices.text: The 5S rRNA of the 50S subunit

choices.label: D
choices.text: The initiator tRNA of the initiation complex

choices.label: E
choices.text: The messenger RNA at the acceptor site

explanation.summary: Peptidyl transferase, the enzyme that forms peptide bonds, resides in the 23S rRNA of the 50S subunit.
explanation.whyCorrect: The 23S rRNA contains peptidyl transferase, the enzyme that forms the peptide bonds between amino acids. A defect there permits tRNA binding but prevents bond formation. Chloramphenicol produces the same functional block by preventing transpeptidation at the 50S subunit.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 16S rRNA is in the small subunit and is involved in decoding, not in peptide bond formation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 5S rRNA is part of the 50S subunit but is not the molecule that carries peptidyl transferase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The initiator tRNA participates in initiation complex formation rather than in transpeptidation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Messenger RNA carries the coding sequence and has no catalytic role in peptide bond formation.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A medicinal chemist describes a class of antibacterial agents constructed from two or more amino sugars linked to a central aminocyclitol nucleus, with individual members differing in the amino sugars they carry. Which antibiotic class is described?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycosides

choices.label: B
choices.text: Macrolides

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oxazolidinones

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptogramins

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tetracyclines

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides are composed of two or more amino sugars bonded to an aminocyclitol nucleus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Structurally, aminoglycosides consist of two or more amino sugars bonded to an aminocyclitol nucleus, and the various aminoglycosides differ in which amino sugars they carry. These sugar moieties make the agents very hydrophilic, which is why they must be given intravenously.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Macrolides carry the suffix '-mycin' and include azithromycin, clarithromycin, and erythromycin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oxazolidinones are represented by linezolid and are structurally unrelated to amino sugars.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Streptogramins comprise dalfopristin and quinupristin and do not share this aminocyclitol structure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tetracyclines are named for their four-ring structure and end in the suffix '-cycline', not for amino sugars.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with a health care-associated gram-negative infection is to be started on an aminoglycoside. Which of the following drugs belongs to that class?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: C
choices.text: Erythromycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Linezolid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tobramycin

explanation.summary: Tobramycin is an aminoglycoside, alongside streptomycin, neomycin, gentamicin, and amikacin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Common examples of aminoglycosides include streptomycin, neomycin, gentamicin, tobramycin, and amikacin. All are 30S protein synthesis inhibitors. Because their structure contains sugar moieties they are very hydrophilic and are administered intravenously.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clindamycin is a lincosamide that binds the 50S ribosomal subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Doxycycline is a second-generation tetracycline, a different 30S protein synthesis inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Erythromycin is a macrolide, identified by the '-mycin' suffix, acting at the 50S subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Linezolid is an oxazolidinone that binds the 23S rRNA of the 50S subunit.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: An intern asks why gentamicin cannot simply be prescribed as a tablet for an outpatient. Which property of aminoglycosides best explains the need for parenteral administration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dietary calcium chelates them within the gastric lumen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism removes them rapidly

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gastric acid degrades them into inactive ring fragments

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gut peptidases destroy them before absorption occurs

choices.label: E
choices.text: Their sugar moieties make them hydrophilic and poorly absorbed

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides are highly hydrophilic because of their sugar moieties, so they are absorbed poorly and given IV or IM.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because their structure contains sugar moieties, aminoglycosides are very hydrophilic. Poor oral absorption follows, so these agents are administered intravenously or intramuscularly. They are then eliminated unchanged by the kidneys.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chelation by dietary cations is not the mechanism given for the parenteral route of aminoglycosides.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The 30S ribosomal inhibitors are not substantially metabolized, so first-pass metabolism does not explain this.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acid degradation is not the stated limitation; poor absorption of a hydrophilic molecule is.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aminoglycosides are not peptides, and proteolysis in the gut is not the reason they are given parenterally.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: Tetracyclines were originally valued for broad-spectrum activity, but bacterial resistance eroded that advantage. Agents with greater antibacterial properties were then developed and remain widely used today. Which pair represents these second-generation tetracyclines?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin and clarithromycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dalfopristin and quinupristin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Doxycycline and minocycline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptomycin and neomycin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tobramycin and amikacin

explanation.summary: Doxycycline and minocycline are the second-generation tetracyclines developed in response to resistance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tetracyclines end in '-cycline' and were known for broad-spectrum activity. As bacteria developed resistance, the second-generation agents doxycycline and minocycline were developed with greater antibacterial properties and are still widely used today.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azithromycin and clarithromycin are macrolides that act at the 50S subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dalfopristin and quinupristin are streptogramins that act synergistically at the 50S subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Streptomycin and neomycin are aminoglycosides, not tetracyclines.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tobramycin and amikacin are aminoglycosides composed of amino sugars.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with community-acquired atypical pneumonia is treated with a macrolide. Which of the following agents is a macrolide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amikacin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Azithromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Chloramphenicol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Linezolid

explanation.summary: Macrolides carry the suffix '-mycin' and include azithromycin, clarithromycin, and erythromycin.
explanation.whyCorrect: The macrolides are 50S protein synthesis inhibitors identified by the suffix '-mycin' and include azithromycin, clarithromycin, and erythromycin. They interfere with protein elongation by binding reversibly to the 50S ribosomal subunit.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amikacin is an aminoglycoside that acts at the 30S subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chloramphenicol is its own agent that binds the 50S subunit and prevents transpeptidation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clindamycin is a lincosamide, a separate class that also binds the 50S subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Linezolid is an oxazolidinone that binds the 23S rRNA of the 50S subunit.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man with an anaerobic soft-tissue infection is treated with clindamycin. To which antibiotic class does clindamycin belong, and which ribosomal subunit does it bind?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycoside; 30S subunit

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lincosamide; 50S subunit

choices.label: C
choices.text: Macrolide; 50S subunit

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxazolidinone; 50S subunit

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tetracycline; 30S subunit

explanation.summary: Clindamycin is the lincosamide among the 50S protein synthesis inhibitors.
explanation.whyCorrect: The 50S protein synthesis inhibitors comprise macrolides, the lincosamide clindamycin, streptogramins, and oxazolidinones. Clindamycin binds reversibly to the 50S ribosomal subunit and, like the macrolides, interferes with protein elongation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aminoglycosides are amino sugar compounds acting at the 30S subunit and 16S rRNA.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Macrolides are the '-mycin' agents azithromycin, clarithromycin, and erythromycin, not clindamycin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The oxazolidinone class is represented by linezolid, a different 50S agent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tetracyclines end in '-cycline' and bind the 30S subunit, which does not describe clindamycin.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman with a resistant gram-positive bloodstream infection is given linezolid. Linezolid is the representative member of which antibiotic class?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycosides

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lincosamides

choices.label: C
choices.text: Macrolides

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxazolidinones

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptogramins

explanation.summary: Linezolid is an oxazolidinone and one of the 50S protein synthesis inhibitors.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oxazolidinones, represented by linezolid, are important members of the 50S protein synthesis inhibitors. Linezolid binds the 23S ribosomal RNA of the 50S subunit at the interphase of the 30S and 50S subunits to prevent initiation complex formation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aminoglycosides are 30S inhibitors built from amino sugars, such as gentamicin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The lincosamide class is represented by clindamycin, not linezolid.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Macrolides carry the '-mycin' suffix and include azithromycin and erythromycin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptogramins are dalfopristin and quinupristin, which are given together for synergy.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: Doxycycline is added to a culture of susceptible bacteria. Translation stalls because charged tRNAs can no longer reach the ribosomal position at which they are first delivered. Which action explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It binds the 30S subunit and blocks aminoacyl-tRNA access to the A site

choices.label: B
choices.text: It blocks translocation of tRNA from the A site to the P site

choices.label: C
choices.text: It causes misreading of mRNA codons by the small ribosomal subunit

choices.label: D
choices.text: It inhibits peptidyl transferase within the large ribosomal subunit

choices.label: E
choices.text: It prevents assembly of the initiation complex at the subunit interface

explanation.summary: Tetracyclines bind the 30S subunit and block access of aminoacyl-tRNA to the A (acceptor) site.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tetracyclines inhibit bacterial protein synthesis by inhibiting ribosomal 30S function. They bind to the 30S subunit and inhibit access of aminoacyl tRNA to the A (acceptor) site on the ribosomal complex, which halts elongation before a new amino acid can be delivered.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Blocking translocation is the action of macrolides and clindamycin at the 50S subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Misreading of mRNA is characteristic of aminoglycosides, which also target the 16S rRNA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibition of peptidyl transferase describes chloramphenicol, which prevents transpeptidation at the 50S subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Preventing initiation complex formation at the subunit interface describes linezolid.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: Tetracyclines are classified as bacteriostatic rather than bactericidal. Which feature of their interaction with the bacterial ribosome best accounts for this classification?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Their binding to the 30S ribosomal subunit is reversible

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are exported by efflux pumps before they can bind

choices.label: C
choices.text: They bind the 50S subunit rather than the 30S subunit

choices.label: D
choices.text: They cannot cross the bacterial cytoplasmic membrane at all

choices.label: E
choices.text: They undergo rapid hepatic metabolism to inactive products

explanation.summary: Reversible binding of tetracyclines to the 30S subunit makes them bacteriostatic.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tetracycline binding to the 30S subunit is reversible, which is what makes tetracycline a bacteriostatic inhibitor. Bacteriostatic agents prevent bacterial reproduction rather than causing death, in contrast to bactericidal agents such as the aminoglycosides.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Efflux by the TetA pump is a resistance mechanism, not the reason the drug class is bacteriostatic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tetracyclines are 30S inhibitors, so this statement misassigns their ribosomal target.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tetracyclines are lipophilic and penetrate tissues well; they do reach the cytoplasmic ribosome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tetracyclines are eliminated by biliary excretion, and metabolism does not define bacteriostatic action.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: Streptomycin is added to a culture of susceptible gram-negative bacilli. Which ribosomal target does this agent primarily engage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The 30S ribosomal subunit, including the 16S rRNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: The 5S rRNA of the 50S ribosomal subunit

choices.label: C
choices.text: The elongation site of the large ribosomal subunit

choices.label: D
choices.text: The interphase between the 30S and 50S subunits

choices.label: E
choices.text: The peptidyl transferase center of the 23S rRNA

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides act primarily at the 30S ribosomal subunit and target the 16S rRNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: The primary site of action of aminoglycosides is the 30S ribosomal subunit, and they also target the 16S ribosomal RNA. Resistance enzymes that acetylate aminoglycosides work precisely by preventing this interaction with the 16S rRNA.

whyWrongByChoice.B: 5S rRNA is part of the 50S subunit and is not the aminoglycoside target.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The elongation site on the large subunit is engaged by macrolides and clindamycin, not aminoglycosides.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Binding at the 30S-50S interphase describes linezolid, which blocks initiation complex formation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The peptidyl transferase center in 23S rRNA is where chloramphenicol acts to block transpeptidation.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: Unlike most protein synthesis inhibitors, aminoglycosides kill susceptible bacteria outright rather than merely arresting their growth. Which sequence of events best explains this bactericidal effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Efflux pumps concentrate the drug in the periplasm, rupturing the cell wall

choices.label: B
choices.text: Incomplete peptides are released, halting all further rounds of initiation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mistranslated proteins are incorporated into the cell membrane, causing lysis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peptide bond formation is blocked, so ribosomes dissociate from the mRNA

choices.label: E
choices.text: The 23S rRNA is methylated, permanently silencing the large subunit

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides are bactericidal because mistranslated proteins inserted into the cell membrane cause lysis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycosides cause incorporation of incorrect amino acids and proteins, and mistranslated proteins are incorporated into the bacterial cell membrane, resulting in lysis. Protein mistranslation also produces abnormal, nonfunctional ribosomes, causing irreversible inhibition and bacterial death. This is why aminoglycosides are bactericidal while most protein synthesis inhibitors are bacteriostatic.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Efflux pumps export drug out of the cytoplasm as a resistance mechanism; they do not concentrate it or rupture the wall.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Release of incomplete proteins describes macrolides and clindamycin, agents that are mostly bacteriostatic.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Blocking peptide bond formation is the bacteriostatic action of chloramphenicol, which does not kill the organism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Methylation of 23S rRNA is the erm-mediated resistance mechanism, not a drug effect that kills bacteria.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: An investigator finds that bacteria exposed to gentamicin produce prematurely truncated and inaccurately sequenced polypeptides. Which drug effect best explains this observation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Competitive displacement of initiator tRNA from the mRNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disruption of translational proofreading, causing mRNA misreading

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enzymatic cleavage of the nascent polypeptide chain

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibition of transpeptidation by the large ribosomal subunit

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reversible blockade of the ribosomal elongation site

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides disrupt translational proofreading and cause misreading of mRNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycosides disrupt translational proofreading of amino acids, causing premature truncation or inaccurate translation of proteins. They also cause misreading of mRNA at the 30S subunit. The resulting abnormal proteins account for the bactericidal action of this class.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Displacement of initiator tRNA is not the described aminoglycoside action; blocking initiation complex formation is linezolid's effect.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Protein synthesis inhibitors do not cleave nascent chains; they interfere with ribosomal function.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibition of transpeptidation is the chloramphenicol mechanism and produces bacteriostatic arrest, not misreading.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reversible blockade at the elongation site describes macrolides and clindamycin, which release incomplete but not misread proteins.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: Erythromycin and clindamycin belong to different antibiotic classes but share a mechanism at the bacterial ribosome. Which statement describes that shared mechanism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They bind 16S rRNA and cause codon misreading in elongation

choices.label: B
choices.text: They bind the 30S subunit and block charged tRNA delivery

choices.label: C
choices.text: They bind the 50S subunit reversibly and block tRNA translocation

choices.label: D
choices.text: They bind the subunit interface and prevent initiation complex formation

choices.label: E
choices.text: They covalently modify peptidyl transferase and thereby halt elongation

explanation.summary: Macrolides and clindamycin bind the 50S subunit reversibly and inhibit transpeptidation and translocation across the A, P, and E sites.
explanation.whyCorrect: Macrolides and clindamycin interfere with protein elongation by binding reversibly to the 50S ribosomal subunit. This binding inhibits transpeptidation and translocation of tRNA across the A, P, and E sites, resulting in the release of incomplete proteins. Most of these agents are bacteriostatic in action.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Binding 16S rRNA with codon misreading describes aminoglycosides, which are 30S agents.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blocking delivery of charged tRNA to the A site at the 30S subunit is the tetracycline mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Binding at the 30S-50S interphase to block initiation is unique to linezolid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: These agents bind reversibly and do not covalently modify peptidyl transferase.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A patient with a resistant gram-positive infection is treated with linezolid. Which action accounts for this drug's effect on bacterial translation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It binds 16S rRNA and induces misreading of the mRNA template

choices.label: B
choices.text: It binds 23S rRNA at the subunit interphase, blocking initiation

choices.label: C
choices.text: It blocks aminoacyl-tRNA delivery to the A site of the 30S subunit

choices.label: D
choices.text: It exports protons inward while pumping the nascent peptide outward

choices.label: E
choices.text: It inhibits peptidyl transferase only after the first peptide bond forms

explanation.summary: Linezolid binds 23S rRNA of the 50S subunit at the 30S-50S interphase and prevents initiation complex formation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Linezolid binds to the interphase of the 30S and 50S subunits to prevent initiation complex formation by blocking the first peptide-bonding step. Its binding site is the 23S ribosomal RNA of the 50S subunit. Because this step is the very first in translation, no polypeptide is produced at all.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Binding 16S rRNA with induced misreading describes aminoglycosides, which act at the 30S subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Blocking aminoacyl-tRNA delivery to the A site of the 30S subunit is the tetracycline mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Proton antiport coupled to drug export describes the TetA efflux pump, a resistance protein.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Linezolid blocks the first peptide-bonding step rather than acting after peptide bonds have formed.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: Linezolid retains activity against many organisms that are already resistant to other protein synthesis inhibitors. Which feature best explains this lack of cross-resistance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It binds the 30S subunit, which is rarely altered by resistance

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is bactericidal rather than bacteriostatic against most organisms

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is converted in vivo to a second, structurally distinct agent

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is not transported by any bacterial membrane antiport protein

choices.label: E
choices.text: It occupies a unique binding site not shared by other inhibitors

explanation.summary: Linezolid's unique binding site on the 23S rRNA deters resistance and frees it from cross-resistance with other protein synthesis inhibitors.
explanation.whyCorrect: Linezolid binds the 23S ribosomal RNA of the 50S subunit at a unique site. This unique binding site acts as a deterrent for developing bacterial resistance and allows linezolid to be free of the cross-resistance that affects other protein synthesis inhibitors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Linezolid binds the 50S subunit, so this statement misassigns its ribosomal target.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cidal versus static activity does not determine cross-resistance; the binding site does.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Linezolid's advantage is its binding site, not conversion to another compound.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The brick attributes linezolid's lack of cross-resistance to its unique binding site, not to efflux pump handling.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: Dalfopristin and quinupristin are administered together because neither agent is adequate alone. Which statement best describes how this combination inhibits bacterial protein synthesis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dalfopristin blocks the 30S subunit while quinupristin blocks the 50S

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dalfopristin inhibits efflux pumps so that quinupristin can accumulate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dalfopristin inhibits the early phase and quinupristin the late phase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dalfopristin methylates 23S rRNA so that quinupristin binds more tightly

choices.label: E
choices.text: Dalfopristin prevents initiation while quinupristin blocks tRNA entry

explanation.summary: The streptogramins act synergistically at the 50S subunit, dalfopristin on the early phase and quinupristin on the late phase of protein synthesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dalfopristin binds the 50S subunit and inhibits the early phase of bacterial protein synthesis, while quinupristin binds the 50S subunit and inhibits the late phase. This synergistic action prevents proper functioning of the ribosomal subunits and disrupts incorporation of amino acids into peptide chains, leading to cell death.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both streptogramins bind the 50S ribosomal subunit; neither acts at the 30S subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Streptogramin synergy comes from inhibiting sequential phases of synthesis, not from blocking efflux pumps.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methylation of 23S rRNA is the erm-mediated resistance mechanism and would reduce, not enhance, drug binding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Preventing initiation complex formation describes linezolid, and blocking tRNA entry describes tetracyclines.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: Chloramphenicol is added to a translating bacterial extract. Peptide bond formation ceases, yet tRNAs continue to occupy the ribosome and the organism is not killed. Which action explains this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acceleration of tRNA translocation out of the elongation site

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blockade of aminoacyl-tRNA entry into the acceptor site

choices.label: C
choices.text: Induction of mRNA misreading by the small ribosomal subunit

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibition of transpeptidation at the 50S ribosomal subunit

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prevention of initiation complex assembly at the subunit interphase

explanation.summary: Chloramphenicol binds the 50S subunit and prevents transpeptidation, a bacteriostatic action.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chloramphenicol binds to the 50S ribosomal subunit and prevents transpeptidation, the peptidyl transferase step that joins amino acids. Because the organism is inhibited but not killed, the action is bacteriostatic, consistent with most protein synthesis inhibitors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Protein synthesis inhibitors block translocation rather than accelerating it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blocking aminoacyl-tRNA entry into the A site is the tetracycline mechanism at the 30S subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Induced mRNA misreading is an aminoglycoside effect and would be bactericidal, not bacteriostatic.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Preventing initiation complex assembly at the subunit interphase describes linezolid.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A student asks why antibiotics that target the 30S and 50S ribosomal subunits do not simply shut down protein synthesis in the patient's own cells. Which explanation is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Human cells export these drugs using the TetA antiport pump protein

choices.label: B
choices.text: Human cells methylate these drugs before they can reach the ribosome

choices.label: C
choices.text: Human ribosomes are not composed of 30S or 50S ribosomal subunits

choices.label: D
choices.text: Human ribosomes are shielded from these drugs by the nuclear membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: Human ribosomes lack ribosomal RNA and use protein enzymes instead

explanation.summary: Protein synthesis inhibitors are selective because eukaryotic ribosomes are not built from 30S and 50S subunits.
explanation.whyCorrect: Eukaryotic ribosomes are not composed of 30S or 50S subunits, so protein synthesis inhibitor antibiotics that target those subunits do not act on human ribosomes. This selectivity does not, however, exclude these agents from having toxic side effects by other means.

whyWrongByChoice.A: TetA is a bacterial efflux pump protein and is not present in human cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Methylation is a bacterial resistance strategy against 50S agents, not a human protective mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Human ribosomes are largely cytoplasmic, and the nuclear membrane does not shield them from drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Eukaryotic ribosomes do contain ribosomal RNA, including 18S and 28S rRNA.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: Aminoglycoside therapy is generally confined to inpatients who can be monitored closely. Which pharmacologic property is the principal reason for this restriction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Their therapeutic range overlaps their toxic concentration range

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are bacteriostatic and must be infused continuously

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are metabolized hepatically to a toxic intermediate

choices.label: D
choices.text: They enter the CSF readily and cause central nervous system toxicity

choices.label: E
choices.text: They require concurrent dosing with a second antibiotic

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides have a narrow therapeutic index, so they are largely restricted to monitored inpatient use.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycosides are known for having a narrow therapeutic index, meaning their therapeutic concentration range is close to or overlaps their toxic concentration range. Because of this narrow window, they are generally confined to inpatient use with careful monitoring.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Aminoglycosides are bactericidal, and the restriction relates to the narrow therapeutic index, not the dosing schedule.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The 30S ribosomal inhibitors are not substantially metabolized and are eliminated unchanged by the kidneys.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The 30S ribosomal inhibitors have minimal CSF penetration, so CNS exposure is not the limiting concern.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Synergistic combination therapy is an option with aminoglycosides but is not a requirement that dictates inpatient use.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A bacterial species is found to be resistant to a protein synthesis inhibitor before it has ever been exposed to the drug. Which term describes this form of resistance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acquired resistance

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adaptive resistance

choices.label: C
choices.text: Induced resistance

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intrinsic resistance

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transmissible resistance

explanation.summary: Intrinsic resistance is pre-existing resistance that is present prior to any antibiotic exposure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacterial resistance can be intrinsic, acquired, or transmissible. Intrinsic resistance is pre-existing bacterial resistance prior to antibiotic exposure, which is exactly what this isolate demonstrates. Acquired and transmissible resistance both require an event after or between organisms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acquired resistance describes resistance that is gained after exposure to the antibiotic.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Adaptive resistance is not among the three named categories of intrinsic, acquired, and transmissible.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Induced resistance is not one of the three categories used to classify bacterial resistance here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transmissible resistance is resistance transferred between bacteria, often by horizontal transfer of plasmids.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A hospitalized patient with a serious infection is started on two antibiotics rather than a single agent. Which of the following is an accepted rationale for combination antibiotic therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It allows both agents to be used at subtherapeutic doses

choices.label: B
choices.text: It can prevent the emergence of resistant organisms

choices.label: C
choices.text: It converts bacteriostatic agents into bactericidal agents

choices.label: D
choices.text: It guarantees adequate penetration into the cerebrospinal fluid

choices.label: E
choices.text: It removes the need for therapeutic drug monitoring

explanation.summary: Combination therapy can enhance effectiveness, prevent emergence of resistant organisms, and broaden the antibacterial spectrum.
explanation.whyCorrect: Combination therapy with antibiotics can enhance effectiveness, prevent the emergence of resistant organisms, or broaden the antibacterial spectrum. Preventing resistant organisms from emerging is one of the three stated rationales for combining agents.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Combination therapy is not used to justify subtherapeutic dosing of either agent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Whether an agent is bacteriostatic or bactericidal is a property of its mechanism, not of combination therapy.
