whyWrongByChoice.D: CSF penetration is determined by the individual drug's properties, such as linezolid's ready CSF entry.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Aminoglycosides still require therapeutic monitoring every 1 to 3 days when used synergistically with other agents.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A gram-negative organism recovered from a health care-associated infection inactivates gentamicin by chemically modifying the drug so that it can no longer interact with 16S rRNA. Which resistance mechanism is responsible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enzymatic acetylation of the drug by a bacterial enzyme

choices.label: B
choices.text: Export of the drug from the cytoplasm by an antiport pump

choices.label: C
choices.text: Methylation of the 23S rRNA within the large ribosomal subunit

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduced affinity of the 50S subunit produced by a point mutation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sequestration of the drug within the bacterial periplasmic space

explanation.summary: Gram-negative organisms inactivate aminoglycosides enzymatically, notably by acetylation that prevents interaction with 16S rRNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacteria can change the antibiotic itself by producing enzymes such as phosphotransferase or adenylyltransferase that inactivate protein synthesis inhibitors by modifying their chemical structure. Gram-negative organisms responsible for health care-associated infections are well documented for spreading enzymes that inactivate aminoglycosides by acetylation, preventing their interaction with the 16S rRNA.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Efflux moves intact drug out of the cell rather than chemically modifying the molecule.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Methylation of 23S rRNA alters the 50S target site and affects macrolides and clindamycin, not gentamicin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aminoglycosides act at the 30S subunit, and this option also describes target alteration rather than drug inactivation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sequestration in the periplasm is not among the described mechanisms of resistance.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A gram-positive isolate acquires an erm gene. Susceptibility testing now shows resistance not only to erythromycin but also to clindamycin. Which change best explains the shared loss of activity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A mutation in 16S rRNA lowers the ribosomal affinity for both drugs

choices.label: B
choices.text: An acetyltransferase modifies both drugs before they reach the ribosome

choices.label: C
choices.text: An efflux pump exports both drugs out of the bacterial cytoplasm

choices.label: D
choices.text: Methylation of 23S rRNA alters the binding site shared by both drugs

choices.label: E
choices.text: Peptidyl transferase is duplicated so that one copy remains functional

explanation.summary: The erm gene methylates 23S rRNA, producing cross-resistance across the entire MLS family because these drugs share a target site.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gram-positive bacteria can transfer erm (erythromycin ribosome methylation) genes, which alter the 23S rRNA. Methylation of parts of the 50S subunit reduces the binding capability of certain 50S agents. Changing this target site creates resistance not only to macrolides but also to the rest of the MLS family, including the lincosamide clindamycin, because of their shared target site.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 16S rRNA is in the 30S subunit; macrolides and clindamycin bind the 50S subunit instead.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Acetylation is the enzymatic inactivation route documented for aminoglycosides, not for erm-mediated resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Efflux is a separate resistance mechanism and is not what the erm gene encodes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Duplication of peptidyl transferase is not a described resistance mechanism.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: Tetracycline resistance in many bacteria is mediated by the TetA protein, which inserts into the bacterial cell membrane. How does this protein reduce the activity of tetracycline?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It binds tetracycline in the cytoplasm and holds it away from ribosomes

choices.label: B
choices.text: It cleaves the tetracycline molecule into inactive ring fragments

choices.label: C
choices.text: It closes outer membrane porins so tetracycline cannot enter the cell

choices.label: D
choices.text: It methylates 16S rRNA so that tetracycline can no longer bind

choices.label: E
choices.text: It pumps tetracycline out of the cell while moving protons inward

explanation.summary: TetA is an antiport efflux pump that expels tetracycline from the cytoplasm while importing protons.
explanation.whyCorrect: Protein synthesis inhibitors must act on the ribosome within the cytoplasm to be effective. Tetracyclines are susceptible to efflux by the TetA pump protein, an antiport pump that inserts into the cell membrane to pump tetracycline out and protons inside the cell. Removing the drug from the cytoplasm keeps it away from its ribosomal target.

whyWrongByChoice.A: TetA actively exports the drug across the membrane rather than sequestering it inside the cell.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Enzymatic inactivation modifies the drug's chemical structure but is not the function of the TetA pump.
whyWrongByChoice.C: TetA is a membrane transport protein, not a regulator of outer membrane porin channels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methylation describes target site alteration, and the erm-mediated version affects 23S rRNA, not 16S.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man with chronic kidney disease is to receive tobramycin for a serious gram-negative infection. How is this drug eliminated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fecal excretion after extensive enterohepatic recirculation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hepatic conjugation with urinary excretion of the metabolites

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hepatic metabolism followed by biliary excretion into the gut

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hydrolysis by plasma esterases to inactive breakdown products

choices.label: E
choices.text: Renal excretion of unchanged drug by the kidneys

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides are not substantially metabolized and are eliminated unchanged by the kidneys.
explanation.whyCorrect: The 30S ribosomal inhibitors are not substantially metabolized. Aminoglycosides are given IV or IM because of poor oral absorption, and they are eliminated unchanged by the kidneys. Their hydrophilic nature underlies this entirely renal clearance, which is why reduced renal function requires lower target serum concentrations.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fecal elimination is seen with tetracyclines such as minocycline, not with aminoglycosides.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aminoglycosides are excreted unchanged, so hepatic conjugation does not occur to a significant degree.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hepatic metabolism with biliary excretion characterizes the 50S ribosomal inhibitors, not aminoglycosides.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Plasma esterase hydrolysis is not a route of elimination for this class.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A patient being treated for a tetracycline-susceptible infection is switched from intravenous to oral doxycycline. Which statement about the administration and elimination of tetracyclines is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They may be given only intravenously and are eliminated unchanged renally

choices.label: B
choices.text: They may be given only topically and are eliminated by plasma hydrolysis

choices.label: C
choices.text: They may be given orally alone and are eliminated by pulmonary exhalation

choices.label: D
choices.text: They may be given orally or IM and are eliminated by salivary secretion

choices.label: E
choices.text: They may be given orally, IV, or IM and are eliminated by biliary excretion

explanation.summary: Tetracyclines can be given orally, IV, or IM and are eliminated by biliary excretion in urine and feces.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tetracyclines can be taken orally, intravenously, or intramuscularly, which makes an IV-to-oral switch straightforward. They are eliminated via biliary excretion in urine and feces. Their lipophilicity also gives them great tissue penetration and distribution.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Restriction to the intravenous route with unchanged renal elimination describes aminoglycosides.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tetracyclines are not limited to topical use, and plasma hydrolysis is not their elimination route.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tetracyclines are not restricted to oral dosing, and pulmonary exhalation is not a route of elimination for them.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Salivary secretion is not the described elimination pathway for the tetracycline class.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A patient with advanced cirrhosis is being considered for therapy with a 50S ribosomal inhibitor. Which general pharmacokinetic feature of this group is most relevant to that decision?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are eliminated unchanged by glomerular filtration in the kidney

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are excreted largely in the feces without being absorbed

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are hydrolyzed in plasma before reaching peripheral tissues

choices.label: D
choices.text: They are metabolized by the liver after oral administration

choices.label: E
choices.text: They are removed almost entirely by biliary sequestration

explanation.summary: The 50S ribosomal inhibitors are generally given orally or topically and are hepatically metabolized.
explanation.whyCorrect: The 50S ribosomal inhibitors can generally be administered orally or topically and are hepatically metabolized. Hepatic handling makes them relevant to liver disease and is also the basis for the drug interactions discussed in the later protein synthesis inhibitor bricks.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Unchanged renal elimination describes aminoglycosides, which are 30S rather than 50S agents.
whyWrongByChoice.B: These agents have good bioavailability and are absorbed, so unabsorbed fecal excretion is incorrect.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Plasma hydrolysis is not the described route of elimination for this group.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Biliary excretion in urine and feces is described for tetracyclines, which are 30S agents.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: Orally administered macrolides reach the systemic circulation incompletely, and the fraction absorbed varies with the stability of the particular agent at gastric pH. What is the approximate oral bioavailability of this group?

explanation.summary: Orally administered macrolides have a bioavailability of about 30% to 50%, depending on gastric pH stability.
explanation.whyCorrect: Orally administered macrolides have a bioavailability of 30% to 50% depending on the stability of the particular drug at gastric pH. Despite this partial absorption, all macrolides have good tissue penetration and are well concentrated in tissues and phagocytic cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A bioavailability of 5% to 10% is well below the range described for orally administered macrolides.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A range of 15% to 25% understates macrolide oral bioavailability.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A range of 60% to 75% overstates macrolide bioavailability.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bioavailability near 90% describes clindamycin after oral administration, not the macrolides.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman with osteomyelitis is treated with oral clindamycin. Which statement about clindamycin's pharmacokinetics is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Oral bioavailability is about 30%, and it concentrates in the CSF

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oral bioavailability is about 50%, and it stays confined to plasma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral bioavailability is about 70%, and it accumulates in the kidney

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral bioavailability is about 90%, and it distributes well into bone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral bioavailability is negligible, and it must be given intravenously

explanation.summary: Clindamycin has roughly 90% oral bioavailability and distributes well into tissues, especially bone, with little CSF penetration.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clindamycin has approximately 90% bioavailability after oral administration and distributes well into body tissues, especially bone. This bone penetration is what makes it attractive for osteomyelitis. It also has little CSF penetration.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A bioavailability near 30% fits the macrolides, and clindamycin has little CSF penetration.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Clindamycin's bioavailability is higher than 50%, and it distributes widely into body tissues rather than remaining in plasma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clindamycin's bioavailability is about 90%, and renal accumulation is not its described distribution pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clindamycin is well absorbed orally, so the intravenous route is not required for tissue penetration.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: Among the protein synthesis inhibitors, one agent has excellent bioavailability and readily enters the cerebrospinal fluid. Which agent is this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: C
choices.text: Erythromycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gentamicin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Linezolid

explanation.summary: Linezolid has excellent bioavailability and readily enters the CSF.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although the 50S ribosomal inhibitors have variable CSF penetration as a group, linezolid stands out with excellent bioavailability and ready entry into the cerebrospinal fluid. The other agents in the group penetrate the CSF poorly.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clindamycin is well absorbed orally but has little CSF penetration.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Doxycycline is a tetracycline, and the 30S inhibitors show minimal CSF penetration.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Macrolides such as erythromycin penetrate CSF poorly in the absence of meningeal inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gentamicin is an aminoglycoside; the 30S inhibitors have minimal CSF penetration and poor oral absorption.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A hospitalized patient receiving an aminoglycoside is evaluated every 1 to 3 days for drug toxicity. Which combination of assessments is used for this monitoring?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complete blood count plus assessment of peripheral sensory function

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prothrombin time plus assessment of muscle strength and reflexes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serum creatinine plus assessment of vestibular and auditory function

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum potassium plus electrocardiographic monitoring of the QT interval

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum transaminases plus assessment of visual acuity and color vision

explanation.summary: Aminoglycoside toxicity is monitored every 1 to 3 days with serum creatinine and subjective assessment of vestibular and auditory function.
explanation.whyCorrect: Therapeutic monitoring of aminoglycoside toxicity is measured every 1 to 3 days via serum creatinine and subjective patient assessment of vestibular and auditory function. This monitoring is necessary because of the narrow therapeutic window that confines these drugs to inpatient use. Lower serum concentrations are targeted when aminoglycosides are used synergistically or in patients with reduced renal function.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blood counts and peripheral sensory testing are not the described monitoring parameters for this class.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Prothrombin time and neuromuscular testing are not used to follow aminoglycoside toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Potassium and QT interval monitoring are not the assessments specified for aminoglycoside toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transaminases and visual assessment are not the parameters used for aminoglycosides, which are renally cleared.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with gram-negative bacteremia completes a 10-day course of an intravenous antibiotic. Two weeks later he reports persistent high-frequency hearing loss and constant ringing in both ears. Which of the following antibiotics is most likely responsible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amikacin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Linezolid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Quinupristin/dalfopristin

explanation.summary: Ototoxicity is one of the two classic adverse reactions of the aminoglycosides.
explanation.whyCorrect: Amikacin is an aminoglycoside, and nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity are the two common adverse reactions of this class. The drug accumulates in cochlear cells, where inhibition of mitochondrial ribosomes causes cell death. Because cochlear cells cannot regenerate, the resulting hearing loss is irreversible.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Clindamycin causes diarrhea, allergic reaction and neuromuscular blockade, and is linked to pseudomembranous colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxycycline is a tetracycline; its characteristic adverse effects are GI upset, photosensitivity and tooth discoloration, not ototoxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Linezolid most characteristically causes bone marrow suppression, peripheral neuropathy and serotonin syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Quinupristin/dalfopristin is a streptogramin, and its hallmark adverse effect is arthralgia/myalgia.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 71-year-old woman receiving gentamicin for 8 days has a rise in serum creatinine from 0.9 mg/dL to 2.1 mg/dL. Urine microscopy shows muddy brown granular casts consistent with acute tubular necrosis. Which of the following best explains this drug's renal toxicity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It constricts the afferent arteriole and lowers glomerular filtration pressure

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is filtered at the glomerulus and accumulates within proximal tubular cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: It obstructs the collecting ducts with pigmented protein casts

choices.label: D
choices.text: It precipitates as insoluble crystals within the distal tubular lumen

choices.label: E
choices.text: It triggers an IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction in the renal interstitium

explanation.summary: Aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity is proximal tubular accumulation leading to acute tubular necrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycosides are able to filter across the glomerulus and then accumulate in the cells of the proximal convoluted tubule. That accumulation increases the permeability of those cells, which can lead to acute tubular necrosis. This is why creatinine and urine sediment are monitored during therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aminoglycosides are not described as causing renal injury through afferent arteriolar constriction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pigment cast obstruction describes myoglobinuric injury, not aminoglycoside toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Crystal precipitation in the tubular lumen is not the mechanism described for aminoglycosides.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The injury is a direct toxic tubular effect, not an allergic interstitial reaction.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: Two patients are started on the same weight-based dose of gentamicin: a 25-year-old man with normal renal function and an 80-year-old woman with a creatinine clearance of 30 mL/min. The older patient is judged to be at substantially higher risk of nephrotoxicity. Which of the following best accounts for this difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycoside plasma protein binding is markedly higher in older adults

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elderly patients absorb a much greater fraction of each intramuscular dose

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elderly patients convert aminoglycosides into a nephrotoxic metabolite

choices.label: D
choices.text: Elderly patients have higher glomerular filtration of aminoglycosides

choices.label: E
choices.text: Impaired renal function and advanced age both raise aminoglycoside nephrotoxic risk

explanation.summary: Aminoglycoside nephrotoxic risk rises with impaired renal function and with older age.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states explicitly that the nephrotoxicity risk of aminoglycosides increases with impaired renal function and in the elderly. Both features apply to the older patient, so the same dose carries a higher risk of tubular accumulation and acute tubular necrosis for her.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Altered protein binding is not given as the reason for the increased risk.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Increased intramuscular absorption with age is not a described risk factor for this toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aminoglycoside toxicity is attributed to accumulation of the drug itself, not to a metabolite.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glomerular filtration falls rather than rises with age and renal impairment.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman treated with amikacin develops bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Six months after the drug was stopped, repeat audiometry shows no improvement. Which of the following best explains the permanence of this deficit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycosides permanently occlude the cochlear blood supply

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cochlear cells that have been killed are unable to regenerate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cochlear damage is sustained by an ongoing autoimmune response

choices.label: D
choices.text: The deficit reflects irreversible injury to the auditory cortex

choices.label: E
choices.text: The drug remains irreversibly bound to cochlear ribosomes for years

explanation.summary: Aminoglycoside hearing loss is permanent because cochlear cells cannot regenerate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ototoxicity is caused by inhibition of mitochondrial ribosomes in cochlear and vestibular cells, resulting in cell death. Cochlear cells are unable to regenerate, so once they are lost the hearing loss is irreversible. This contrasts with the vestibular deficits, which are sometimes reversed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Vascular occlusion of the cochlea is not the described mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: No autoimmune mechanism is described for aminoglycoside ototoxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The lesion is in the cochlear hair cells of the inner ear, not in the auditory cortex.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The brick attributes the permanence to cell death and failed regeneration, not to persistent drug binding.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man treated with gentamicin develops disequilibrium and unsteady gait along with hearing loss. Over the following months his balance gradually improves, although his hearing remains unchanged. Which of the following best explains the improvement in his balance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycosides are cleared from vestibular tissue within hours

choices.label: B
choices.text: The balance symptoms were caused by a transient electrolyte shift

choices.label: C
choices.text: The vestibular nerve is shielded from the drug by the blood-labyrinth barrier

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vestibular cells are able to regenerate after they are injured

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vestibular cells are not affected by aminoglycoside exposure

explanation.summary: Vestibular cells can regenerate, so aminoglycoside balance deficits are sometimes reversible.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycosides kill both cochlear and vestibular cells by inhibiting mitochondrial ribosomes. Unlike cochlear cells, vestibular cells can regenerate, and balance deficits are therefore sometimes reversed. The cochlear loss in the same patient remains permanent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Rapid clearance from the tissue is not the reason given for recovery.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The deficit is due to drug-induced vestibular cell death, not an electrolyte disturbance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The vestibular apparatus is clearly exposed to the drug, as shown by the symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vestibular cells are directly affected; that is why the patient became unsteady in the first place.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A researcher exposes cultured cochlear hair cells to increasing concentrations of gentamicin and observes progressive cell death. Which of the following intracellular targets is most directly responsible for this toxicity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lysosomal proton pumps

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mitochondrial ribosomes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nuclear DNA topoisomerase II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Plasma membrane sodium channels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sarcoplasmic calcium ATPase

explanation.summary: Aminoglycoside ototoxicity comes from inhibition of mitochondrial ribosomes in inner ear cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ototoxicity is caused by inhibition of mitochondrial ribosomes in cochlear and vestibular cells, which results in cell death. Mitochondrial ribosomes resemble the bacterial ribosomes these drugs are designed to target, which is why host inner ear cells are vulnerable.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lysosomal proton pumps are not the target described for aminoglycoside inner ear toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Topoisomerase inhibition is not a mechanism attributed to aminoglycosides.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sodium channel blockade is unrelated to aminoglycoside cochlear injury.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Calcium ATPase inhibition is not described as the basis of ototoxicity.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman with myasthenia gravis is given intravenous tobramycin for a resistant urinary tract infection. Within hours she develops worsening ptosis, diplopia, and shallow breathing requiring respiratory support. Which of the following drug effects best explains this deterioration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antagonism of acetylcholine receptors producing neuromuscular blockade

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blockade of voltage-gated sodium channels in the phrenic nerve

choices.label: C
choices.text: Depletion of acetylcholine stores from presynaptic vesicles

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased production of anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibition of acetylcholinesterase at the motor end plate

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides can rarely antagonize acetylcholine receptors and cause neuromuscular blockade.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rarely, aminoglycosides antagonize acetylcholine receptors, leading to neuromuscular blockade, so caution is advised in patients with myasthenia gravis. In myasthenia gravis, antibodies already interrupt acetylcholine binding at the receptor, and an aminoglycoside blockade directly compounds that existing deficit.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The effect described is at the acetylcholine receptor, not at nerve sodium channels.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aminoglycosides act on the receptor rather than by depleting presynaptic acetylcholine stores.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aminoglycosides are not described as increasing autoantibody production.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Acetylcholinesterase inhibition would increase acetylcholine at the junction and improve, not worsen, weakness.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman reports drooping eyelids and weakness of her arms that worsens the longer she uses them and improves with rest. Which of the following best describes the underlying defect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibodies that block acetylcholine binding to its receptor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoantibodies directed against skeletal muscle actin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Degeneration of anterior horn motor neurons

choices.label: D
choices.text: Demyelination of peripheral motor nerves

choices.label: E
choices.text: Failure of acetylcholine release from the presynaptic terminal

explanation.summary: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disease in which antibodies interrupt acetylcholine binding at its receptor.
explanation.whyCorrect: Myasthenia gravis classically presents as muscle weakness that worsens with usage. Normally acetylcholine released from the nerve activates receptors on muscle to initiate contraction; in myasthenia gravis, antibodies alter those receptors and interrupt acetylcholine binding. This is the deficit that an aminoglycoside-induced neuromuscular blockade would compound.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The antibodies are directed at the acetylcholine receptor rather than at muscle actin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Anterior horn cell degeneration describes a motor neuron disease, not myasthenia gravis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Demyelination of motor nerves is not the lesion in myasthenia gravis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The defect is at the postsynaptic receptor, not in presynaptic acetylcholine release.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman who is 16 weeks pregnant requires antibiotic therapy. Which of the following agents is most likely to be avoided in this patient because of the risk of fetal harm?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin, given orally

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clindamycin, given orally

choices.label: C
choices.text: Erythromycin, given orally

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gentamicin, given intravenously

choices.label: E
choices.text: Quinupristin/dalfopristin, given intravenously

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides can cause fetal harm and are avoided in pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gentamicin is an aminoglycoside, and the brick states that aminoglycosides can cause fetal harm if given in pregnancy. Of the listed protein synthesis inhibitors, it is the one whose fetal risk is specifically highlighted.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azithromycin is a macrolide; fetal harm is not the adverse effect emphasized for this class.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Clindamycin's listed adverse effects are diarrhea, allergic reaction and neuromuscular blockade.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Erythromycin's concerns are hepatic metabolism, CYP3A4 interactions and QT prolongation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptogramins are associated with arthralgia/myalgia and laboratory abnormalities, not fetal harm.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man is receiving amikacin for a resistant Pseudomonas infection, and the team wants to avoid adding a second nephrotoxic agent. Which of the following medications would most increase his risk of renal injury?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Linezolid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Concurrent nephrotoxic drugs such as vancomycin add to aminoglycoside renal risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists concurrent use of other nephrotoxic drugs as a risk multiplier for aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity, naming amphotericin B, polymyxins, NSAIDs, radiocontrast dye and vancomycin. Adding vancomycin to amikacin therefore compounds the tubular injury risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azithromycin's key concerns are CYP3A4 interactions and QT prolongation, not renal toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Clindamycin is associated with diarrhea and pseudomembranous colitis rather than nephrotoxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxycycline is linked to GI symptoms and photosensitivity, not renal injury.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Linezolid causes bone marrow suppression, peripheral neuropathy and serotonin syndrome.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman begins oral tetracycline for acne and asks what side effects are most likely. Which of the following should she be told is the most common problem with this drug?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Easy bruising and mucosal bleeding

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea

choices.label: C
choices.text: Numbness and tingling of the feet

choices.label: D
choices.text: Painful joints and aching muscles

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ringing in the ears and hearing loss

explanation.summary: Tetracyclines are generally well tolerated but commonly cause gastrointestinal upset.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tetracyclines are considered generally safe, and their most common adverse reactions are gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea, vomiting and diarrhea. Counseling patients that these may occur, and asking them to report if the symptoms become a problem, is part of routine advice when starting the drug.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bleeding from blood dyscrasias suggests chloramphenicol or linezolid marrow toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Peripheral neuropathy is characteristic of prolonged linezolid therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Arthralgia and myalgia are the hallmark of the streptogramins.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tinnitus and hearing loss point to aminoglycoside ototoxicity, not tetracyclines.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy is given a 3-week course of tetracycline. Two years later his erupting permanent teeth show permanent yellow discoloration, and his growth has lagged. Which of the following best explains these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The drug chelates calcium and deposits in calcifying teeth and bone

choices.label: B
choices.text: The drug directly inhibits ribosomes inside mature ameloblasts

choices.label: C
choices.text: The drug induces enamel-degrading matrix metalloproteinases

choices.label: D
choices.text: The drug is oxidized to a yellow pigment within saliva

choices.label: E
choices.text: The drug stimulates melanocytes located within the dental pulp

explanation.summary: Tetracyclines chelate calcium and deposit in calcifying teeth and bone.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tetracyclines other than doxycycline deposit in calcifying teeth and bone, which discolors teeth yellow and can stunt growth in children. The mechanism is chelation, in which the drug binds calcium. This is why tetracyclines are contraindicated in children younger than 8 years.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The dental effect is due to calcium chelation and deposition, not host ribosomal inhibition.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Enzymatic degradation of enamel is not how tetracyclines discolor teeth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Salivary oxidation to a pigment is not the described mechanism of staining.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Melanocyte stimulation in the pulp is not a described tetracycline effect.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A pediatrician is selecting an oral antibiotic and wishes to avoid tetracycline-associated dental staining and growth effects. Tetracyclines are contraindicated in children younger than which of the following ages?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 2 years

choices.label: B
choices.text: 4 years

choices.label: C
choices.text: 8 years

choices.label: D
choices.text: 12 years

choices.label: E
choices.text: 16 years

explanation.summary: Tetracyclines are contraindicated in children younger than 8 years of age.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because tetracyclines chelate calcium and deposit in calcifying teeth and bone, they can discolor teeth and stunt growth in children. For that reason the brick sets the contraindication at children younger than 8 years of age.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 2 years is far below the age threshold used for this class.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 4 years is below the stated threshold and would still leave children at risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 12 years is higher than the age cutoff the brick gives.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 16 years is well beyond the stated contraindication age.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy has a tick-borne illness for which doxycycline is the drug of choice. His mother has read that tetracyclines stain children's teeth and asks whether the drug is safe. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A short course of less than 21 days is acceptable in children

choices.label: B
choices.text: Doxycycline is safe at any duration because it does not bind calcium at all

choices.label: C
choices.text: Doxycycline stains teeth more than other tetracyclines and must be avoided

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staining occurs only once the permanent teeth have fully erupted

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tooth staining can be prevented by taking each dose together with milk

explanation.summary: Short-term doxycycline, under 21 days, is acceptable in children despite the tetracycline class warning.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tetracyclines other than doxycycline are the ones that deposit in calcifying teeth and bone, and the brick states that short-term use of doxycycline for less than 21 days in children is acceptable. A tick-borne illness treated with a brief course falls within that allowance.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The exception is limited to short courses, not an unrestricted duration of therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxycycline is the tetracycline singled out as less likely to deposit in teeth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The risk relates to deposition in calcifying teeth, not to teeth that have already erupted.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Taking the drug with milk causes chelation and blocks absorption rather than preventing staining.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman who is 6 weeks pregnant and still breastfeeding her toddler asks whether she may take tetracycline for acne. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is contraindicated both in pregnancy and in nursing mothers

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is safe during pregnancy but must be stopped while nursing

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is safe while nursing but must be stopped during pregnancy

choices.label: D
choices.text: It may be used in either setting at a reduced daily dose

choices.label: E
choices.text: It may be used in either setting if taken with an antacid

explanation.summary: Tetracycline chelation can cause fetal harm, so the drug is contraindicated in pregnancy and in nursing mothers.
explanation.whyCorrect: The same chelation that deposits tetracyclines in calcifying teeth and bone can also cause fetal harm. The brick therefore lists tetracyclines as contraindicated in pregnancy and in nursing mothers, which covers both of this patient's circumstances.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Pregnancy is one of the two settings in which the drug is contraindicated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nursing mothers are explicitly included in the contraindication.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dose reduction is not offered as a way around the contraindication.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Taking the drug with an antacid chelates it and blocks absorption; it does not make it safe.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man taking doxycycline for acne develops an exaggerated sunburn over his face and forearms after one afternoon outdoors. Which of the following is the most appropriate counseling for him?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Avoid excessive sunlight for the duration of therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Double the dose to overcome the developing tolerance

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stop the drug permanently and never take a tetracycline again

choices.label: D
choices.text: Take each dose at bedtime with a glass of milk

choices.label: E
choices.text: Take each dose together with calcium carbonate tablets

explanation.summary: Tetracyclines cause photosensitivity reactions, so patients are told to limit sun exposure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tetracyclines are associated with photosensitivity reactions after sunlight or ultraviolet exposure. The counseling the brick gives is to advise patients to avoid excessive sunlight while they are on the drug.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Photosensitivity is an adverse reaction, not tolerance, and raising the dose would worsen it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sun avoidance is the recommended measure; a lifelong class ban is not what the brick advises.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dairy products must be separated from dosing because they also chelate the drug.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Calcium carbonate is a cation-containing antacid that chelates tetracycline and blocks its absorption.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A patient starting tetracycline asks how to time her milk and yogurt around her doses. Based on the chelation interaction, which of the following schedules is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Avoid dairy for 1 hour before and 2 hours after each dose

choices.label: B
choices.text: Avoid dairy for 2 hours before and 1 hour after each dose

choices.label: C
choices.text: Avoid dairy for 4 hours before and 4 hours after each dose

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dairy may be taken at the same time as each dose

choices.label: E
choices.text: Dairy restrictions apply only to patients taking doxycycline

explanation.summary: Dairy products should be avoided 1 hour before and 2 hours after a tetracycline dose.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dairy products contain calcium that chelates tetracyclines and prevents their absorption. The brick specifies that milk and yogurt should be avoided 1 hour before or 2 hours after tetracycline use, which is the separation this patient needs.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The intervals are reversed; the restriction is 1 hour before and 2 hours after.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The 4-hour window belongs to the antacid and polyvalent cation rule, not to dairy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Taking dairy with the dose is exactly what causes chelation and loss of drug absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Chelation is a class effect of tetracyclines and is not limited to doxycycline.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man taking tetracycline for rosacea also chews calcium carbonate antacid tablets with every meal, including at the time of each antibiotic dose. His infection is not improving. Which of the following best explains the treatment failure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The antacid accelerates hepatic metabolism of the tetracycline

choices.label: B
choices.text: The antacid cation chelates the tetracycline and blocks its absorption

choices.label: C
choices.text: The antacid displaces the tetracycline from plasma protein binding sites

choices.label: D
choices.text: The antacid induces bacterial efflux pumps that expel the tetracycline

choices.label: E
choices.text: The antacid markedly raises renal clearance of the tetracycline

explanation.summary: Cation-containing antacids chelate tetracyclines and prevent their absorption.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antacids such as sodium bicarbonate or calcium carbonate contain cations that chelate with tetracyclines. Because the chelated drug is not absorbed, taking them together leads to subtherapeutic levels. Antacids should be dosed 1 to 2 hours before or 4 hours after the tetracycline.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antacids are not described as inducers of tetracycline metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Protein binding displacement is not the mechanism of this interaction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The interaction occurs in the gut lumen before absorption, not at bacterial efflux pumps.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Increased renal clearance is not the interaction described for antacids and tetracyclines.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman taking tetracycline for an infection uses several over-the-counter products at home. Which of the following is most likely to reduce absorption of her antibiotic through chelation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acetaminophen extended-release tablets

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bismuth subsalicylate suspension

choices.label: C
choices.text: Docusate sodium stool softener capsules

choices.label: D
choices.text: Guaifenesin expectorant syrup

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loratadine 10 mg oral tablets

explanation.summary: Bismuth subsalicylate is a polyvalent cation product that chelates tetracyclines.
explanation.whyCorrect: Along with antacids, the brick names polyvalent cations such as magnesium, iron, aluminum and zinc, multivitamins, and bismuth subsalicylate, an antidiarrheal, as agents that chelate tetracyclines. These products must be separated from the antibiotic by 1 to 2 hours before or 4 hours after the dose.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acetaminophen does not supply polyvalent cations and is not listed as a chelator.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Docusate is a stool softener and is not one of the chelating products named.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Guaifenesin is not described as interfering with tetracycline absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Loratadine is not among the cation-containing products that bind tetracyclines.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man who has taken simvastatin for years is prescribed an antibiotic for bronchitis. Ten days later he develops severe diffuse muscle pain and a markedly elevated creatine kinase. Which of the following antibiotics most likely precipitated this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clarithromycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gentamicin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Linezolid

explanation.summary: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4 and should be avoided with simvastatin and lovastatin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Macrolides are hepatically metabolized, and erythromycin and clarithromycin are both CYP3A4 substrates and inhibitors. Medications metabolized by CYP3A4 may need to be avoided, and the brick specifically says simvastatin and lovastatin should be avoided with these drugs. Rising statin levels explain the myopathy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Clindamycin is associated with diarrhea, allergy and pseudomembranous colitis, not statin toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxycycline's interactions involve chelation with cations rather than CYP3A4.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gentamicin's risks are nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity, not CYP3A4 interactions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Linezolid's key interaction is with serotonergic drugs through monoamine oxidase inhibition.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman whose warfarin dose has been stable for a year is given erythromycin for an infection, and her INR rises sharply within several days. Which of the following best explains this interaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Erythromycin blocks the renal tubular excretion of warfarin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Erythromycin directly inhibits platelet aggregation in the circulation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Erythromycin displaces warfarin from vitamin K epoxide reductase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Erythromycin inhibits CYP3A4 and reduces the metabolism of warfarin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Erythromycin substantially increases intestinal absorption of warfarin

explanation.summary: Macrolides inhibit CYP3A4, so CYP3A4-metabolized drugs such as warfarin need caution.
explanation.whyCorrect: Erythromycin and clarithromycin are CYP3A4 substrates and inhibitors. Drugs metabolized by CYP3A4 may need to be avoided or used with caution, and warfarin is named as one to use cautiously. Reduced metabolism raises warfarin exposure and pushes the INR up.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Renal excretion blockade is not the macrolide interaction the brick teaches.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Macrolides are not described as having a direct antiplatelet action.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The interaction is metabolic, not competition at vitamin K epoxide reductase.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Increased absorption of warfarin is not the described mechanism.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with heart failure is started on an oral antibiotic for pneumonia. A follow-up electrocardiogram shows a newly prolonged QT interval. Which of the following classes of antibiotics is most likely responsible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycosides

choices.label: B
choices.text: Macrolides

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oxazolidinones

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptogramins

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tetracyclines

explanation.summary: Macrolides can cause QT prolongation and must be used cautiously in cardiac disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Macrolides should be used with caution in patients with existing cardiovascular disorders because they can cause QT prolongation, a type of arrhythmia. They should also be avoided together with other agents that increase the risk of QT prolongation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aminoglycosides cause nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity, not QT prolongation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Linezolid causes bone marrow suppression, peripheral neuropathy and serotonin syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Streptogramins characteristically cause arthralgia and myalgia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tetracyclines are associated with GI upset, tooth discoloration and photosensitivity.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman with a documented history of cholestatic jaundice and persistently abnormal liver function tests requires treatment for community-acquired pneumonia. Which of the following classes of antibiotics is contraindicated in this setting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycosides

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lincosamides

choices.label: C
choices.text: Macrolides

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxazolidinones

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tetracyclines

explanation.summary: Macrolides are hepatically metabolized and are contraindicated in cholestatic jaundice or hepatic dysfunction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Macrolides are hepatically metabolized, and the brick states they are contraindicated in patients with cholestatic jaundice or hepatic dysfunction. This patient has both, so a macrolide should not be used.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aminoglycoside cautions concern renal function, the inner ear and pregnancy, not the liver.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Clindamycin's listed adverse effects are diarrhea, allergic reaction and neuromuscular blockade.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Linezolid's cautions concern marrow suppression, neuropathy and serotonergic drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tetracycline contraindications are young children, pregnancy and nursing mothers.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman treated with clindamycin for a dental abscess develops profuse watery diarrhea, abdominal cramping, and fever. Colonoscopy shows scattered yellow-white pseudomembranes on the colonic mucosa. Which of the following best explains her illness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An IgE-mediated allergic reaction to clindamycin in the bowel wall

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct toxic injury of colonocytes by clindamycin itself

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ischemic colonic injury from clindamycin-induced vasoconstriction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Osmotic diarrhea caused by unabsorbed clindamycin in the lumen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile after disruption of gut flora

explanation.summary: Pseudomembranous colitis from Clostridioides difficile overgrowth is classically attributed to clindamycin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among clindamycin's adverse effects, pseudomembranous colitis from Clostridioides difficile overgrowth is the one most often attributed to this drug. The pseudomembranes seen on colonoscopy are the classic finding of that infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clindamycin can cause allergic reactions, but these do not produce colonic pseudomembranes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Direct cytotoxic injury to colonocytes is not the mechanism described for this complication.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clindamycin is not described as causing ischemic colitis through vasoconstriction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An osmotic effect would not create pseudomembranes or fever.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 39-year-old man is about to begin clindamycin therapy. Which of the following adverse effects is specifically associated with this drug?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gray baby syndrome in newborns

choices.label: B
choices.text: Irreversible sensorineural hearing loss

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neuromuscular blockade

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serotonin syndrome with antidepressants

choices.label: E
choices.text: Yellow discoloration of the teeth

explanation.summary: Clindamycin's adverse effects are diarrhea, allergic reaction and neuromuscular blockade.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists clindamycin's adverse effects as diarrhea, allergic reaction and neuromuscular blockade, with pseudomembranous colitis from Clostridioides difficile overgrowth also frequently attributed to it. Neuromuscular blockade is the effect among the options that belongs to clindamycin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gray baby syndrome is specific to chloramphenicol.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Irreversible hearing loss is the aminoglycoside ototoxicity effect.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serotonin syndrome is the linezolid interaction with SSRIs and SNRIs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tooth discoloration is caused by tetracyclines through calcium chelation.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman taking sertraline is given linezolid for a methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infection. Several hours after the first dose she develops shivering, diarrhea, agitation, muscle rigidity, and a temperature of 39.2°C. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute dystonic reaction

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anticholinergic toxicity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Malignant hyperthermia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serotonin syndrome

explanation.summary: Linezolid combined with an SSRI can precipitate serotonin syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Linezolid is a reversible monoamine oxidase inhibitor, so co-administration with drugs that raise serotonin, such as SSRIs and SNRIs, can result in serotonin syndrome. The syndrome ranges from mild shivering and diarrhea to muscle rigidity, fever and seizures, and it typically begins within several hours of starting the new drug.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An acute dystonic reaction would produce focal muscle spasm without fever or diarrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Anticholinergic toxicity is not a described consequence of this drug combination.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Malignant hyperthermia is triggered by anesthetic agents rather than antibiotics.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome follows antipsychotic exposure, not linezolid plus an SSRI.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A pharmacist flags an order that combines linezolid with venlafaxine and recommends against the combination. Which of the following properties of linezolid underlies this warning?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It blocks presynaptic serotonin reuptake transporters directly

choices.label: B
choices.text: It induces hepatic CYP2D6 and raises venlafaxine concentrations

choices.label: C
choices.text: It inhibits the renal clearance of serotonergic drugs

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a direct agonist at postsynaptic 5-HT2A receptors

choices.label: E
choices.text: It reversibly inhibits monoamine oxidase

explanation.summary: Linezolid is a reversible monoamine oxidase inhibitor, which is why it raises serotonin levels.
explanation.whyCorrect: Monoamine oxidase normally breaks down monoamine neurotransmitters such as serotonin, so inhibiting it increases serotonin levels. Linezolid is a reversible monoamine oxidase inhibitor, and combining it with an SNRI such as venlafaxine can result in serotonin syndrome.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Reuptake transporter blockade is the mechanism of the SSRI, not of linezolid.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Linezolid's interaction is through monoamine oxidase inhibition, not CYP2D6 induction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reduced renal clearance of the antidepressant is not the described interaction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Linezolid is not described as a direct serotonin receptor agonist.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man completing a 4-week course of linezolid for osteomyelitis has a platelet count of 62,000/mm3 and a hemoglobin of 9.1 g/dL, both of which were normal before therapy. Which of the following best explains these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibody-mediated hemolysis of circulating erythrocytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Folate antagonism producing a maturation arrest in the marrow

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immune-mediated destruction of circulating platelets

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibition of mitochondrial protein synthesis in marrow cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Splenic sequestration from drug-induced portal hypertension

explanation.summary: Linezolid bone marrow suppression results from inhibition of mitochondrial protein synthesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Linezolid's adverse effects include bone marrow suppression, peripheral neuropathy and serotonin syndrome. The bone marrow suppression and the peripheral neuropathy are both due to linezolid's inhibition of mitochondrial protein synthesis, which is why they emerge with prolonged courses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hemolysis is not the mechanism given for linezolid-associated anemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Folate antagonism is not the mechanism attributed to linezolid.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The cytopenias are a direct marrow suppressive effect rather than immune platelet destruction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Linezolid is not described as causing portal hypertension or splenic sequestration.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 57-year-old woman has received prolonged oral antibiotic therapy for chronic osteomyelitis. She now reports progressive numbness and burning in both feet, and laboratory studies show a falling platelet count and hemoglobin. Which of the following antibiotics is most likely responsible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amikacin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clarithromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: E
choices.text: Linezolid

explanation.summary: Peripheral neuropathy together with marrow suppression points to linezolid.
explanation.whyCorrect: Linezolid causes both bone marrow suppression and peripheral neuropathy, and both arise from its inhibition of mitochondrial protein synthesis. The combination of distal sensory symptoms and falling blood counts during a prolonged course is therefore characteristic of linezolid.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amikacin causes nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity rather than peripheral neuropathy with cytopenias.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Clarithromycin's concerns are CYP3A4 interactions, QT prolongation and hepatic effects.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clindamycin causes diarrhea, allergic reaction, neuromuscular blockade and colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doxycycline causes GI symptoms and photosensitivity, not marrow suppression.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A hospital team is counseling a patient who is beginning a new medication that raises serotonin levels. Which of the following statements best characterizes serotonin syndrome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It develops only after several weeks of continuous therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is confined to mild symptoms such as shivering and diarrhea

choices.label: C
choices.text: It occurs only when three or more serotonergic drugs are combined

choices.label: D
choices.text: It resolves on its own and never requires medical intervention

choices.label: E
choices.text: It typically begins within hours and can be life-threatening

explanation.summary: Serotonin syndrome usually starts within hours of a new drug or dose increase and can be fatal if untreated.
explanation.whyCorrect: Serotonin syndrome is caused by excessive accumulation of serotonin, often from medications that increase serotonin levels. It typically occurs within several hours of taking a new drug or increasing the dose of an existing one, and if left untreated the severe form can be life-threatening.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Onset is typically within several hours, not after weeks of therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Symptoms range from mild shivering and diarrhea to muscle rigidity, fever and seizures.
whyWrongByChoice.C: It can occur when a serotonergic drug is combined with a single other agent such as linezolid.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Severe untreated cases can be life-threatening, so intervention may be required.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man receiving quinupristin/dalfopristin for vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium develops diffuse joint and muscle pain during therapy. Which of the following best describes this adverse effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It indicates an allergic vasculitis requiring corticosteroids

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is caused by drug-induced rhabdomyolysis of skeletal muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is rare and should prompt a search for septic arthritis

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is very common, occurring in more than 45% of patients

choices.label: E
choices.text: It reflects urate crystal deposition within the joint spaces

explanation.summary: Arthralgias and myalgias affect more than 45% of patients receiving streptogramins.
explanation.whyCorrect: Arthralgia and myalgia are the signature adverse effect of the streptogramins and are described as very common, occurring in more than 45% of patients. The cause is not known, but the association with quinupristin/dalfopristin is strong enough that the symptom is expected rather than alarming.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An allergic vasculitis is not the mechanism given for streptogramin arthralgia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Rhabdomyolysis is not the described cause of these symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The reaction is very common rather than rare, so it does not by itself suggest joint infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Crystal deposition is not offered as the explanation for this drug effect.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man is receiving quinupristin/dalfopristin and has routine laboratory studies drawn. Which of the following abnormalities occurs in roughly a third of patients treated with this drug?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elevated serum amylase with elevated lipase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hypokalemia with a metabolic alkalosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased serum creatinine with hyperbilirubinemia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neutropenia with thrombocytopenia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prolonged prothrombin time with low fibrinogen

explanation.summary: Streptogramins raise serum creatinine and bilirubin in more than a third of patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: In addition to the very common arthralgias and myalgias, streptogramins cause an increase in serum creatinine and hyperbilirubinemia in more than 33% of patients. These laboratory changes are expected enough that they are monitored during therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pancreatic enzyme elevation is not among the described streptogramin effects.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Electrolyte and acid-base disturbances are not the laboratory changes described for this class.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cytopenias belong to chloramphenicol and linezolid rather than to streptogramins.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Coagulation abnormalities are not the laboratory findings attributed to these drugs.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man treated with chloramphenicol for a severe infection develops fatigue, bruising, and recurrent fevers. Blood counts show pancytopenia, and a bone marrow biopsy shows a markedly hypocellular marrow. Which of the following adverse effects does this represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aplastic anemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cholestatic jaundice

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gray baby syndrome

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pseudomembranous colitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serotonin syndrome

explanation.summary: Chloramphenicol causes blood dyscrasias, including aplastic anemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chloramphenicol's adverse effects include blood dyscrasias such as aplastic anemia, thrombocytopenia and granulocytopenia. Its blood cell toxicity is attributed to inhibition of mitochondrial protein synthesis affecting a pathway important in maintaining iron homeostasis. A hypocellular marrow with pancytopenia is the picture of aplastic anemia.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cholestatic jaundice relates to macrolide contraindications rather than marrow toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gray baby syndrome affects newborns and presents with hypotension and cyanosis, not marrow failure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pseudomembranous colitis is a clindamycin-associated colonic infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serotonin syndrome is a linezolid interaction and does not cause pancytopenia.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A premature neonate being treated with chloramphenicol develops vomiting, an ashen gray color, hypotension, and cyanosis over 24 hours. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Congenital cyanotic heart disease

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gray baby syndrome

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kernicterus from unconjugated bilirubin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Methemoglobinemia from a topical anesthetic

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neonatal sepsis with septic shock

explanation.summary: Gray baby syndrome is a potentially fatal chloramphenicol reaction presenting with hypotension and cyanosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gray baby syndrome is specific to chloramphenicol and occurs in newborns, especially premature infants. It is potentially fatal and characteristically presents with hypotension and cyanosis, matching this neonate's course during chloramphenicol therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Congenital heart disease would not appear abruptly after starting an antibiotic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Kernicterus reflects bilirubin deposition in the brain rather than this drug reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methemoglobinemia is not the chloramphenicol reaction described in the brick.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Septic shock would not be the expected explanation in an infant already receiving the drug that causes this syndrome.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: An attending explains why newborns, and premature infants in particular, are uniquely vulnerable to gray baby syndrome. Which of the following best accounts for this susceptibility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Their blood-brain barrier allows greater drug penetration

choices.label: B
choices.text: Their hemoglobin binds the drug with unusually high affinity

choices.label: C
choices.text: They absorb the drug far more completely from the gut

choices.label: D
choices.text: They lack the renal mass needed to excrete the drug

choices.label: E
choices.text: They lack UDP-glucuronosyltransferase to metabolize the drug

explanation.summary: Gray baby syndrome is due to a newborn's lack of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase, which metabolizes chloramphenicol.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gray baby syndrome is attributed to a newborn's lack of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase, and the deficiency is most pronounced in prematurity. Without that enzyme the infant cannot metabolize chloramphenicol, the drug accumulates, and the potentially fatal syndrome of hypotension and cyanosis follows.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blood-brain barrier permeability is not the described basis of the syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemoglobin binding of chloramphenicol is not the mechanism described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Enhanced gastrointestinal absorption is not the explanation given.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The brick attributes the syndrome to a metabolic enzyme deficiency, not to renal immaturity.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 17-year-old girl with severe pustular acne is about to start oral tetracycline. Which of the following is the most appropriate step before beginning therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Obtain a baseline audiogram

choices.label: B
choices.text: Obtain a baseline electrocardiogram

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obtain a baseline platelet count

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obtain a baseline serum creatinine

choices.label: E
choices.text: Obtain a urine pregnancy test

explanation.summary: A pregnancy test is checked before starting tetracycline in a woman of childbearing age because the drug harms a fetus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tetracycline chelation can cause fetal harm, so the drug is contraindicated in pregnancy. The counseling in this brick's case states that a urine pregnancy test is checked before starting tetracycline in all women of childbearing age, because the medicine would have effects on a growing fetus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Baseline hearing testing is relevant to the ototoxic aminoglycosides, not tetracyclines.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An electrocardiogram addresses the QT prolongation risk of macrolides.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Platelet monitoring fits linezolid or chloramphenicol marrow toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Creatinine monitoring fits aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity rather than tetracycline use.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors–2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman presents with 2 days of dysuria, urinary frequency, urgency, and a sensation of incomplete bladder emptying. She is afebrile, and examination shows mild suprapubic tenderness without costovertebral angle tenderness. A urine culture is obtained before empiric therapy is begun. Which of the following organisms is most likely to be recovered?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterococcus faecalis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Escherichia coli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Klebsiella pneumoniae

choices.label: D
choices.text: Proteus mirabilis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Staphylococcus saprophyticus

explanation.summary: Acute cystitis is primarily caused by Escherichia coli.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute cystitis is an infection of the lower urinary tract, and it is primarily caused by Escherichia coli. E. coli is a gram-negative rod of the Enterobacteriaceae family, the group that typically causes urinary tract infections. Her afebrile presentation with suprapubic tenderness and no costovertebral angle tenderness is the classic lower-tract picture.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterococci can cause acute cystitis but account for a minority of cases compared with E. coli.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Klebsiella is listed among the other organisms that can cause acute cystitis, not the most likely one.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Proteus is also an occasional cause of acute cystitis but is not the predominant pathogen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Staphylococcus saprophyticus is a recognized cause of acute cystitis but is far less common than E. coli.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with lobar pneumonia is started on ciprofloxacin. Sputum culture grows Streptococcus pneumoniae, and after 3 days he remains febrile with worsening hypoxemia. Which of the following best explains his poor response to therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin has limited coverage of gram-positive bacteria

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin has no activity against Klebsiella or Proteus species

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin is active only against anaerobic organisms

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin is effective only when given as a topical preparation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin lacks activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa

explanation.summary: Ciprofloxacin has limited coverage of gram-positive organisms such as S. pneumoniae and S. aureus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although fluoroquinolones are broad-spectrum agents, ciprofloxacin's strength is aerobic gram-negative bacilli. Its coverage of gram-positive bacteria, specifically S. pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus, is limited, so pneumococcal pneumonia is a predictable treatment failure. Levofloxacin and moxifloxacin are the fluoroquinolones that cover the common respiratory pathogens.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ciprofloxacin has excellent activity against Klebsiella and Proteus species.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ciprofloxacin is not restricted to anaerobes; it is a broad-spectrum agent with strong aerobic gram-negative activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ciprofloxacin is used systemically; topical formulation is not the issue here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ciprofloxacin does have activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, so this is not the explanation.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman is being treated for community-acquired pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae when she also develops dysuria and urinary frequency. The team wants a single fluoroquinolone that covers the common respiratory pathogens and also reaches effective concentrations in the urine. Which of the following agents best meets both requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Levofloxacin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Linezolid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Moxifloxacin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Levofloxacin covers the common respiratory pathogens and can also be used for urinary tract infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Levofloxacin has activity against both gram-positive and gram-negative pathogens and is active against the common respiratory pathogens S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, and M. catarrhalis. It is also one of the fluoroquinolones that can be used to treat urinary tract infections, making it the single agent that satisfies both needs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ciprofloxacin has limited gram-positive coverage and would not reliably treat S. pneumoniae pneumonia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Linezolid is used for MRSA coverage and is not a fluoroquinolone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Moxifloxacin covers respiratory pathogens but is not renally eliminated and does not concentrate in the urine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin is used for MRSA coverage and is not a fluoroquinolone.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man has a polymicrobial intra-abdominal infection involving both gram-positive and gram-negative organisms. The team wants a fluoroquinolone whose enhanced gram-positive activity makes it useful in this setting. Which of the following is the most appropriate choice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Levofloxacin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Linezolid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Moxifloxacin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Moxifloxacin has enhanced gram-positive activity, making it effective for polymicrobial infections such as intra-abdominal infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Moxifloxacin's spectrum is similar to that of levofloxacin, but it has enhanced gram-positive activity. That added gram-positive potency is what makes moxifloxacin effective against polymicrobial infections such as intra-abdominal infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ciprofloxacin has limited gram-positive coverage, so it does not fit the description of enhanced gram-positive activity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Levofloxacin covers gram-positive and gram-negative pathogens but does not have the enhanced gram-positive activity attributed to moxifloxacin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Linezolid is not a fluoroquinolone; it is used for MRSA coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin is not a fluoroquinolone; it is used for MRSA coverage.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A resident proposes moxifloxacin for a patient with an uncomplicated urinary tract infection. The attending explains that moxifloxacin is a poor choice for this indication. Which of the following best supports the attending's reasoning?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It cannot be administered by the oral route to adults

choices.label: B
choices.text: It has no activity against any aerobic gram-negative bacilli

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is chemically inactivated by the acidic pH of the urine

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is contraindicated in every patient older than 60 years

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is not renally eliminated and does not concentrate in the urine

explanation.summary: Moxifloxacin is not used for UTIs because it is not renally eliminated and does not concentrate in the urine.
explanation.whyCorrect: Moxifloxacin is not typically used to treat urinary tract infections because it is not renally eliminated and does not concentrate in the urine. As a result it never reaches levels in the urinary tract sufficient to kill the infecting bacteria, regardless of how susceptible they look in vitro.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Route of administration is not the limitation; the limitation is lack of urinary concentration.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Moxifloxacin does have gram-negative activity, including activity against P. aeruginosa; the problem is drug delivery to the urine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Urinary pH inactivation is not the reason given for avoiding moxifloxacin in UTIs.
