whyWrongByChoice.D: Age over 60 raises the risk of tendon rupture with fluoroquinolones but is not an absolute contraindication and is unrelated to UTI efficacy.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man who began levofloxacin 5 days ago for pneumonia reports new pain and swelling just above the right heel that worsens with walking. Which of the following fluoroquinolone adverse effects best explains his symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Photosensitivity

choices.label: B
choices.text: QTc prolongation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Red-man syndrome

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sulfa hypersensitivity

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tendon rupture

explanation.summary: Fluoroquinolones cause tendon rupture, a risk that increases in patients older than 60 years.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tendon injury and rupture are well-described fluoroquinolone adverse effects, and the risk increases with age greater than 60. Pain and swelling over the Achilles region in a 68-year-old man started on levofloxacin is the classic presentation of this complication.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Photosensitivity produces an exaggerated sunburn reaction on sun-exposed skin, not focal heel pain.
whyWrongByChoice.B: QTc prolongation is an electrocardiographic effect and does not cause localized tendon pain.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Red-man syndrome is associated with vancomycin, not with the fluoroquinolones.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sulfa hypersensitivity follows sulfonamide exposure and typically presents as a skin reaction.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman with pneumonia is already taking a medication known to lengthen the QT interval. Her physician is reluctant to add a fluoroquinolone to her regimen. Which fluoroquinolone-associated risk is the physician most concerned about?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Photosensitivity

choices.label: B
choices.text: QTc prolongation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Red-man syndrome

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tendon rupture

choices.label: E
choices.text: Teratogenic fetal effects

explanation.summary: Fluoroquinolones prolong the QTc and should be avoided when the risk of further QT lengthening is high.
explanation.whyCorrect: The use of fluoroquinolones is associated with QTc prolongation, so these agents should be avoided when there is already a risk of increasing the QT interval. Adding a fluoroquinolone to another QT-prolonging drug compounds that risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Photosensitivity is a skin reaction to sun exposure and has no electrocardiographic consequence.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Red-man syndrome is a vancomycin infusion reaction, not a fluoroquinolone effect.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tendon rupture is a genuine fluoroquinolone risk but is unrelated to the QT interval.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Teratogenicity is a concern in pregnancy and is not relevant to a QT-prolonging co-medication.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman who is 10 weeks pregnant is diagnosed with acute cystitis. Her physician specifically avoids prescribing ciprofloxacin. Which property of the fluoroquinolones explains this decision?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are eliminated exclusively by hepatic metabolism

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are teratogenic and should be avoided in pregnancy

choices.label: C
choices.text: They cannot be absorbed from the gut during pregnancy

choices.label: D
choices.text: They cause flushing and rash when infused rapidly

choices.label: E
choices.text: They have no activity against Escherichia coli

explanation.summary: Fluoroquinolones are teratogenic and should be avoided in pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fluoroquinolones are teratogenic, so they should be avoided in pregnant patients. For a pregnant woman with acute cystitis another class must be selected even though the fluoroquinolones would otherwise cover the likely uropathogens.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Elimination route is the issue for moxifloxacin in UTIs, not the reason to avoid fluoroquinolones in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Impaired absorption in pregnancy is not the stated reason to avoid these drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Flushing and rash during rapid infusion describe red-man syndrome, which is caused by vancomycin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fluoroquinolones such as ciprofloxacin cover E. coli very well; efficacy is not the problem.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman taking ciprofloxacin for a urinary tract infection spends an afternoon outdoors and develops an exaggerated sunburn-like erythema over sun-exposed skin. Which adverse effect of the fluoroquinolones does this represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Photosensitivity

choices.label: B
choices.text: QTc prolongation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Red-man syndrome

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tendon rupture

choices.label: E
choices.text: Teratogenicity

explanation.summary: Fluoroquinolones can cause photosensitivity reactions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Photosensitivity is a recognized fluoroquinolone adverse effect. Patients develop an exaggerated sunburn-type reaction on sun-exposed skin, which is exactly what this patient describes after an afternoon outdoors on ciprofloxacin.

whyWrongByChoice.B: QTc prolongation is detected on electrocardiogram and produces no skin findings.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Red-man syndrome follows rapid vancomycin infusion, not sun exposure on a fluoroquinolone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tendon rupture presents with focal tendon pain and swelling, not a sun-distributed rash.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Teratogenicity refers to fetal harm and is not a cutaneous reaction in the patient.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: During a rapid intravenous antibiotic infusion, a patient develops flushing and an erythematous rash over the face and upper torso. Which of the following drugs is classically responsible for this reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Levofloxacin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Moxifloxacin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Red-man syndrome is associated with vancomycin, not with the fluoroquinolones.
explanation.whyCorrect: Flushing with an erythematous rash during a rapid infusion is red-man syndrome, which is associated with the use of vancomycin. It is specifically not a fluoroquinolone adverse effect, a point the brick makes when listing fluoroquinolone warnings.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ciprofloxacin causes QTc prolongation, tendon rupture, and photosensitivity, but not red-man syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Levofloxacin shares the fluoroquinolone class warnings and is not linked to red-man syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Moxifloxacin shares the fluoroquinolone class warnings and is not linked to red-man syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim causes hypersensitivity skin reactions but not infusion-related red-man syndrome.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman with no drug allergies is diagnosed with acute uncomplicated cystitis. Which of the following is the usual first-line antibiotic for this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intravenous cefepime every 8 hours

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intravenous piperacillin/tazobactam

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intravenous vancomycin or linezolid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral moxifloxacin 400 mg daily

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim

explanation.summary: First-line treatment of an uncomplicated UTI is often sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute cystitis is treated with antibiotics, and first-line therapy is often sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim. The combination covers the usual uropathogens, including E. coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Proteus mirabilis. Fluoroquinolones such as ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin are alternatives.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cefepime is used when gram-negative and pseudomonal coverage is needed, not for uncomplicated cystitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Piperacillin/tazobactam is reserved for gram-negative and pseudomonal coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vancomycin and linezolid are used for MRSA coverage rather than for routine cystitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Moxifloxacin does not concentrate in the urine and is not used for urinary tract infections.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A team is reviewing the gram-positive spectrum of sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim before selecting therapy. Which of the following organisms lies within that spectrum?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterococcus faecalis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Group A Streptococcus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus epidermidis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae

explanation.summary: Sulfonamide gram-positive coverage includes Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfonamides cover some gram-positive bacteria, and the organisms named are Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis. Staphylococcus epidermidis therefore falls squarely inside the documented sulfonamide gram-positive spectrum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterococcus faecalis is not among the gram-positive organisms covered by the sulfonamides.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Group A Streptococcus is treated with agents such as ampicillin/sulbactam, not with sulfonamides.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MRSA requires vancomycin or linezolid rather than a sulfonamide.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus pneumoniae is not listed within the sulfonamide gram-positive spectrum.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A patient with a urinary tract infection improves on sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim, and the culture later grows an organism that is susceptible. Which of the following organisms is consistent with the documented spectrum of this agent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterococcus faecalis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Group A Streptococcus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Proteus mirabilis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pseudomonas aeruginosa

explanation.summary: Sulfonamides cover gram-negative organisms including E. coli, K. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, and P. mirabilis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The gram-negative spectrum of the sulfonamides includes Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Proteus mirabilis. Because Proteus mirabilis is a recognized uropathogen inside that spectrum, it fits both the infection and the drug chosen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterococcus faecalis is not listed among the organisms sulfonamides reliably cover.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Group A Streptococcus is not part of the documented sulfonamide spectrum.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MRSA is outside the sulfonamide spectrum and is treated with vancomycin or linezolid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pseudomonas aeruginosa requires antipseudomonal agents such as cefepime, piperacillin/tazobactam, or a carbapenem other than ertapenem.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A patient with partial-thickness burns is prescribed a topical antimicrobial to treat the burn wound. Topical agents from which of the following drug classes are used for this indication?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Carbapenems

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fluoroquinolones

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycopeptides

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oxazolidinones

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sulfonamides

explanation.summary: Topical sulfonamides are used to treat burns.
explanation.whyCorrect: In addition to their systemic uses, topical sulfonamides are applied to treat burns. This topical role persists even though the systemic usefulness of the sulfonamides has declined with rising bacterial resistance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Carbapenems are parenteral agents used for broad gram-positive and gram-negative coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fluoroquinolones are used systemically for respiratory, intra-abdominal, and urinary infections, not as burn wound topicals.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glycopeptides such as vancomycin are used for MRSA coverage rather than topical burn care.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oxazolidinones such as linezolid are used for MRSA coverage rather than topical burn care.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 9-year-old boy has purulent discharge and conjunctival injection of the right eye and is prescribed topical sulfonamide drops. This treatment is directed at which of the following conditions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute cystitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bacterial conjunctivitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Community-acquired pneumonia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intra-abdominal infection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Methicillin-resistant S. aureus bacteremia

explanation.summary: Topical sulfonamides are used to treat bacterial conjunctivitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Topical sulfonamides have two classic uses: burns and bacterial conjunctivitis. Purulent ocular discharge with conjunctival injection treated by sulfonamide eye drops is the conjunctivitis indication.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acute cystitis is treated with systemic agents such as sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim, not topical drops.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pneumonia is treated systemically with agents such as levofloxacin or moxifloxacin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Intra-abdominal infection requires systemic therapy such as moxifloxacin or a carbapenem.
whyWrongByChoice.E: MRSA bacteremia requires intravenous vancomycin or linezolid.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: An attending notes that sulfonamides were once used far more widely than they are today. Which of the following best explains the decline in their clinical usefulness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacterial resistance to these agents has emerged over time

choices.label: B
choices.text: They can no longer be produced in topical formulations

choices.label: C
choices.text: They lost all gram-negative activity when reformulated

choices.label: D
choices.text: They were replaced because they cannot be given orally

choices.label: E
choices.text: They were withdrawn because of universal hepatotoxicity

explanation.summary: The clinical usefulness of sulfonamides has decreased because of emerging bacterial resistance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfonamides still cover a range of gram-positive and gram-negative organisms, but their clinical usefulness has decreased over time due to the emergence of bacterial resistance. Resistance, not a change in formulation or toxicity profile, is what narrowed their role.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Topical sulfonamides remain in use for burns and bacterial conjunctivitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sulfonamides retain gram-negative activity against organisms such as E. coli and P. mirabilis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim is commonly given orally, including as first-line UTI therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Universal hepatotoxicity is not the stated reason for their reduced use.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Beyond their antibacterial spectrum, sulfonamides also have activity against certain protozoal organisms. Which of the following is such an organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Candida albicans

choices.label: B
choices.text: Klebsiella pneumoniae

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pseudomonas aeruginosa

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus epidermidis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Toxoplasma gondii

explanation.summary: Sulfonamides are active against certain protozoa, including Toxoplasma gondii.
explanation.whyCorrect: In addition to gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, sulfonamides are active against certain protozoal species such as Toxoplasma gondii. This broadens their role beyond the strictly antibacterial indications.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Candida albicans is a fungus and is not the protozoal organism covered by sulfonamides.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a gram-negative bacterium covered by sulfonamides, but it is not a protozoan.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a gram-negative bacterium and lies outside the sulfonamide spectrum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Staphylococcus epidermidis is a gram-positive bacterium covered by sulfonamides, but it is not a protozoan.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A blood culture from a hospitalized patient grows methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. Which of the following provides appropriate coverage for this organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ampicillin/sulbactam

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ceftriaxone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ertapenem

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin or linezolid

explanation.summary: MRSA coverage is provided by vancomycin or linezolid.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the regimens tabulated in this brick, MRSA is the one pathogen category matched specifically to vancomycin and linezolid. The other listed agents are assigned to non-MRSA gram-positive, gram-negative, or pseudomonal coverage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ampicillin/sulbactam covers non-MRSA gram-positive organisms such as MSSA and Group A Streptococcus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ceftriaxone is used for gram-negative coverage and does not cover MRSA.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ciprofloxacin has limited gram-positive coverage and does not treat MRSA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ertapenem is used for non-MRSA gram-positive and gram-negative coverage.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A patient has a soft-tissue infection caused by methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus together with Group A Streptococcus. Which of the following agents provides appropriate coverage for this combination?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ampicillin/sulbactam

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cefepime

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ceftriaxone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Piperacillin/tazobactam

explanation.summary: Non-MRSA gram-positive organisms are covered by ampicillin/sulbactam or ertapenem.
explanation.whyCorrect: Non-MRSA gram-positive pathogens, specifically S. aureus, Group A Streptococcus, and S. epidermidis, are matched with ampicillin/sulbactam or ertapenem for good gram-positive coverage. Ampicillin/sulbactam is therefore the correct choice among these options.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cefepime is selected for gram-negative and pseudomonal coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ceftriaxone provides gram-negative coverage without antipseudomonal activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ciprofloxacin has limited gram-positive coverage and is aimed at aerobic gram-negative bacilli.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Piperacillin/tazobactam is used when gram-negative and pseudomonal coverage is required.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A neutropenic patient develops a bloodstream infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Which of the following agents provides reliable antipseudomonal coverage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ampicillin/sulbactam

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cefepime

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ceftriaxone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ertapenem

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Pseudomonas requires cefepime, piperacillin/tazobactam, or a carbapenem other than ertapenem.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antipseudomonal regimens include cefepime, piperacillin/tazobactam, and the carbapenems with the explicit exception of ertapenem. Cefepime provides gram-negative plus pseudomonal coverage and is the appropriate choice here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ampicillin/sulbactam is directed at non-MRSA gram-positive organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ceftriaxone gives gram-negative coverage but specifically no pseudomonal coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ertapenem is the carbapenem excluded from the antipseudomonal group.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin is used for MRSA coverage and has no gram-negative activity.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A patient has a culture-confirmed Pseudomonas aeruginosa wound infection, and the team reviews the available agents. Which of the following lacks activity against this organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cefepime

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ertapenem

choices.label: D
choices.text: Levofloxacin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Piperacillin/tazobactam

explanation.summary: Ertapenem is the carbapenem that does not provide pseudomonal coverage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pseudomonal coverage comes from cefepime, piperacillin/tazobactam, and the carbapenems except ertapenem. Ertapenem is singled out as the carbapenem that does not cover Pseudomonas, so it is the wrong agent for this infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cefepime provides gram-negative and pseudomonal coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ciprofloxacin has documented activity against P. aeruginosa.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Levofloxacin has documented activity against P. aeruginosa.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Piperacillin/tazobactam is an antipseudomonal agent.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A patient with gram-negative bacteremia is started on ceftriaxone. Which of the following best describes a limitation of this agent's spectrum?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It does not cover any gram-negative rods

choices.label: B
choices.text: It does not cover Escherichia coli

choices.label: C
choices.text: It does not cover Klebsiella pneumoniae

choices.label: D
choices.text: It does not cover Proteus mirabilis

choices.label: E
choices.text: It does not cover Pseudomonas aeruginosa

explanation.summary: Ceftriaxone gives gram-negative coverage but no pseudomonal coverage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ceftriaxone is listed as an option for gram-negative organisms such as E. coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Proteus mirabilis, with the explicit caveat that it provides no pseudomonal coverage. If Pseudomonas is suspected, an antipseudomonal agent must replace it.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftriaxone is specifically valued for its gram-negative coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ceftriaxone is an appropriate option for E. coli.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ceftriaxone is an appropriate option for Klebsiella pneumoniae.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ceftriaxone is an appropriate option for Proteus mirabilis.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman with acute cystitis reports major hives after fluoroquinolones and a severe skin reaction to sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim. She is afebrile with normal vital signs, mild suprapubic tenderness, and no costovertebral angle tenderness. Which of the following is the most appropriate empiric therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cephalexin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Levofloxacin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Moxifloxacin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim

explanation.summary: With both a sulfa allergy and a fluoroquinolone allergy, a beta-lactam such as cephalexin or amoxicillin/clavulanate is the option.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim would normally be considered for empiric therapy of acute cystitis, but this patient has a sulfa allergy, and her hives rule out the fluoroquinolone class. Beta-lactams such as amoxicillin/clavulanate or cephalexin are the good options to consider in this situation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone, and she develops major hives with this class.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Levofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone and carries the same allergy risk for her.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Moxifloxacin is both a fluoroquinolone and an agent that does not concentrate in the urine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim caused a severe skin reaction and must be avoided.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman has 2 days of dysuria and urinary frequency. She is afebrile, her vital signs are normal, and she has mild suprapubic tenderness but no costovertebral angle tenderness. Which of the following findings most supports an infection confined to the lower urinary tract?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A sensation of incomplete bladder emptying

choices.label: B
choices.text: Absence of fever and costovertebral angle tenderness

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dysuria of two days' duration

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased urinary frequency with urgency

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mild lower abdominal discomfort

explanation.summary: Normal vital signs with no fever and no costovertebral angle tenderness indicate no systemic or upper-tract involvement.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute cystitis is an infection of the lower urinary tract. The physical examination that supports this localization is the absence of systemic infection signs, meaning normal vital signs, no fever, and no costovertebral angle tenderness. That combination is what allows empiric outpatient therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Incomplete bladder emptying is a bladder symptom that does not rule out kidney involvement.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dysuria is a lower-tract symptom but is also present when infection ascends.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Frequency and urgency occur in cystitis but persist when the upper tract is also infected.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mild lower abdominal discomfort accompanies cystitis but does not exclude upper-tract disease.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A woman with signs and symptoms of acute cystitis is evaluated in clinic. Her physician sends a urine culture and at the same visit begins an antibiotic. Which of the following best describes the role of that culture?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It confirms the pathogen after empiric therapy has been started

choices.label: B
choices.text: It establishes whether the patient has a sulfa allergy

choices.label: C
choices.text: It measures the urinary concentration of the antibiotic

choices.label: D
choices.text: It must return before any antibiotic can be prescribed

choices.label: E
choices.text: It removes the need for antibiotic therapy in cystitis

explanation.summary: Urine cultures confirm the causative pathogen while empiric therapy is already underway.
explanation.whyCorrect: In acute cystitis, urine cultures confirm the pathogen causing the infection, but treatment does not wait for them. Empiric therapy is initiated based on the clinical assessment and prior culture results, and the new culture then confirms or redirects that choice.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Drug allergy is established from the patient's history, not from a urine culture.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A urine culture identifies organisms; it does not assay drug levels in urine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Empiric therapy is started before the culture result returns.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Treatment for acute cystitis typically involves antibiotics; the culture does not replace them.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A student is asked which group of organisms most commonly causes urinary tract infections. Which of the following is the best answer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acid-fast bacilli of the Mycobacterium group

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anaerobic gram-positive rods of the gut flora

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram-negative rods of the Enterobacteriaceae family

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gram-positive cocci of the Staphylococcus group

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spiral organisms of the spirochete group

explanation.summary: Urinary tract infections are typically caused by gram-negative rods of the Enterobacteriaceae family.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute cystitis is usually the result of a urinary tract infection, and those infections are typically caused by gram-negative rods of the Enterobacteriaceae family. E. coli, Klebsiella, and Proteus are the members most often implicated, which is why empiric regimens target gram-negative organisms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acid-fast bacilli are not the typical cause of acute cystitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Anaerobic gram-positive rods are not the organisms typically responsible for urinary infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Staphylococcus saprophyticus can cause cystitis, but staphylococci are not the usual cause of UTIs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Spirochetes are not among the organisms that typically cause urinary tract infection.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A patient is being treated with ciprofloxacin. Which of the following organisms lies within its spectrum of activity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Group A Streptococcus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pseudomonas aeruginosa

choices.label: D
choices.text: Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae

explanation.summary: Ciprofloxacin has activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa but limited gram-positive coverage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ciprofloxacin's strength is aerobic gram-negative bacilli, and its spectrum explicitly includes Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Its gram-positive coverage, by contrast, is limited, which is why gram-positive pathogens are poor targets for this drug.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Group A Streptococcus is covered by agents such as ampicillin/sulbactam rather than ciprofloxacin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: MRSA requires vancomycin or linezolid, not a fluoroquinolone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Staphylococcus aureus is named as an organism ciprofloxacin covers poorly.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus pneumoniae is named as an organism ciprofloxacin covers poorly.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Ciprofloxacin's potent activity against Escherichia coli, Klebsiella species, and Proteus species makes it a good option for which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intra-abdominal and urinary tract infections

choices.label: B
choices.text: Methicillin-resistant S. aureus bacteremia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pneumococcal community-acquired pneumonia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Topical therapy of bacterial conjunctivitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topical treatment of partial-thickness burns

explanation.summary: Ciprofloxacin's gram-negative bacillary coverage makes it a good option for intra-abdominal and urinary tract infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ciprofloxacin has the greatest activity of the fluoroquinolones against aerobic gram-negative bacilli, including E. coli, Klebsiella species, and Proteus species. Because those organisms dominate at these sites, ciprofloxacin is a good option for intra-abdominal infections and urinary tract infections.

whyWrongByChoice.B: MRSA bacteremia requires vancomycin or linezolid, not a fluoroquinolone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pneumococcal pneumonia is poorly treated by ciprofloxacin because of its limited gram-positive coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bacterial conjunctivitis is the classic indication for a topical sulfonamide preparation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Burn wounds are treated with topical sulfonamides rather than systemic ciprofloxacin.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: In addition to its activity against aerobic gram-negative bacilli, ciprofloxacin has potent activity against which of the following pairs of organisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Group A Streptococcus and Enterococcus faecalis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Haemophilus influenzae and Moraxella catarrhalis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Methicillin-resistant S. aureus and S. epidermidis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae and Staphylococcus epidermidis

explanation.summary: Ciprofloxacin has potent activity against Haemophilus influenzae and Moraxella catarrhalis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beyond E. coli, Klebsiella, and Proteus, ciprofloxacin also has potent activity against Haemophilus influenzae and Moraxella catarrhalis. These gram-negative respiratory organisms sit within its spectrum even though the gram-positive respiratory pathogen S. pneumoniae does not.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Group A Streptococcus and enterococci are gram-positive organisms treated with other agents.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MRSA and S. epidermidis are gram-positive organisms outside ciprofloxacin's effective range.
whyWrongByChoice.D: S. pneumoniae and S. aureus are the gram-positive organisms ciprofloxacin covers only poorly.
whyWrongByChoice.E: S. pneumoniae and S. epidermidis are gram-positive organisms not reliably covered by ciprofloxacin.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A pharmacology lecture describes the fluoroquinolones as broad-spectrum antibiotics. Which of the following best characterizes the overall spectrum of this class?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anaerobes and mycobacterial species only

choices.label: B
choices.text: Atypical pathogens and protozoa only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram-negative organisms and fungi only

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gram-positive organisms and anaerobes only

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gram-positive, gram-negative, and atypical pathogens

explanation.summary: Fluoroquinolones are broad-spectrum agents active against gram-positive, gram-negative, and atypical pathogens.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fluoroquinolones are broad-spectrum antibiotics with activity against gram-positive, gram-negative, and atypical pathogens. Within that shared class spectrum there are very specific distinctions among ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, and moxifloxacin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Limiting the class to anaerobes and mycobacteria misstates its broad aerobic spectrum.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Protozoal coverage is a feature of the sulfonamides, not a defining fluoroquinolone property.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fluoroquinolones are antibacterial agents and are not antifungal drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Restricting the class to gram-positives and anaerobes ignores its strong gram-negative activity.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Five patients are about to begin levofloxacin therapy. Which of the following patients is at greatest risk for fluoroquinolone-associated tendon rupture?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 19-year-old man with acute bacterial cystitis

choices.label: B
choices.text: A 24-year-old woman taking oral contraceptives

choices.label: C
choices.text: A 35-year-old man with a known sulfa allergy

choices.label: D
choices.text: A 40-year-old woman with fair, sun-sensitive skin

choices.label: E
choices.text: A 72-year-old man with lobar pneumonia

explanation.summary: The risk of fluoroquinolone tendon rupture increases with age greater than 60 years.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tendon rupture is a recognized fluoroquinolone adverse effect, and the risk rises specifically in patients older than 60. Of these patients, only the 72-year-old man falls into that higher-risk age group.

whyWrongByChoice.A: At 19 years of age this patient is well below the age threshold that increases tendon risk.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Oral contraceptive use is not identified as a risk factor for fluoroquinolone tendon injury.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A sulfa allergy matters when choosing sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim, not for tendon risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sun-sensitive skin raises concern for photosensitivity, a different adverse effect.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A patient has a bloodstream infection caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae, and the team wants a single agent that supplies good gram-positive as well as gram-negative coverage. Which of the following best fits that description?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ampicillin/sulbactam

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cefepime

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ceftriaxone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ertapenem

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Ertapenem supplies good gram-positive and gram-negative coverage for organisms such as E. coli, K. pneumoniae, and P. mirabilis.
explanation.whyCorrect: For gram-negative organisms such as E. coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Proteus mirabilis, ertapenem together with levofloxacin or moxifloxacin is listed as providing good gram-positive and gram-negative coverage. Ertapenem is the only option here carrying that dual designation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ampicillin/sulbactam is designated for good gram-positive coverage of non-MRSA organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cefepime is designated for gram-negative and pseudomonal coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ceftriaxone is designated as gram-negative coverage without pseudomonal activity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin is designated for MRSA coverage and lacks gram-negative activity.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Besides Escherichia coli, which of the following organisms is a recognized cause of acute cystitis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Haemophilus influenzae

choices.label: B
choices.text: Moraxella catarrhalis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Staphylococcus saprophyticus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Toxoplasma gondii

explanation.summary: Other causes of acute cystitis include Klebsiella, Proteus, Enterococci, and Staphylococcus saprophyticus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute cystitis is primarily caused by E. coli, but the other pathogens that cause it are Klebsiella, Proteus, Enterococci, and Staphylococcus saprophyticus. Staphylococcus saprophyticus is therefore the organism on this list that belongs to the cystitis group.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Haemophilus influenzae is a respiratory pathogen and is not a listed cystitis organism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Moraxella catarrhalis is a respiratory pathogen targeted by the fluoroquinolones.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a respiratory pathogen, not a listed cause of acute cystitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Toxoplasma gondii is a protozoan covered by sulfonamides, not a cause of cystitis.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with acute cystitis reports a severe rash after sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim in the past but has tolerated other antibiotic classes without difficulty. Which of the following is an appropriate alternative for her urinary tract infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A topical sulfonamide preparation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Linezolid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Moxifloxacin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: When sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim cannot be used, fluoroquinolones such as ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin can treat a UTI.
explanation.whyCorrect: First-line treatment of a UTI is often sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim, but fluoroquinolones such as ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin can also be used. Ciprofloxacin additionally has the greatest activity against the aerobic gram-negative bacilli that cause cystitis, and she has no fluoroquinolone allergy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Topical sulfonamides are used for burns and conjunctivitis, and she reacts to sulfonamides.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Linezolid provides MRSA coverage and is not an agent for uncomplicated cystitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Moxifloxacin is not renally eliminated and does not concentrate in the urine, so it is not used for UTIs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin provides MRSA coverage and is not an agent for uncomplicated cystitis.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A young woman completing treatment for acute cystitis asks what she can do to reduce the chance of worsening symptoms and future urinary tract infections. Which of the following is the most appropriate advice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask for a drug that previously caused her hives

choices.label: B
choices.text: Avoid all sunlight exposure for one year afterward

choices.label: C
choices.text: Finish the full antibiotic course and avoid irritants

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stop the antibiotic as soon as her dysuria resolves

choices.label: E
choices.text: Take a topical sulfonamide preparation by mouth

explanation.summary: Patients treated for cystitis should complete the full antibiotic course and avoid irritants.
explanation.whyCorrect: After empiric therapy is begun for acute cystitis, the counseling point is that the patient should complete the full course of antibiotics and avoid irritants in order to prevent exacerbation of symptoms and future urinary tract infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A drug that caused hives represents a major allergy and must be avoided entirely.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Photosensitivity precautions apply while taking a fluoroquinolone, not for a year afterward.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stopping early when symptoms improve is the opposite of completing the full antibiotic course.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Topical sulfonamides are applied to burns or the eye and are not taken orally.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly contrasts two fluoroquinolones?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin covers Pseudomonas aeruginosa, while levofloxacin has no antipseudomonal activity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin has enhanced gram-positive activity, while moxifloxacin is limited to gram-negative bacilli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin is best against aerobic gram-negative bacilli, while moxifloxacin has enhanced gram-positive activity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Levofloxacin lacks respiratory pathogen activity, while ciprofloxacin covers those organisms best

choices.label: E
choices.text: Moxifloxacin concentrates in the urine, while ciprofloxacin fails to reach the urinary tract

explanation.summary: Ciprofloxacin is strongest against aerobic gram-negative bacilli, whereas moxifloxacin has enhanced gram-positive activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: The key contrast within the class is that ciprofloxacin is most effective against aerobic gram-negative bacilli, while moxifloxacin has enhanced gram-positive activity that makes it useful in polymicrobial infections. Both distinctions sit inside a shared broad-spectrum class profile.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Levofloxacin does have activity against P. aeruginosa, so the contrast is false.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This reverses the two agents; the enhanced gram-positive activity belongs to moxifloxacin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Levofloxacin is active against the common respiratory pathogens, and ciprofloxacin covers S. pneumoniae poorly.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Moxifloxacin is the agent that does not concentrate in the urine, whereas ciprofloxacin treats UTIs well.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–3 Fluoroquinolones and Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A medical historian describes the antimicrobial class that first made systemic antibacterial therapy possible. These agents were in clinical use more than a decade before penicillin, and they are built around a sulfur-containing functional group. Which class is being described?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycosides

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fluoroquinolones

choices.label: C
choices.text: Macrolides

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sulfonamides

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tetracyclines

explanation.summary: Sulfa drugs were the first systemic antibiotics, preceding penicillin by more than a decade.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfur compounds have been used to inhibit microbial growth for centuries, and sulfonamides became the first true systemic antibiotics. Penicillin usually gets credit as the first antibiotic, but the sulfa drugs beat that 'miracle drug' to the clinic by more than ten years and launched the transformation of modern medicine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aminoglycosides were introduced after the sulfonamide era had already begun.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fluoroquinolones are among the most recently introduced antibacterial classes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Macrolides are a later class and were not the first systemic antibacterials.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tetracyclines came into use well after the sulfa drugs and after penicillin.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A medicinal chemist groups several drugs by a shared core: a sulfur atom double bonded to two oxygen atoms and single bonded to a nitrogen, with variable R groups attached. Drugs carrying this core include certain diuretics and diabetes medications as well as antibacterials. Which structure is being described?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aminoglycoside amino sugar

choices.label: B
choices.text: Beta-lactam ring

choices.label: C
choices.text: Macrolide lactone ring

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sulfonamide functional group

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tetracycline four-ring nucleus

explanation.summary: The sulfonamide functional group is the core active structure of the sulfa drugs.
explanation.whyCorrect: The sulfonamide functional group consists of a sulfur atom bonded to two oxygens and to a nitrogen, with R groups that vary between agents. This single functional group defines the entire family of sulfa drugs, which spans antibacterials, diuretics, diabetes medications, and anti-inflammatory agents.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aminoglycoside amino sugars are linked sugar rings bearing amino groups, not sulfonyl groups.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The beta-lactam ring is a four-membered nitrogen-containing ring with no sulfonyl group.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The macrolide lactone ring is a large cyclic ester and contains no sulfur.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The tetracycline nucleus is a fused four-ring hydrocarbon skeleton, not a sulfonyl core.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man with advanced HIV infection is treated for cerebral toxoplasmosis with a short-acting sulfonamide that has a half-life of about 10 hours, given together with pyrimethamine. Which drug did he most likely receive?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pyrimethamine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sulfadiazine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sulfamethoxazole

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sulfisoxazole

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trimethoprim

explanation.summary: Sulfadiazine is the short-acting sulfonamide (half-life about 10 hours) that is paired with pyrimethamine.
explanation.whyCorrect: Of the two sulfonamides commonly used in humans, sulfadiazine is classified as short acting with a half-life of roughly 10 hours and is given for systemic disease in combination with pyrimethamine. Pyrimethamine blocks dihydrofolate reductase one step downstream of the sulfonamide, giving synergistic killing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pyrimethamine is the partner drug named in the stem and is a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sulfamethoxazole is intermediate acting (9–12 hours) and is paired with trimethoprim, not pyrimethamine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sulfisoxazole is not the agent classified as short acting and paired with pyrimethamine for systemic use.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trimethoprim is a folate antagonist, not a sulfonamide, and it has no sulfonamide core.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman is prescribed an oral sulfonamide for a urinary tract infection. The agent is described as intermediate acting, with a half-life of 9 to 12 hours, and it is co-formulated with trimethoprim. Which sulfonamide is she taking?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Para-aminobenzoic acid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pyrimethamine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sulfadiazine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sulfamethoxazole

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trimethoprim

explanation.summary: Sulfamethoxazole is the intermediate-acting sulfonamide (9–12 hour half-life) combined with trimethoprim.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfamethoxazole has a half-life of 9 to 12 hours, which places it in the intermediate-acting group, and it is most often given with trimethoprim. The pair is used for urinary tract infections as well as gut and skin infections and systemic disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Para-aminobenzoic acid is the bacterial substrate that sulfonamides mimic, not a drug.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pyrimethamine is a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor, not a sulfonamide.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sulfadiazine is short acting with a half-life near 10 hours and is combined with pyrimethamine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trimethoprim is the co-formulated partner named in the stem, not the sulfonamide itself.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Sulfamethoxazole is routinely co-formulated with a second drug that acts at a different step of the same bacterial pathway in order to augment its activity. Which drug is it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Folic acid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pyrimethamine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sulfadiazine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trimethoprim

choices.label: E
choices.text: Warfarin

explanation.summary: Sulfamethoxazole is combined with trimethoprim, which blocks a later step of the same folate pathway.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfamethoxazole blocks dihydropteroate synthase while trimethoprim blocks dihydrofolate reductase, one step further along the same pathway. Hitting two sequential enzymes augments the activity of sulfamethoxazole and converts two bacteriostatic drugs into a bactericidal combination.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Folic acid is supplemented to treat drug-induced folate deficiency, not to augment activity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pyrimethamine is the folate antagonist paired with sulfadiazine, not with sulfamethoxazole.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sulfadiazine is another sulfonamide; combining sulfonamides adds no benefit.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Warfarin is an anticoagulant whose metabolism is affected by sulfamethoxazole, not a partner drug.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: The sulfonamide functional group is found in many medications that are not antibacterials. Which of the following groups of drugs also contains sulfonamide-based agents?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anticoagulants, antiarrhythmics, and inhaled corticosteroids

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antihistamines, antacids, and inhaled bronchodilators

choices.label: C
choices.text: Antipsychotics, antiepileptics, and antiemetic agents

choices.label: D
choices.text: Beta-blockers, statins, and opioid analgesics

choices.label: E
choices.text: Diuretics, diabetes medications, and anti-inflammatory drugs

explanation.summary: Sulfa drugs include diuretics, diabetes medications, and anti-inflammatory agents in addition to antibacterials.
explanation.whyCorrect: The sulfonamide functional group defines a broad family of medications called the sulfa drugs. Only a subset of them are used as antimicrobials; diuretics, diabetes medications, and anti-inflammatory drugs are other major sulfa-containing classes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anticoagulants, antiarrhythmics, and inhaled corticosteroids do not share this functional group.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Antihistamines, antacids, and bronchodilators are not sulfa drug classes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antipsychotics, antiepileptics, and antiemetics are not defined by a sulfonamide core.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Beta-blockers, statins, and opioids are not built on a sulfonamide core.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Long-acting and even ultra-long-acting sulfonamide antibiotics exist and some are still used in veterinary medicine, but they are seldom prescribed for people. Which of the following best explains why they are rarely used in human practice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Limited human efficacy data, cost, side effects, and widespread resistance

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are bactericidal and therefore considered too toxic for outpatient use

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are destroyed by hepatic CYP2C9 enzymes before ever reaching the urine

choices.label: D
choices.text: They cannot be given orally and must be dosed parenterally in hospital

choices.label: E
choices.text: They have no measurable affinity for the dihydropteroate synthase enzyme

explanation.summary: Long-acting sulfonamides are rarely used in humans because of poor efficacy data, cost, side effects, and resistance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Long-acting and ultra-long-acting sulfonamides were developed but never found a durable clinical niche in humans. Limited efficacy data, cost, adverse effects, and highly prevalent resistance keep them out of human practice, though some remain in veterinary care.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Sulfonamides given alone are bacteriostatic, not bactericidal, and toxicity is not tied to duration.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Only sulfamethoxazole undergoes partial CYP2C9 metabolism, and the drug still reaches the urine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sulfonamides in general have very good oral absorption, so route is not the limitation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: All sulfonamides act on dihydropteroate synthase; that is the defining mechanism of the class.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A sulfonamide is used as monotherapy against a susceptible organism. Which of the following best describes its effect on that bacterial population?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It kills the bacteria by cleaving the bacterial chromosome

choices.label: B
choices.text: It kills the bacteria by forming pores in the cell membrane

choices.label: C
choices.text: It lyses the bacteria by disrupting cell wall cross-linking

choices.label: D
choices.text: It neutralizes the toxins that the bacteria release into tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: It stops bacterial growth and replication without killing

explanation.summary: Sulfonamides used alone are bacteriostatic.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfonamides do not actually kill bacteria on their own. By starving the cell of tetrahydrofolic acid they stop growth and replication, leaving clearance of the organism to host defenses. Only when a sulfonamide is paired with a folate antagonist does the combination become lethal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sulfonamides do not cleave DNA; they limit the precursors needed to make it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sulfonamides do not act on the bacterial membrane or form pores.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cell wall disruption is the mechanism of beta-lactams, not of folate pathway inhibitors.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sulfonamides have no toxin-neutralizing activity.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim are each bacteriostatic when used alone. Which of the following best describes what happens when the two are given together?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The combination becomes bactericidal only in the urine

choices.label: B
choices.text: The combination becomes bactericidal through synergy

choices.label: C
choices.text: The combination is bacteriostatic only against anaerobes

choices.label: D
choices.text: The combination stays bacteriostatic but lasts longer

choices.label: E
choices.text: The two drugs antagonize each other and lose activity

explanation.summary: Pairing a sulfonamide with a folate antagonist converts two bacteriostatic drugs into a bactericidal combination.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfamethoxazole blocks dihydropteroate synthase and trimethoprim blocks dihydrofolate reductase. Blocking two sequential steps of the same pathway drives tetrahydrofolic acid production low enough that the combined bacteriostatic actions become synergistic and lethal to the bacteria.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The synergy is a property of the pathway blockade, not of the urinary compartment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim does not cover anaerobes at all.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The character of the effect changes, not just its duration; the pair becomes bactericidal.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The two drugs are synergistic rather than antagonistic.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the mechanism by which sulfonamides inhibit bacterial growth?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Competitive inhibition of bacterial DNA polymerase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Competitive inhibition of bacterial RNA polymerase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Competitive inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Competitive inhibition of dihydropteroate synthase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Competitive inhibition of the 30S ribosomal subunit

explanation.summary: Sulfonamides are competitive inhibitors of bacterial dihydropteroate synthase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfonamides compete with para-aminobenzoic acid at the active site of dihydropteroate synthase, the enzyme that makes a key precursor of tetrahydrofolic acid. Without tetrahydrofolic acid the organism cannot make the DNA, RNA, and proteins it needs, so sulfonamides are effectively inhibitors of nucleic acid synthesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inhibition of DNA polymerase is the mechanism of other agents, not of sulfonamides.
whyWrongByChoice.B: RNA polymerase inhibition describes rifampin-type drugs, not sulfonamides.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dihydrofolate reductase is the target of trimethoprim and pyrimethamine, one step downstream.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sulfonamides have no direct effect on the bacterial ribosome.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Sulfonamides act as competitive inhibitors of their target enzyme because they closely resemble one of that enzyme's substrates. Which molecule do sulfonamides mimic?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dihydrofolic acid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Methionine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Para-aminobenzoic acid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pteridine

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tetrahydrofolic acid

explanation.summary: Sulfonamides are structural mimics of para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA).
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacteria take in or produce PABA, which dihydropteroate synthase condenses with pteridine. Because sulfonamides look like PABA, they occupy the enzyme's active site and competitively block formation of dihydropteroic acid, which stalls the whole folate pathway.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dihydrofolic acid lies downstream of the sulfonamide-sensitive step.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Methionine is a product made using tetrahydrofolic acid, not an enzyme substrate here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pteridine is the other substrate of the enzyme but is not what sulfonamides resemble.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tetrahydrofolic acid is the end product of the pathway, not the mimicked substrate.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Bacterial dihydropteroate synthase condenses para-aminobenzoic acid with pteridine. Which product does this reaction generate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dihydrofolic acid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dihydropteroic acid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Methionine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tetrahydrofolic acid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thymidine monophosphate

explanation.summary: Dihydropteroate synthase uses PABA and pteridine to make dihydropteroic acid.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pathway runs PABA plus pteridine to dihydropteroic acid, then dihydropteroic acid to dihydrofolic acid, then dihydrofolic acid to tetrahydrofolic acid. Dihydropteroic acid is the immediate product of the dihydropteroate synthase step, which is exactly where sulfonamides act.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dihydrofolic acid is formed from dihydropteroic acid, one step after this reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Methionine is also a downstream product of tetrahydrofolic acid metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tetrahydrofolic acid is produced two steps later by dihydrofolate reductase.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thymidine is made downstream using tetrahydrofolic acid as a cofactor.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A patient who started a sulfonamide antibiotic three days ago calls to report a side effect. Which of the following pairs represents the most common adverse reactions to these drugs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gastrointestinal upset and skin rash

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hepatitis and peripheral neuropathy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tendon rupture and photosensitivity

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tinnitus and vertigo

explanation.summary: The common adverse reactions to sulfonamides are GI upset and skin reactions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nausea and vomiting together with rash and pruritus are the everyday adverse reactions patients report on sulfonamides. The severe reactions such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis are genuinely rare, though any new rash on a sulfonamide must be taken seriously.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hepatitis and peripheral neuropathy are not the usual complaints on these drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity are not the common sulfonamide adverse reactions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tendon rupture and photosensitivity are associated with other antibacterial classes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tinnitus and vertigo are not typical sulfonamide reactions.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A bacterium is unable to generate tetrahydrofolic acid. Synthesis of which set of products is most directly impaired?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fatty acids, phospholipids, and mycolic acids

choices.label: B
choices.text: Heme, cytochromes, and iron-sulfur clusters

choices.label: C
choices.text: Peptidoglycan, teichoic acid, and lipopolysaccharide

choices.label: D
choices.text: Purines, thymidine, and methionine

choices.label: E
choices.text: Riboflavin, biotin, and pantothenic acid

explanation.summary: Tetrahydrofolic acid is required to make purines, thymidine, and methionine, and therefore DNA, RNA, and protein.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tetrahydrofolic acid feeds three branches: purines for DNA and RNA, thymidine for DNA, and methionine for protein. Blocking folate synthesis therefore starves the cell of nucleic acid and protein precursors, which is why sulfonamides are effectively inhibitors of nucleic acid synthesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lipid synthesis does not depend directly on the folate pathway.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Heme and iron-sulfur cluster assembly are independent of tetrahydrofolic acid.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cell wall components are not made from tetrahydrofolic acid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: These vitamins are not the downstream products of the folate pathway.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Sulfonamides are far more toxic to bacteria than to human cells. Which feature of human physiology best explains this selective toxicity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Human cells make para-aminobenzoic acid in large excess

choices.label: B
choices.text: Human cells pump sulfonamides out using efflux transporters

choices.label: C
choices.text: Human dihydrofolate reductase is absent from most tissues

choices.label: D
choices.text: Humans lack dihydropteroate synthase and import dietary folate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Humans rapidly conjugate and excrete sulfonamides in the bile

explanation.summary: Humans do not possess the sulfonamide target enzyme and instead take up preformed folate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mammals cannot make folic acid at all; we have a folic acid transporter and obtain folate from the diet. Because we do not express dihydropteroate synthase, the drug target simply is not present in human cells, which gives sulfonamides their selective toxicity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Human cells do not produce PABA in excess to outcompete the drug.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Efflux is a bacterial resistance mechanism, not the basis of human safety.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Humans do possess dihydrofolate reductase, which is why trimethoprim can cause folate deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Biliary handling of the drug is not what spares human cells from its mechanism.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A researcher notes that a minority of bacterial species are auxotrophic for folic acid, taking it up from their environment rather than making it. Compared with the majority of bacteria, how would such an organism be expected to respond to a sulfonamide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Killed rather than inhibited, because folate stores are depleted faster

choices.label: B
choices.text: More susceptible, because it cannot upregulate its PABA synthesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: More susceptible, because sulfonamides also block folate uptake

choices.label: D
choices.text: Relatively unaffected, because it does not depend on dihydropteroate synthase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unaffected, because it also lacks dihydrofolate reductase entirely

explanation.summary: Bacteria that scavenge preformed folate do not rely on the enzyme sulfonamides inhibit.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfonamides work only because most bacteria must synthesize their own folate through dihydropteroate synthase. An organism that is auxotrophic for folic acid ingests it ready made, so blocking that synthetic enzyme does little. The broad activity of sulfonamides comes from the fact that the majority of bacteria do have to make folate themselves.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sulfonamides are bacteriostatic on their own and do not kill such organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Increased PABA synthesis is a resistance mechanism, but its absence does not create susceptibility in a folate scavenger.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sulfonamides inhibit an enzyme; they do not block folate transport.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Dihydrofolate reductase is still needed to reduce imported folate to the active form.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Trimethoprim and pyrimethamine are folate antagonists that are paired with sulfonamides for synergy. Which enzyme do both of these drugs inhibit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dihydrofolate reductase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dihydropteroate synthase

choices.label: C
choices.text: DNA gyrase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thymidylate synthase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topoisomerase IV

explanation.summary: Trimethoprim and pyrimethamine both inhibit dihydrofolate reductase, which converts DHF to THF.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dihydrofolate reductase catalyzes the conversion of dihydrofolic acid to tetrahydrofolic acid. Trimethoprim and pyrimethamine block this step, which sits immediately downstream of the sulfonamide-sensitive step and is why the pairings work so well together.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Dihydropteroate synthase is the sulfonamide target, one step upstream.
whyWrongByChoice.C: DNA gyrase is the target of the fluoroquinolone class of drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thymidylate synthase acts after tetrahydrofolic acid is available and is not the target here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Topoisomerase IV is also a quinolone target, not a folate pathway enzyme.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Trimethoprim inhibits an enzyme that human cells also possess, yet at therapeutic doses it is generally well tolerated. Which property best accounts for this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It binds bacterial dihydrofolate reductase much more avidly than the human form

choices.label: B
choices.text: It can reach the human enzyme only within the cells of the renal tubule

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is absorbed only at the intestinal sites where the target bacteria reside

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is actively concentrated inside bacterial cells by outer membrane porins

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is destroyed by human hepatic enzymes before it can reach the tissues

explanation.summary: Trimethoprim has much stronger affinity for bacterial dihydrofolate reductase than for the human enzyme.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both bacteria and humans use dihydrofolate reductase, so selectivity has to come from affinity rather than from the absence of a target. Trimethoprim binds the bacterial enzyme far more tightly, which allows bacterial folate synthesis to be shut down at doses that leave most human folate metabolism intact.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The drug is not confined to the kidney, and human enzyme inhibition can occur elsewhere.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Trimethoprim is well absorbed and distributes widely through the body.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Selectivity is not explained by porin-mediated concentration of the drug.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The drug must remain intact to work; hepatic destruction would abolish its activity.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A clinician explains why sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim can retain activity against an organism that has developed resistance to one of the two drugs. Which of the following best supports that explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Each drug increases the intracellular accumulation of the other

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mutating two enzymes of one pathway at once is unlikely

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sulfamethoxazole destroys the plasmid carrying trimethoprim resistance

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sulfamethoxazole saturates the same enzyme that trimethoprim inhibits

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trimethoprim blocks the efflux pumps that export sulfamethoxazole

explanation.summary: Attacking two enzymes in the same pathway makes simultaneous resistance mutations improbable.
explanation.whyCorrect: A single enzyme is relatively easy for bacteria to mutate, but mutating two crucial enzymes in the same pathway at the same time is much less likely. Pairing a sulfonamide with a folate antagonist therefore helps overcome resistance to one or the other drug.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The benefit comes from dual pathway blockade, not from altered drug accumulation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neither drug eliminates resistance plasmids.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The two drugs act on different enzymes, which is precisely the point of the pairing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trimethoprim does not inhibit sulfonamide efflux pumps.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Historically, 'triple sulfa' preparations combining several sulfonamides were marketed in the hope of improving efficacy, but trials showed no benefit. Which of the following best explains that result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All sulfonamides competitively inhibit the same bacterial enzyme

choices.label: B
choices.text: Combining sulfonamides sharply increases the risk of crystalluria

choices.label: C
choices.text: Each sulfonamide induces the metabolism of the others via CYP2C9

choices.label: D
choices.text: The agents compete with one another for renal tubular secretion

choices.label: E
choices.text: The shorter-acting agents are excreted before the others act

explanation.summary: Stacking sulfonamides adds nothing because every sulfonamide inhibits the same target enzyme.
explanation.whyCorrect: Synergy in this pathway comes from hitting two different enzymes, as with a sulfonamide plus trimethoprim. Since all sulfonamides competitively inhibit dihydropteroate synthase, combining several of them simply piles more inhibitor onto one target, which is why triple sulfa preparations showed no good efficacy data.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Crystalluria risk is a safety issue but was not the reason efficacy failed to improve.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sulfonamides inhibit rather than induce CYP2C9, and that is not why the combinations failed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Competition for tubular secretion is not the explanation given for the lack of benefit.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Differences in half-life do not explain why the combination added no activity.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: An Escherichia coli isolate remains susceptible to trimethoprim but is resistant to sulfamethoxazole. Sequencing shows a point mutation in the gene for dihydropteroate synthase that lowers the enzyme's affinity for the drug while preserving its affinity for PABA. Which resistance mechanism does this represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alteration of the bacterial target enzyme

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased permeability of the outer membrane

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enzymatic inactivation of the drug molecule

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased efflux of the drug from the cell

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased synthesis of para-aminobenzoic acid

explanation.summary: A mutation that changes the drug-binding site of DHPS is target alteration, one of three sulfonamide resistance mechanisms.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfonamide resistance occurs by alteration of the bacterial DHPS enzyme, by decreased uptake or increased efflux, or by increased PABA synthesis. A point mutation that reduces drug affinity while preserving substrate affinity is the classic example of target alteration.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Reduced permeability is an uptake problem, not a change in the target enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Enzymatic drug destruction is not among the sulfonamide resistance mechanisms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Efflux resistance lowers intracellular drug levels and leaves the enzyme sequence normal.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Increased PABA synthesis would outcompete the drug without any change in the enzyme itself.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A bacterial isolate resists sulfamethoxazole even though its dihydropteroate synthase sequence is normal and drug uptake is normal. Intracellular levels of the enzyme's natural substrate are markedly elevated. Which resistance mechanism best explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The organism has acquired a second copy of the target enzyme

choices.label: B
choices.text: The organism has lost the porin used for drug entry

choices.label: C
choices.text: The organism hydrolyzes the sulfonamide with a sulfatase

choices.label: D
choices.text: The organism now salvages thymidine from its environment

choices.label: E
choices.text: The organism overproduces para-aminobenzoic acid

explanation.summary: Overproducing PABA outcompetes a competitive inhibitor at the enzyme active site.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfonamides are competitive inhibitors, so their effect can be overcome by raising the concentration of the true substrate. Increased PABA synthesis is one of the three recognized sulfonamide resistance mechanisms and fits an isolate with a normal enzyme, normal drug entry, and high substrate levels.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gene duplication of the target is not among the described resistance mechanisms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Loss of a porin would reduce drug uptake, but the stem states uptake is normal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sulfonamides are not inactivated by bacterial hydrolytic enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thymidine salvage is not the mechanism described, and it would not raise PABA levels.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A Gram-negative isolate is resistant to sulfamethoxazole. Its dihydropteroate synthase binds the drug normally and PABA production is normal, but intracellular drug concentrations remain very low throughout exposure. Which mechanism is most likely responsible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Beta-lactamase-mediated hydrolysis of the drug

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased drug uptake or increased drug efflux

choices.label: C
choices.text: Methylation of the ribosome that blocks drug binding

choices.label: D
choices.text: Overproduction of para-aminobenzoic acid by the organism

choices.label: E
choices.text: Point mutation within the dihydropteroate synthase gene

explanation.summary: Low intracellular drug with a normal target and normal PABA points to an uptake or efflux problem.
explanation.whyCorrect: One of the three sulfonamide resistance mechanisms is decreased uptake or increased efflux of the drug. If the enzyme still binds drug normally and substrate levels are normal, the only way the organism can survive is by keeping the drug out of the cytoplasm.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Beta-lactamases hydrolyze beta-lactam rings and have no action on sulfonamides.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ribosomal methylation confers resistance to protein synthesis inhibitors, not sulfonamides.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PABA production is stated to be normal in this isolate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The enzyme is stated to bind the drug normally, excluding target alteration.
