questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man is to be treated with a sulfonamide. Which of the following best describes the absorption and available routes of administration of these drugs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absorption limited to the colon, restricting use to gut infections

choices.label: B
choices.text: Good oral absorption but negligible absorption through skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Good oral and topical absorption, with parenteral forms available

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral absorption only when taken with a high-fat meal

choices.label: E
choices.text: Poor oral absorption, so only parenteral dosing is effective

explanation.summary: Sulfonamides are given orally, topically, and parenterally, with very good oral and good topical absorption.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most sulfonamides in use today are available as oral, topical, and parenteral formulations. All have very good oral absorption and good topical absorption, which is why oral therapy is the usual route even for systemic infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: These drugs are absorbed systemically and treat urinary, skin, and systemic infections.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Topical absorption is also good, not negligible.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Absorption does not depend on a fatty meal.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oral absorption is excellent, so parenteral dosing is not required for efficacy.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Both sulfadiazine and sulfamethoxazole undergo hepatic metabolism, and sulfamethoxazole in particular is partly handled by one cytochrome P450 isoform that explains several of its drug interactions. Which isoform is it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: CYP1A2

choices.label: B
choices.text: CYP2C19

choices.label: C
choices.text: CYP2C9

choices.label: D
choices.text: CYP2D6

choices.label: E
choices.text: CYP3A4

explanation.summary: Sulfamethoxazole undergoes partial metabolism by CYP2C9 and also inhibits that enzyme.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfadiazine and sulfamethoxazole are both metabolized in the liver, and sulfamethoxazole is partly metabolized by CYP2C9. Because it also inhibits CYP2C9, it slows the clearance of other substrates of that enzyme, most notably warfarin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CYP1A2 does not handle sulfamethoxazole.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CYP2C19 is a different isoform and induction of it would lower rather than raise INR.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CYP2D6 is not involved in sulfonamide metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CYP3A4 is not the isoform responsible for sulfamethoxazole metabolism or its main interaction.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man on chronic warfarin is prescribed sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim for a skin infection. Four days later his INR is markedly elevated and he reports bleeding gums. Which mechanism best explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct inhibition of hepatic vitamin K epoxide reductase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Displacement of warfarin from hepatic storage sites

choices.label: C
choices.text: Induction of CYP2C19, which accelerates warfarin clearance

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibition of CYP2C9, which slows warfarin metabolism

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibition of platelet cyclooxygenase, prolonging bleeding

explanation.summary: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim inhibits CYP2C9 and therefore raises INR in patients on warfarin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Warfarin is metabolized by CYP2C9, and sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim inhibits that enzyme. Warfarin accumulates, anticoagulation deepens, and INR rises with an increased risk of bleeding, so patients on both drugs require close monitoring.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inhibiting vitamin K epoxide reductase is warfarin's own mechanism, not the added effect of the antibiotic.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The interaction is a metabolic one, not displacement from hepatic stores.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Induction of a metabolizing enzyme would lower INR rather than raise it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Platelet cyclooxygenase inhibition affects bleeding time, not the INR.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: An 80-year-old woman with chronic kidney disease who takes lisinopril and ibuprofen is started on sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim. One week later she reports weakness, and an ECG shows peaked T waves. Which electrolyte abnormality is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hypercalcemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hyperkalemia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hypocalcemia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hypokalemia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hyponatremia

explanation.summary: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim raises potassium, especially alongside ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or NSAIDs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim increases the risk of hyperkalemia, and that risk compounds when it is combined with drugs such as ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and NSAIDs. Hyperkalemia can be life threatening in the elderly and in patients with chronic kidney disease, so these patients need close monitoring.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Calcium is likewise unaffected by this antibiotic combination.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim does not affect calcium levels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The drug raises rather than lowers serum potassium.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sodium disturbance is not the characteristic electrolyte effect of this drug.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A physician needs an orally administered agent that will reach the central nervous system. Which statement about the distribution of sulfadiazine and sulfamethoxazole is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are kept out of vaginal fluid and other secretions

choices.label: B
choices.text: They concentrate only within the liver and biliary tract

choices.label: C
choices.text: They penetrate cerebrospinal fluid and most body fluids well

choices.label: D
choices.text: They reach the urine but are excluded from middle ear fluid

choices.label: E
choices.text: They stay confined to plasma because of heavy protein binding

explanation.summary: Sulfadiazine and sulfamethoxazole distribute widely, including good CSF penetration.
explanation.whyCorrect: After absorption, the active sulfonamides and their paired folate inhibitors distribute into most tissues and body fluids, including urine, vaginal fluid, and middle ear fluid. Both sulfadiazine and sulfamethoxazole also achieve good cerebrospinal fluid penetration.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Vaginal fluid is specifically among the fluids these drugs enter.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Distribution is broad and is not limited to the hepatobiliary system.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Middle ear fluid is one of the compartments these drugs are known to reach.
whyWrongByChoice.E: These drugs distribute widely rather than remaining confined to plasma.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Sulfonamides are particularly effective for urinary tract infections. Which pharmacokinetic property best explains this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complete hepatic conversion to an active glucuronide

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elimination restricted to filtration of protein-bound drug

choices.label: C
choices.text: Extensive biliary excretion with enterohepatic recycling

choices.label: D
choices.text: Selective uptake and storage within renal tubular cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Urinary excretion with much of the drug still unmetabolized

explanation.summary: Sulfonamides are excreted in urine largely unmetabolized, giving high active drug levels in the urinary tract.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both sulfamethoxazole and sulfadiazine are excreted primarily through the urine, and a significant amount appears there unmetabolized. Active drug therefore bathes the urinary tract at high concentration, which underlies their good efficacy for UTIs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hepatic metabolism is partial, and the urinary activity depends on unmetabolized drug.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Protein-bound drug is not filtered; the point is that free active drug reaches the urine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: These drugs are not eliminated mainly through bile and enterohepatic recycling.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The drugs are excreted into the urine rather than stored within tubular cells.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A pharmacist counsels a patient starting sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim to take each tablet with at least 8 ounces of water. This advice is intended to prevent which adverse effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anuria

choices.label: B
choices.text: Crystalluria

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dysuria

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nausea and vomiting

choices.label: E
choices.text: Polyuria

explanation.summary: Drinking at least 8 ounces of water with sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim helps prevent crystalluria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim can precipitate in the urine and cause crystalluria. Taking each tablet with at least 8 ounces of water helps solubilize the drug and keeps urine flow high, which lowers the chance of crystals forming.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anuria does not develop with use of sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dysuria is not an effect attributed to this drug combination.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GI upset does occur, but water intake is advised specifically to prevent crystal formation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Polyuria is not associated with sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim therapy.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man develops fatigue, scleral icterus, and dark urine two days after starting sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim for a skin infection. His hemoglobin has fallen from 14 to 9 g/dL and the smear shows red cell fragmentation and bite cells. Which underlying condition best explains this reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hereditary spherocytosis of the red cell membrane

choices.label: C
choices.text: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria with complement lysis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pyruvate kinase deficiency of the glycolytic pathway

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sickle cell trait inherited from one parent

explanation.summary: Sulfonamide exposure in G6PD deficiency can trigger rapid acute hemolytic anemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the rarer sulfonamide adverse reactions is acute hemolysis in patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency. Exposure to the drug in these patients can cause a rapid acute hemolytic anemia, which presents exactly as this abrupt drop in hemoglobin with jaundice and dark urine shortly after starting the drug.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hereditary spherocytosis is not the enzyme deficiency that sulfonamides unmask.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria is not triggered by sulfonamide exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pyruvate kinase deficiency is not the condition linked to sulfonamide hemolysis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sickle cell trait does not predispose to sulfonamide-triggered hemolysis.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: On day 5 of sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim therapy, a 30-year-old woman develops a painful rash with mucosal erosions and sheets of detaching epidermis. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Continue therapy and add an oral antihistamine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continue therapy and apply a topical corticosteroid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Halve the dose and complete the planned course

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stop the sulfonamide and do not rechallenge

choices.label: E
choices.text: Switch to a long-acting sulfonamide preparation

explanation.summary: Any rash on a sulfonamide requires stopping the drug, because SJS and TEN can be fatal.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfonamides can rarely induce Stevens-Johnson syndrome and its deadlier counterpart toxic epidermal necrolysis, which lie on a spectrum defined by how much body surface is involved. If a patient taking a sulfonamide begins to develop a rash, the offending drug must be discontinued, since these reactions can be fatal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Continuing the drug risks progression from SJS to toxic epidermal necrolysis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Topical therapy does not remove the offending drug, which is the essential step.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dose reduction does not address an immune-mediated severe cutaneous reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Any sulfonamide can provoke the same reaction, so switching within the class is unsafe.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man on long-term suppressive sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim develops a macrocytic anemia with low serum folate. Which of the following best explains this finding and its management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sulfamethoxazole blocks the human folate transporter; stop the drug

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sulfamethoxazole inhibits human dihydrofolate reductase; give folic acid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Trimethoprim blocks human dihydropteroate synthase; give vitamin B12

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trimethoprim destroys folate stored in the liver; give vitamin B12

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trimethoprim inhibits human dihydrofolate reductase; give folic acid

explanation.summary: Trimethoprim inhibits the human dihydrofolate reductase, so folate deficiency is treated with folic acid supplementation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Humans obtain folate from the diet and do not express dihydropteroate synthase, so the sulfonamide component has no human target. Trimethoprim, however, does inhibit human dihydrofolate reductase, and in patients who become folate deficient, supplementation with folic acid is recommended.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sulfamethoxazole acts on a bacterial enzyme and does not block the human folate transporter.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dihydrofolate reductase is the trimethoprim target, not the sulfamethoxazole target.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Humans do not express dihydropteroate synthase, so it cannot be the site of this toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trimethoprim inhibits an enzyme rather than destroying hepatic folate stores.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman in her first trimester of pregnancy has an uncomplicated urinary tract infection with Escherichia coli confirmed on culture. She asks to take the sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim that worked for her previous infections. Which of the following is the best reason to choose a different antibiotic?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sulfamethoxazole crosses the placenta and causes fetal crystalluria

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sulfamethoxazole induces fetal CYP2C9 and accelerates drug clearance

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sulfamethoxazole loses activity against E. coli during pregnancy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trimethoprim displaces fetal bilirubin from albumin, causing kernicterus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trimethoprim interferes with folate metabolism, risking neural tube defects

explanation.summary: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim is avoided in the first trimester because trimethoprim's antifolate effect raises the risk of neural tube defects.
explanation.whyCorrect: Trimethoprim interferes with folate metabolism, and adequate folate is essential for neural tube closure early in gestation. For that reason sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim should generally be avoided in the first trimester and a safer antibiotic chosen for the urinary tract infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Crystalluria is a maternal urinary adverse effect, not the fetal risk driving this decision.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fetal CYP2C9 induction is not a recognized risk of this combination.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Activity against E. coli is unchanged in pregnancy; the concern is fetal safety.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bilirubin displacement is a sulfonamide effect and is the concern in the last month, not the first trimester.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A woman at 37 weeks' gestation requires antibiotic therapy, and her obstetrician specifically avoids sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim. Which mechanism underlies this late-pregnancy concern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sulfamethoxazole causes premature closure of the ductus arteriosus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sulfamethoxazole precipitates in fetal renal tubules and causes anuria

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sulfonamides displace bilirubin from albumin and raise free bilirubin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Trimethoprim depletes maternal folate and causes neural tube defects

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trimethoprim inhibits fetal dihydropteroate synthase and impairs growth

explanation.summary: Near term, sulfonamides displace bilirubin from albumin and raise free unconjugated bilirubin, risking kernicterus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfonamides compete with bilirubin for binding sites on serum albumin. In the last month of pregnancy this displacement increases free unconjugated bilirubin in the newborn, which can deposit in the brain and cause kernicterus, so the drug should be avoided if possible at that stage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ductal closure is an NSAID effect and is not attributed to sulfonamides.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Crystalluria is a maternal urinary effect, not a described fetal renal toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The folate and neural tube concern applies to the first trimester, not to term.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The fetus, like all mammals, does not express dihydropteroate synthase.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim has broad coverage of many aerobic Gram-positive and Gram-negative species but does not cover anaerobes. An infection caused by which of the following organisms would therefore be expected to respond to this combination?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacteroides fragilis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clostridioides difficile

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clostridium botulinum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Clostridium perfringens

choices.label: E
choices.text: Klebsiella pneumoniae

explanation.summary: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim covers aerobic organisms such as Klebsiella pneumoniae but not anaerobes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim has broad activity against many aerobic Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms, and Klebsiella pneumoniae falls squarely in that group. Anaerobes are outside its spectrum, which is why anaerobic infections require a different agent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bacteroides fragilis is an anaerobe and is not covered by this combination.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Clostridioides difficile is also anaerobic and is not treated with this combination.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clostridium botulinum is an anaerobic organism outside the drug's spectrum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clostridium perfringens is likewise an anaerobe and is not covered.

questions.topicName: DNA Gyrase Inhibitors and Folic acid synthesis inhibitors – 1 of 2: Sulfonamides

questions.stem: A medical student is reviewing a group of antibiotics that bind the 50S ribosomal subunit, including azithromycin, linezolid, and the streptogramins. Which of the following best describes how these agents usually affect susceptible bacteria?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bactericidal, by cleaving bacterial chromosomal DNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bactericidal, by collapsing the bacterial membrane potential

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bactericidal, by lysing the bacterial cell wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bacteriostatic, by blocking bacterial folate synthesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Bacteriostatic, by disrupting bacterial protein translation

explanation.summary: The 50S protein synthesis inhibitors disrupt bacterial translation and are typically bacteriostatic.
explanation.whyCorrect: Agents that bind the 50S ribosomal subunit interfere with the assembly of peptide chains, halting bacterial protein production. Because the organism is stopped from growing rather than directly killed, these drugs are classed as bacteriostatic. The group includes the macrolides (azithromycin, clarithromycin), linezolid, and the streptogramins.

whyWrongByChoice.A: DNA-directed killing describes the fluoroquinolones, which are a separate class from the 50S inhibitors.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Membrane disruption is not how 50S protein synthesis inhibitors work, and these agents are not typically bactericidal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cell wall lysis is the mechanism of beta-lactams such as amoxicillin and the cephalosporins, not of ribosomal agents.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Folate synthesis inhibition is not the mechanism of any drug that binds the 50S subunit.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A pharmacology handout groups antibacterial drugs by their molecular target. Which of the following agents exerts its effect at the 50S ribosomal subunit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Azithromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cephalexin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin

explanation.summary: Macrolides such as azithromycin are 50S protein synthesis inhibitors.
explanation.whyCorrect: The 50S inhibitors discussed here are the macrolides (azithromycin, clarithromycin), linezolid, and the streptogramins. Azithromycin is a macrolide and therefore acts at the 50S subunit to block translation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin is a beta-lactam that targets the cell wall.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aztreonam is a beta-lactam active against gram-negative organisms, not a ribosomal inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cephalexin is a cephalosporin and works on the cell wall.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone and does not act at the ribosome.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 19-year-old college student has 2 weeks of nonproductive cough, low-grade fever, and malaise. Testing supports infection with Mycoplasma pneumoniae. Which of the following oral agents provides the best coverage for this organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Azithromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cephalexin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Clindamycin

explanation.summary: Macrolides have excellent coverage of atypical organisms such as Mycoplasma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Macrolides are the class with excellent activity against atypical bacteria, including Chlamydia, Mycoplasma, Mycobacterium, and Legionella. Azithromycin is therefore an appropriate oral choice for Mycoplasma pneumoniae, which is one of the atypical causes of community-acquired pneumonia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin is a beta-lactam without meaningful atypical coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aztreonam covers gram-negative organisms and has no atypical activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cephalosporins do not cover the atypical bacteria.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clindamycin is used for aerobic gram-positive cocci and anaerobes above the diaphragm, not atypicals.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man develops pneumonia after staying at a hotel with a contaminated water system, and urinary antigen testing confirms Legionnaires' disease. Which of the following is an appropriate first-line treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Azithromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cephalexin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Clindamycin

explanation.summary: Legionnaires' disease is treated first-line with azithromycin or levofloxacin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unlike most of the other fastidious and vector-borne atypical infections, where doxycycline is first-line, Legionnaires' disease is treated with azithromycin or levofloxacin. Macrolides have excellent activity against Legionella, one of the classic atypical respiratory pathogens.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin is a beta-lactam and does not cover Legionella.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aztreonam is directed at gram-negative bacteria and does not treat atypicals.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cephalosporins do not cover any of the atypical bacteria.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clindamycin has no atypical coverage; it is aimed at aerobic gram-positive cocci and anaerobes above the diaphragm.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: An attending explains why macrolides are frequently chosen for upper and lower respiratory tract infections. In addition to atypical organisms, macrolides also have good activity against which of the following groups of respiratory pathogens?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enterococcus and gram-negative anaerobic bacteria

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pseudomonas and other aerobic gram-negative bacilli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rickettsia rickettsii and Ehrlichia chaffeensis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus, and Moraxella

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococci and MRSA

explanation.summary: Macrolides cover S. pneumoniae, Haemophilus, and Moraxella in addition to atypicals, which is why they suit respiratory infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beyond their excellent atypical coverage, macrolides have good activity against Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus, and Moraxella. Because these organisms are common causes of upper and lower respiratory tract infection, macrolides are a practical treatment option in that setting.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enterococcus and gram-negative anaerobes are organisms that clindamycin also fails to cover; they are not the macrolide target group.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pseudomonas and other aerobic gram-negative bacilli are covered by agents such as aztreonam, not macrolides.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tick-borne organisms such as Rickettsia and Ehrlichia are treated first-line with doxycycline.
whyWrongByChoice.E: MRSA and VRE are the province of linezolid and the streptogramins, not the macrolides.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman with no comorbidities is diagnosed with community-acquired pneumonia and is determined not to require hospitalization. Which of the following empiric oral regimens best covers the expected pathogens?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin/clavulanate plus azithromycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aztreonam plus oral vancomycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin plus oral clindamycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Clindamycin plus oral cephalexin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Linezolid plus oral azithromycin

explanation.summary: Outpatient CAP is treated empirically with a beta-lactam plus a macrolide.
explanation.whyCorrect: Empiric outpatient CAP regimens are designed to cover Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and the atypicals (Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Legionella pneumophila, Chlamydia pneumoniae). The standard first-line option pairs a beta-lactam such as amoxicillin/clavulanate or a third-generation cephalosporin with a macrolide, most often azithromycin, for the atypical coverage.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Aztreonam and vancomycin cover gram-negatives and resistant gram-positives but miss the atypical pathogens entirely.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ciprofloxacin has poor Streptococcus pneumoniae activity, and clindamycin adds no atypical coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clindamycin does not cover the atypicals or Haemophilus, and cephalexin does not cover atypicals either.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Linezolid adds gram-positive coverage such as MRSA and VRE, which is not what empiric outpatient CAP requires.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with community-acquired pneumonia is started on cefdinir, but a macrolide is contraindicated. Which of the following should be added to his regimen to cover atypical pathogens?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cephalexin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Doxycycline

explanation.summary: Doxycycline substitutes for the macrolide in a CAP regimen when a macrolide is contraindicated.
explanation.whyCorrect: In outpatient CAP the macrolide component supplies atypical coverage. When a macrolide cannot be used, doxycycline is the recommended substitute in that role, preserving coverage of Mycoplasma, Legionella, and Chlamydia alongside the beta-lactam.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin is another beta-lactam and would duplicate, not complement, the cefdinir.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aztreonam covers gram-negative organisms and contributes no atypical coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cephalexin is a cephalosporin, and cephalosporins do not cover atypical bacteria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clindamycin covers aerobic gram-positive cocci and anaerobes above the diaphragm, not atypicals.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 51-year-old woman with community-acquired pneumonia is to be managed as an outpatient but can take neither a beta-lactam nor a macrolide. Which of the following is an acceptable single-agent alternative?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aztreonam monotherapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cephalexin monotherapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin monotherapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Clindamycin monotherapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Levofloxacin monotherapy

explanation.summary: A respiratory fluoroquinolone such as levofloxacin can be used as monotherapy for CAP.
explanation.whyCorrect: In addition to the beta-lactam plus macrolide combination, a respiratory fluoroquinolone given as monotherapy is an accepted option for community-acquired pneumonia. Levofloxacin is a respiratory fluoroquinolone and covers both typical and atypical CAP pathogens on its own.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aztreonam is a gram-negative agent and misses both S. pneumoniae and the atypicals.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cephalexin is a beta-lactam, which is excluded here, and it does not cover atypicals.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ciprofloxacin is not considered a respiratory fluoroquinolone because of its poor activity against Streptococcus pneumoniae.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clindamycin lacks coverage of Haemophilus and the atypicals and is not a CAP regimen.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A resident asks why ciprofloxacin is not grouped with the respiratory fluoroquinolones even though it is a fluoroquinolone. Which of the following best explains this distinction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It has poor activity against Legionella pneumophila

choices.label: B
choices.text: It has poor activity against Moraxella catarrhalis

choices.label: C
choices.text: It has poor activity against Mycoplasma pneumoniae

choices.label: D
choices.text: It has poor activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa

choices.label: E
choices.text: It has poor activity against Streptococcus pneumoniae

explanation.summary: Ciprofloxacin is excluded from the respiratory fluoroquinolones because of poor Streptococcus pneumoniae activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a leading cause of community-acquired pneumonia, so an agent used as CAP monotherapy must cover it reliably. Ciprofloxacin's activity against S. pneumoniae is poor, which is the primary reason it is not called a respiratory fluoroquinolone.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Legionella activity is not the deficiency that disqualifies ciprofloxacin from this label.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Moraxella coverage is not the stated basis for the respiratory fluoroquinolone designation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mycoplasma coverage is not the cited reason for excluding ciprofloxacin from this group.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ciprofloxacin's gram-negative activity, including Pseudomonas, is one of its strengths rather than a weakness.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man admitted for a hip fracture develops fever, cough, and a new pulmonary infiltrate on hospital day 5. Compared with pneumonia acquired outside a health care facility, this infection is best classified as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Atypical pneumonia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chronic pneumonitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Community-acquired pneumonia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hospital-acquired pneumonia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Recurrent pneumonia

explanation.summary: Pneumonia acquired in the hospital is HAP, as distinguished from community-acquired pneumonia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Community-acquired pneumonia is by definition a respiratory infection acquired from the community, in contrast to hospital-acquired pneumonia. A new infiltrate arising several days into an admission fits the hospital-acquired category, which is not treated with the standard outpatient CAP regimens.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Atypical pneumonia refers to the causative organism group, not to where the infection was acquired.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic pneumonitis does not describe an acute new infiltrate developing during a hospitalization.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CAP is acquired outside the hospital, which does not fit an infiltrate that appeared during the admission.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Recurrence describes repeated episodes over time rather than the setting of acquisition.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man has a dental abscess that has spread into the submandibular space, and an anaerobic infection above the diaphragm is suspected. Which of the following agents is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cephalexin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Linezolid

explanation.summary: Clindamycin is the agent used for anaerobic infections above the diaphragm.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clindamycin's niche is anaerobic infection above the diaphragm, along with aerobic gram-positive cocci. An odontogenic anaerobic infection in the head and neck falls squarely within that spectrum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azithromycin is used for atypical and common respiratory pathogens, not anaerobic abscesses.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aztreonam covers gram-negative bacteria and is not an anaerobic agent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cephalexin is a cephalosporin without the anaerobic spectrum needed here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Linezolid provides gram-positive coverage including MRSA and VRE rather than anaerobic coverage.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: Which of the following types of bacteria are effectively treated with clindamycin?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aerobic gram-negative bacilli

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aerobic gram-positive cocci

choices.label: C
choices.text: Anaerobic bacteria below the diaphragm

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gram-negative anaerobic bacteria

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococci

explanation.summary: Clindamycin covers aerobic gram-positive cocci and anaerobes above the diaphragm.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clindamycin is effective against aerobic gram-positive cocci and against anaerobic infections located above the diaphragm. It is not effective against enterococci or gram-negative pathogens, including gram-negative anaerobes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aerobic gram-negative bacilli are not covered by clindamycin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clindamycin's anaerobic coverage is restricted to organisms above the diaphragm, not below it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gram-negative anaerobic bacteria are specifically excluded from clindamycin's coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clindamycin has minimal Enterococcus activity, so VRE is well outside its spectrum.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man has an intra-abdominal abscess growing Enterococcus species and gram-negative anaerobes. A resident proposes clindamycin monotherapy. Which of the following best describes clindamycin's limitation in this situation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It covers both organisms but not aerobic gram-positive cocci

choices.label: B
choices.text: It covers both organisms only at maximal oral dosing

choices.label: C
choices.text: It covers Enterococcus but not the gram-negative anaerobes

choices.label: D
choices.text: It covers neither Enterococcus nor the gram-negative anaerobes

choices.label: E
choices.text: It covers the gram-negative anaerobes but not Enterococcus

explanation.summary: Clindamycin misses both Enterococcus and gram-negative anaerobes, so it cannot cover this abscess.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clindamycin is not effective against enterococci, and it is not effective against gram-negative pathogens, a group that explicitly includes gram-negative anaerobic bacteria. Both organisms cultured here fall in its blind spots, so clindamycin monotherapy would fail.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aerobic gram-positive cocci are in fact one of clindamycin's core targets.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dose escalation does not extend clindamycin's spectrum to organisms it inherently does not cover.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clindamycin has minimal Enterococcus activity, so it does not cover that organism either.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gram-negative anaerobes are among the pathogens clindamycin fails to cover.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A resident proposes clindamycin for a patient with an anaerobic infection. Clindamycin's anaerobic activity is best described as reliable against anaerobes in which of the following locations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anaerobes above the diaphragm only

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anaerobes at any body site, including the colon

choices.label: C
choices.text: Anaerobes below the diaphragm only

choices.label: D
choices.text: Anaerobes confined to the urinary tract only

choices.label: E
choices.text: Anaerobes only when present in the bloodstream

explanation.summary: Clindamycin's anaerobic coverage is limited to infections above the diaphragm.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clindamycin is used against anaerobic infections above the diaphragm together with aerobic gram-positive cocci. Below-the-diaphragm anaerobic infections frequently involve gram-negative anaerobes, which clindamycin does not cover.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Clindamycin is not an all-sites anaerobic agent, since gram-negative anaerobes escape it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This reverses the rule; below-the-diaphragm anaerobes are the ones clindamycin is unreliable against.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The clindamycin anaerobic rule is anatomic with respect to the diaphragm, not the urinary tract.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bloodstream location is not what defines clindamycin's anaerobic spectrum.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man has bacteremia caused by vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium. Which of the following can treat a VRE infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Azithromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: D
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Linezolid

explanation.summary: Linezolid covers gram-positive bacteria including MRSA and vancomycin-resistant Enterococci.
explanation.whyCorrect: Linezolid's coverage resembles that of vancomycin for gram-positive organisms, but it importantly extends to staphylococci including MRSA and to vancomycin-resistant Enterococci. That makes it a treatment option when Enterococcus is vancomycin resistant.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin is not effective against vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Azithromycin is directed at atypical and common respiratory pathogens, not VRE.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aztreonam covers many gram-negative bacteria, including Pseudomonas, and has no gram-positive activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clindamycin has minimal activity against Enterococcus species of any resistance pattern.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: Linezolid and the streptogramins have a spectrum of activity most similar to which of the following agents?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Azithromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Linezolid and streptogramins provide vancomycin-like gram-positive coverage.
explanation.whyCorrect: The coverage of linezolid and the streptogramins is described as similar to that of vancomycin, meaning strong gram-positive activity. Both additionally reach resistant gram-positives that vancomycin may not, such as MRSA for both agents and VRE for linezolid.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin's spectrum does not match the resistant gram-positive coverage of these drugs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Azithromycin is a macrolide whose strength is atypical and respiratory pathogen coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aztreonam is a gram-negative agent, the opposite end of the spectrum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone with predominantly gram-negative activity.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman with a methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infection is clinically stable and will be managed at home. Which property of linezolid makes it well suited to this plan?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It can be given orally in the outpatient setting

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is dosed as a single intramuscular injection

choices.label: C
choices.text: It must be combined with a beta-lactam to be active

choices.label: D
choices.text: It requires intravenous infusion through a central line

choices.label: E
choices.text: It requires weekly serum drug level monitoring

explanation.summary: Linezolid is administered orally, allowing MRSA to be treated outside the hospital.
explanation.whyCorrect: Linezolid covers gram-positive bacteria including MRSA and VRE, and it is administered orally, so it can be used in an outpatient setting. That oral route is what distinguishes it practically from vancomycin for a stable patient who does not need admission.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Linezolid is not administered as a one-time intramuscular dose.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Linezolid does not depend on a beta-lactam partner for its gram-positive activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Linezolid is given orally, which is precisely why it suits outpatient management.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Routine weekly drug level monitoring is not the feature that makes linezolid useful here.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: Which of the following drug combinations represents a streptogramin?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin/clavulanate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ampicillin/sulbactam

choices.label: C
choices.text: Piperacillin/tazobactam

choices.label: D
choices.text: Quinupristin/dalfopristin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole

explanation.summary: Quinupristin/dalfopristin is the streptogramin combination.
explanation.whyCorrect: The streptogramins are represented by quinupristin/dalfopristin, a 50S protein synthesis inhibitor with excellent gram-positive coverage including MRSA.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin/clavulanate is a beta-lactam paired with a beta-lactamase inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ampicillin/sulbactam is likewise a beta-lactam with a beta-lactamase inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Piperacillin/tazobactam is a beta-lactam plus beta-lactamase inhibitor combination.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole is a folate pathway combination, not a ribosomal agent.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A hospitalized patient with a methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection cannot receive vancomycin, and quinupristin/dalfopristin is considered. This agent is expected to provide which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excellent anaerobic coverage below the diaphragm

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excellent atypical coverage including Legionella

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excellent coverage of tick-borne Rickettsia species

choices.label: D
choices.text: Excellent gram-negative coverage including Pseudomonas

choices.label: E
choices.text: Excellent gram-positive coverage including MRSA

explanation.summary: Streptogramins give excellent gram-positive coverage, MRSA included.
explanation.whyCorrect: Streptogramins such as quinupristin/dalfopristin have coverage similar to vancomycin, meaning excellent gram-positive activity, and that activity extends to MRSA. This is why they are considered when a vancomycin-like gram-positive agent is needed but vancomycin itself cannot be used.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anaerobic coverage below the diaphragm is not provided by the streptogramins.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Atypical coverage including Legionella is a macrolide strength, not a streptogramin one.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tick-borne Rickettsia infections are treated first-line with doxycycline.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Coverage of Pseudomonas and other gram-negatives belongs to agents such as aztreonam.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: Compared with the streptogramins, linezolid is distinguished by additional reliable activity against which of the following organisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Legionella pneumophila pneumonia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rickettsia rickettsii infection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococci

explanation.summary: Both agents cover MRSA, but linezolid also covers VRE.
explanation.whyCorrect: Linezolid and the streptogramins both deliver excellent gram-positive coverage that includes MRSA. Linezolid is the agent that additionally covers vancomycin-resistant Enterococci, which is the point of difference emphasized here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Legionella is an atypical organism covered by macrolides, not by linezolid.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mycoplasma is an atypical pathogen treated with macrolides or doxycycline.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pseudomonas is a gram-negative organism outside the spectrum of both agents.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rickettsia rickettsii is treated with doxycycline, not with gram-positive agents.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 9-year-old boy develops fever, headache, and a rash several days after a tick bite, and Rocky Mountain spotted fever is diagnosed. Which of the following is the treatment of choice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cephalexin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: E
choices.text: Linezolid

explanation.summary: Rocky Mountain spotted fever is treated with doxycycline.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ticks, fleas, and lice transmit atypical bacteria that cause potentially life-threatening disease, and for most of these infections doxycycline is the first-line treatment. Rocky Mountain spotted fever, caused by Rickettsia rickettsii, is treated with doxycycline.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azithromycin is first-line for Legionnaires' disease, not for Rickettsia infections.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cephalosporins do not cover the atypical bacteria that cause tick-borne illness.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clindamycin targets aerobic gram-positive cocci and anaerobes above the diaphragm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Linezolid provides gram-positive coverage such as MRSA and VRE, not rickettsial coverage.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 30-year-old hiker develops fever and a rash after a tick bite, and doxycycline is started for Rocky Mountain spotted fever. Which of the following organisms is responsible for this disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Borrelia burgdorferi

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ehrlichia chaffeensis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Legionella pneumophila

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mycoplasma pneumoniae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rickettsia rickettsii

explanation.summary: Rocky Mountain spotted fever is caused by Rickettsia rickettsii.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the fastidious and vector-borne pathogens, Rocky Mountain spotted fever is attributed to Rickettsia rickettsii, and its first-line treatment is doxycycline.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Borrelia burgdorferi causes Lyme disease, also treated with doxycycline.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ehrlichia chaffeensis causes ehrlichiosis, a different tick-borne illness.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Legionella pneumophila causes Legionnaires' disease, treated with azithromycin or levofloxacin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mycoplasma pneumoniae is an atypical respiratory pathogen, not a tick-borne organism.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman is diagnosed with Lyme disease due to Borrelia burgdorferi after a tick exposure. Which of the following is the first-line treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: E
choices.text: Linezolid

explanation.summary: Lyme disease caused by B. burgdorferi is treated first-line with doxycycline.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lyme disease is one of the tick-borne atypical infections in which doxycycline is the first-line agent, alongside Rocky Mountain spotted fever and ehrlichiosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azithromycin is reserved as first-line for Legionnaires' disease among these infections.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aztreonam covers gram-negative organisms including Pseudomonas, not spirochetes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clindamycin covers aerobic gram-positive cocci and anaerobes above the diaphragm, not Borrelia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Linezolid is a gram-positive agent covering MRSA and VRE.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man develops fever and malaise after a tick bite, and testing confirms infection with Ehrlichia chaffeensis. Which of the following is the first-line treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Azithromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Levofloxacin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Linezolid

explanation.summary: Ehrlichiosis, caused by Ehrlichia chaffeensis, is treated with doxycycline.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ehrlichiosis joins Rocky Mountain spotted fever and Lyme disease in the group of vector-borne atypical infections for which doxycycline is first-line therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin is a beta-lactam with no activity against these atypical organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Azithromycin is first-line for Legionnaires' disease among these infections.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Levofloxacin is listed as an option for Legionnaires' disease, not for ehrlichiosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Linezolid is a gram-positive agent and does not treat Ehrlichia.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man is being treated for Legionnaires' disease but cannot tolerate azithromycin. Which of the following is an appropriate alternative first-line agent for this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cephalexin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Levofloxacin

explanation.summary: Legionnaires' disease is treated with azithromycin or levofloxacin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the fastidious pathogens, Legionella is the exception to the doxycycline rule: its listed first-line options are azithromycin or levofloxacin. When the macrolide cannot be used, levofloxacin is the alternative.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin is a beta-lactam that does not cover atypical organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aztreonam is aimed at gram-negative bacteria such as Pseudomonas, not Legionella.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cephalosporins do not cover any of the atypical bacteria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clindamycin has no atypical coverage and would not treat Legionella.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: What is the first-line treatment for infections caused by atypical bacteria transmitted by ticks, fleas, and lice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cephalexin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: E
choices.text: Linezolid

explanation.summary: Doxycycline is first-line for most vector-borne atypical infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ticks, fleas, and lice host atypical bacteria capable of causing life-threatening disease. From a treatment standpoint, doxycycline is the first-line agent in most of these cases, including Rocky Mountain spotted fever, Lyme disease, and ehrlichiosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azithromycin is reserved as first-line for Legionnaires' disease rather than the vector-borne group.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cephalosporins do not cover any of the atypical bacteria.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clindamycin targets gram-positive cocci and anaerobes above the diaphragm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Linezolid does not cover the atypicals; it covers gram-positives such as MRSA and VRE.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman comes to urgent care with shortness of breath, productive cough, and a temperature of 100.8°F. Chest radiograph shows a left lower lobe infiltrate, and pneumonia is diagnosed. She has a penicillin allergy and a documented history of QT prolongation and does not require hospitalization. Which of the following is the most appropriate empiric treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin/clavulanate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Azithromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clarithromycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Doxycycline

explanation.summary: With a penicillin allergy and QT prolongation, doxycycline is the empiric choice for outpatient CAP.
explanation.whyCorrect: Empiric outpatient options for community-acquired pneumonia in an otherwise healthy patient are amoxicillin/clavulanate, doxycycline, or a macrolide. Her penicillin allergy rules out amoxicillin/clavulanate, and macrolides increase the risk of QT prolongation, which she already has. Doxycycline remains and covers the expected typical and atypical pathogens.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin/clavulanate is inappropriate given her documented penicillin allergy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Azithromycin is a macrolide and would add to her risk of QT prolongation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clarithromycin is also a macrolide and carries the same QT prolongation concern.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clindamycin does not cover the atypical pathogens or Haemophilus and is not a CAP regimen.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman with outpatient community-acquired pneumonia has a penicillin allergy and a history of QT prolongation. Which of the following best explains why azithromycin is avoided in her case?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Macrolides are inactive against Streptococcus pneumoniae

choices.label: B
choices.text: Macrolides characteristically cause photosensitive reactions

choices.label: C
choices.text: Macrolides cross-react with a penicillin allergy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Macrolides increase the risk of QT prolongation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Macrolides lack activity against atypical organisms

explanation.summary: Macrolides are avoided in patients with QT prolongation because they increase that risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: Macrolides increase the risk of QT prolongation, so in a patient with a documented history of a prolonged QT interval they are not the preferred atypical coverage. Doxycycline can be used in place of the macrolide when such a contraindication exists.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Macrolides in fact have good activity against Streptococcus pneumoniae.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Photosensitive reactions are an adverse effect associated with doxycycline, not macrolides.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Macrolides are structurally unrelated to penicillins and are commonly used in penicillin-allergic patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Atypical coverage is the principal strength of the macrolide class.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman is discharged on doxycycline for community-acquired pneumonia and asked to keep recording her temperature and cough. Which of the following additional counseling points is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Expect a metallic taste whenever alcohol is consumed

choices.label: B
choices.text: Expect a permanent blue-gray discoloration of the skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obtain an electrocardiogram to follow the QT interval

choices.label: D
choices.text: Report any new ringing or fullness in the ears

choices.label: E
choices.text: Take measures to protect herself from sun exposure

explanation.summary: Doxycycline can cause photosensitive reactions, so patients should be advised on sun protection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Doxycycline use can cause photosensitive reactions. Patients started on it should be advised to protect themselves appropriately from the sun in addition to monitoring their symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A disulfiram-like metallic reaction with alcohol is not a doxycycline counseling point.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Permanent blue-gray skin discoloration is not the adverse effect associated with doxycycline here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: QT interval monitoring is the concern that applies to macrolides, which is why doxycycline was chosen instead.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ototoxic symptoms are not the adverse effect highlighted for doxycycline.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman with community-acquired pneumonia reports a penicillin allergy. Which of the following empiric options should be avoided specifically for that reason?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin/clavulanate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oral azithromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral clarithromycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral doxycycline

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral levofloxacin

explanation.summary: A penicillin allergy makes amoxicillin/clavulanate an inappropriate empiric CAP option.
explanation.whyCorrect: The three empiric outpatient options considered for this patient are amoxicillin/clavulanate, doxycycline, and a macrolide. Amoxicillin/clavulanate is penicillin based, so a documented penicillin allergy removes it from consideration.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Azithromycin is a macrolide and is not excluded by a penicillin allergy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clarithromycin is a macrolide, so it is limited by QT risk rather than by penicillin allergy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doxycycline is unrelated to the penicillins and is in fact the agent chosen here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Levofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone and carries no penicillin cross-reactivity concern.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A patient with vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus bacteremia is mistakenly prescribed aztreonam. Aztreonam's spectrum of activity is best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anaerobic organisms above the diaphragm

choices.label: B
choices.text: Atypical bacteria, including Legionella

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram-negative bacteria, including Pseudomonas

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gram-positive cocci, including MRSA

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tick-borne organisms, including Rickettsia

explanation.summary: Aztreonam covers many gram-negative bacteria, including Pseudomonas, so it cannot treat VRE.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aztreonam's activity is confined to gram-negative organisms, a group that includes Pseudomonas. Enterococcus is a gram-positive organism, so aztreonam would have no effect on VRE bacteremia; linezolid is the agent that covers VRE.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anaerobic coverage above the diaphragm describes clindamycin, not aztreonam.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Atypical coverage including Legionella is a macrolide property.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MRSA and other resistant gram-positives are covered by linezolid and the streptogramins.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tick-borne organisms such as Rickettsia are treated with doxycycline.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man with community-acquired pneumonia is treated with cefdinir alone and remains symptomatic after several days. Which of the following best explains the inadequate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cephalosporins are destroyed by normal gastric acid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cephalosporins do not cover Haemophilus influenzae

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cephalosporins do not cover Streptococcus pneumoniae

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cephalosporins do not cover the atypical bacteria

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cephalosporins do not reach the lung parenchyma

explanation.summary: Cephalosporins miss the atypical pathogens, so a beta-lactam alone is insufficient for CAP.
explanation.whyCorrect: Empiric CAP therapy must cover Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and the atypicals. Cephalosporins do not cover any of the atypical bacteria, which is why a macrolide, or doxycycline in its place, is paired with the beta-lactam.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gastric inactivation is not the explanation; cefdinir is an oral agent used in outpatient CAP.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Haemophilus coverage is part of why the beta-lactam is included in the regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A third-generation cephalosporin such as cefdinir is used in CAP precisely for typical pathogen coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Failure to reach lung tissue is not the reason cephalosporin monotherapy is inadequate in CAP.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 78-year-old man with a vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus infection is switched from amoxicillin to linezolid. Which of the following best explains this change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin cannot be combined with QT-prolonging drugs

choices.label: B
choices.text: Amoxicillin covers atypicals but not gram-positive organisms

choices.label: C
choices.text: Amoxicillin is a 50S inhibitor with a very narrow spectrum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Amoxicillin is not effective against VRE

choices.label: E
choices.text: Amoxicillin must be given intravenously for bacteremia

explanation.summary: Amoxicillin does not treat VRE, whereas linezolid covers vancomycin-resistant Enterococci.
explanation.whyCorrect: Amoxicillin is not effective against vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus. Linezolid covers gram-positive bacteria and specifically includes MRSA and VRE, making it the appropriate substitution.

whyWrongByChoice.A: QT prolongation is a macrolide concern and has nothing to do with amoxicillin here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Amoxicillin is a beta-lactam without atypical coverage, so this description is backwards.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Amoxicillin is a cell wall agent, not a 50S protein synthesis inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Route of administration is not the reason amoxicillin fails against VRE.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of drugs are both macrolides?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin and clarithromycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aztreonam and amoxicillin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cefdinir and cephalexin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Doxycycline and levofloxacin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Linezolid and clindamycin

explanation.summary: Azithromycin and clarithromycin are the macrolides among the 50S inhibitors.
explanation.whyCorrect: The 50S protein synthesis inhibitors include the macrolides, and azithromycin and clarithromycin are the macrolides named. They provide excellent atypical coverage as well as good activity against S. pneumoniae, Haemophilus, and Moraxella.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Aztreonam and amoxicillin are beta-lactams, not macrolides.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cefdinir and cephalexin are cephalosporins that act on the cell wall.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doxycycline is a tetracycline and levofloxacin is a respiratory fluoroquinolone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Linezolid and clindamycin are separate agents, neither of which is a macrolide.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: An outpatient community-acquired pneumonia regimen pairs a macrolide with a beta-lactam. Which of the following is the third-generation cephalosporin commonly used as the beta-lactam component?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amoxicillin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aztreonam

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cefdinir

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cephalexin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Piperacillin

explanation.summary: Cefdinir is the third-generation cephalosporin used with a macrolide in outpatient CAP.
explanation.whyCorrect: The common first-line outpatient CAP regimen uses a beta-lactam, usually a third-generation cephalosporin such as cefdinir or amoxicillin/clavulanate, combined with a macrolide for atypical coverage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amoxicillin is a penicillin-class agent, not a cephalosporin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aztreonam is a gram-negative agent and is not part of outpatient CAP therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cephalexin is a cephalosporin but is not the third-generation agent named for this regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Piperacillin is an extended-spectrum penicillin rather than a cephalosporin.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman is treated with azithromycin for a Chlamydia infection. Macrolides provide excellent coverage of Chlamydia and of which of the following additional groups of organisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacteroides and other gram-negative anaerobes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enterococcus and Staphylococcus species

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mycoplasma and Mycobacterium species

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pseudomonas and other aerobic gram-negative bacilli

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rickettsia and Ehrlichia species

explanation.summary: Macrolides cover the atypicals: Chlamydia, Mycoplasma, Mycobacterium, and Legionella.
explanation.whyCorrect: Excellent atypical coverage is the defining feature of the macrolides, and the atypical group named includes Chlamydia, Mycoplasma, Mycobacterium, and Legionella. That coverage is why macrolides are relied on for respiratory and other atypical infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gram-negative anaerobes are not covered by macrolides, and clindamycin misses them as well.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Resistant gram-positive organisms such as VRE and MRSA are covered by linezolid and the streptogramins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pseudomonas and related gram-negative bacilli fall to agents such as aztreonam.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rickettsia and Ehrlichia infections are treated first-line with doxycycline.

questions.topicName: Spectrum of Activity and Indications–4 50S inhibitors

questions.stem: A hospital quality committee is writing the charter for a new program and asks a resident to state in one sentence what antibiotic stewardship is meant to accomplish. Which of the following best describes the purpose of antibiotic stewardship?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eliminating all antibiotic use outside of the intensive care unit

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ensuring that every admitted patient receives at least one antibiotic dose

choices.label: C
choices.text: Optimizing patient outcomes while minimizing resistance and adverse drug events

choices.label: D
choices.text: Replacing culture-based diagnosis with empiric treatment for all infections

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reserving every antibiotic on the formulary for infectious disease consultation

explanation.summary: Antibiotic stewardship is a coordinated effort to improve antibiotic use so that patient outcomes are optimized while resistance and adverse drug events are minimized.
explanation.whyCorrect: Stewardship is defined as a coordinated effort to improve the use of antibiotics. Its three stated aims are to optimize patient outcomes, minimize the development of antibiotic resistance, and minimize adverse drug events. It works through strategies that ensure antibiotics are used appropriately, not through banning them.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Stewardship does not eliminate antibiotic use in any care setting; it makes that use appropriate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Giving every patient an antibiotic is the opposite of stewardship and drives unnecessary exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stewardship depends on cultures and susceptibilities to narrow therapy, not on abandoning them.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Restriction of select agents is only one stewardship intervention, not the definition of the program.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A student asks why vancomycin is never used to treat an Escherichia coli urinary tract infection, even in strains recovered from patients who have never received the drug. Which of the following best explains this observation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clavulanate is required before vancomycin can reach its cell wall target site

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prior antibiotic exposure has selected out a vancomycin-resistant subpopulation

choices.label: C
choices.text: The organism acquires a plasmid encoding vancomycin resistance from enterococci

choices.label: D
choices.text: The organism secretes an extended-spectrum beta-lactamase that degrades vancomycin

choices.label: E
choices.text: The vancomycin molecule is too large to penetrate the cell wall of E. coli

explanation.summary: E. coli is intrinsically resistant to vancomycin because the drug is too large to penetrate its cell wall.
explanation.whyCorrect: Intrinsic resistance is resistance that is natural to the organism and requires no previous drug exposure. E. coli is the classic example: vancomycin simply cannot get through the cell wall to reach its target, so the species is resistant from the outset. This is why glycopeptides are never an option for gram-negative infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clavulanate is a beta-lactamase inhibitor and has no role in vancomycin delivery or activity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Selection pressure explains emergence of resistance after exposure, which these strains never had.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acquired resistance involves gene transfer, but E. coli is resistant without acquiring anything.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Extended-spectrum beta-lactamases degrade penicillins and cephalosporins, not vancomycin.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: Resistance that is a natural property of an organism and is present without any prior antibiotic exposure is best termed which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acquired resistance

choices.label: B
choices.text: Empiric therapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enzyme inactivation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intrinsic resistance

choices.label: E
choices.text: Selection pressure

explanation.summary: Intrinsic resistance is resistance that is natural to the organism itself.
explanation.whyCorrect: Of the mechanisms by which bacteria resist antibiotics, intrinsic resistance is the one that is built into the species and requires no exposure, gene transfer, or enzyme production. The example given is E. coli and vancomycin, where the drug cannot cross the cell wall.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acquired resistance requires that resistance genes be taken up from another organism or the environment.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Empiric therapy is a prescribing strategy, not a bacterial resistance mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Enzyme inactivation requires the organism to produce an enzyme that destroys the drug.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Selection pressure requires antibiotic exposure that kills susceptible bacteria and leaves resistant ones.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A 68-year-old hospitalized woman receives a prolonged course of oral vancomycin. Two weeks later, stool surveillance cultures grow vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus, which was not present on admission. Which mechanism best explains this change in her gut flora?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enzymatic destruction of vancomycin by an extended-spectrum beta-lactamase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inadequate vancomycin dosing caused by a lack of pharmacokinetic monitoring

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intrinsic resistance of every Enterococcus species to glycopeptide antibiotics

choices.label: D
choices.text: Selection pressure that removed susceptible enterococci and let resistant ones predominate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transfer of a carbapenemase gene from Enterobacteriaceae into the enterococci

explanation.summary: Antibiotic exposure kills susceptible organisms and leaves resistant strains to multiply; this is selection pressure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Normal GI flora includes Enterococcus. When an antibiotic such as oral vancomycin eliminates the susceptible enterococci, the vancomycin-resistant enterococci that remain are free to multiply and become predominant. Emergence of VRE after vancomycin exposure is the example used for selection pressure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Extended-spectrum beta-lactamases act on penicillins and cephalosporins, not on vancomycin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Underdosing is not the described mechanism; the resistant population was selected by drug exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Enterococci are not intrinsically vancomycin resistant; many were susceptible in this patient on admission.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Carbapenemase genes confer beta-lactam resistance and would not produce vancomycin resistance.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines selection pressure as a mechanism of antibiotic resistance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibiotics kill susceptible bacteria, leaving behind resistant strains to multiply

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bacterial enzymes chemically degrade the antibiotic before it can reach its target

choices.label: C
choices.text: Resistance genes are picked up from fragments of dead bacteria in the environment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Resistance is an inherent property of the species and requires no drug exposure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum drug levels are monitored to keep antibiotic exposure in a therapeutic range

explanation.summary: Selection pressure is the survival and outgrowth of resistant strains after susceptible bacteria are killed by an antibiotic.
explanation.whyCorrect: Resistance occurs when antibiotics kill off the susceptible members of a bacterial population, leaving behind the more resistant strains to multiply. This is one of the four common mechanisms of resistance and is a major reason to limit unnecessary antibiotic exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Chemical degradation of the drug describes enzyme inactivation, such as beta-lactamase production.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Picking up resistance genes from the environment or another species describes acquired resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inherent, exposure-independent resistance describes intrinsic resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pharmacokinetic monitoring is a stewardship intervention, not a resistance mechanism.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: Whole-genome sequencing shows that a resistance gene carried by a patient's Klebsiella isolate is identical to one carried by an unrelated Escherichia coli isolate on the same ward, indicating that the gene moved between the two species. This transfer of resistance DNA between different species is best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acquired resistance

choices.label: B
choices.text: Empiric therapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intrinsic resistance

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pharmacokinetic failure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Selection pressure

explanation.summary: Acquired resistance is resistance DNA transferred between species or picked up from dead bacterial fragments in the environment.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacterial DNA containing resistance genes can be transferred between different species and can also be picked up from dead bacterial fragments in the environment. A resistance gene that is identical in two unrelated species is the signature of this acquired mechanism rather than of an inborn trait.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Empiric therapy is a treatment strategy used before an organism is identified.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Intrinsic resistance is native to a species and would not appear as a shared, mobile gene.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inadequate drug exposure is a dosing problem, not a mechanism of genetic resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Selection pressure enriches resistant organisms already present; it does not move genes between species.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A bacterial isolate is resistant to ampicillin alone, but susceptibility is restored when ampicillin is combined with sulbactam. Which resistance mechanism does this pattern indicate?

choices.label: A
