choices.text: Selection pressure has enriched a subpopulation with an altered drug target

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sulbactam itself has potent intrinsic activity against the isolated organism

choices.label: C
choices.text: The organism acquired resistance DNA from dead bacterial fragments nearby

choices.label: D
choices.text: The organism is intrinsically impermeable to all beta-lactam antibiotics

choices.label: E
choices.text: The organism produces a beta-lactamase that breaks the beta-lactam structure

explanation.summary: Restoration of activity by adding a beta-lactamase inhibitor identifies beta-lactamase-mediated enzyme inactivation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beta-lactamase is produced by some bacteria and breaks down the beta-lactam structure of beta-lactam antibiotics, rendering them ineffective. That is exactly why many beta-lactams are paired with beta-lactamase inhibitors such as clavulanate, sulbactam, and tazobactam; protecting the beta-lactam ring restores activity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A selected target mutation would not be reversed by adding an enzyme inhibitor to the regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sulbactam is used to protect the partner beta-lactam from enzymatic destruction, not as the active drug.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acquired resistance describes how a gene arrives, not the inhibitor-reversible enzyme itself.
whyWrongByChoice.D: True impermeability would leave the organism resistant whether or not sulbactam is added.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A beta-lactam antibiotic is being paired with a second agent whose purpose is to protect it from enzymatic destruction. Which of the following is such a beta-lactamase inhibitor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ceftaroline

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ciprofloxacin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Meropenem

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tazobactam

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin

explanation.summary: Clavulanate, sulbactam, and tazobactam are the beta-lactamase inhibitors paired with beta-lactam antibiotics.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because beta-lactamase breaks down the beta-lactam structure, many beta-lactam antibiotics are combined with a beta-lactamase inhibitor. The three named inhibitors are clavulanate, sulbactam, and tazobactam; the inhibitor shields the partner drug so it can reach its target.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftaroline is a fifth-generation cephalosporin, itself a beta-lactam antibiotic and not an inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone and has no effect on beta-lactamase enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Meropenem is a carbapenem used to treat organisms that produce extended-spectrum beta-lactamases.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vancomycin is a large glycopeptide with no beta-lactam ring and no inhibitory role.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A urine isolate of Escherichia coli from a nursing home resident is reported by the laboratory as an extended-spectrum beta-lactamase producer. Which of the following best characterizes this organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It became resistant only because susceptible organisms were killed by prior therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: It breaks down all penicillins and some cephalosporins and is usually treated with a carbapenem

choices.label: C
choices.text: It breaks down penicillins, most cephalosporins, and carbapenems, leaving very few options

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a gram-positive organism whose resistance comes from an altered cell wall target

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is intrinsically resistant to vancomycin because it acquired a plasmid-borne gene

explanation.summary: Extended-spectrum beta-lactamases are gram-negative enzymes that destroy all penicillins and some cephalosporins, so carbapenems are usually used.
explanation.whyCorrect: Extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs) are beta-lactamases produced by some gram-negative bacteria that break down all penicillins and some cephalosporins. These organisms can be difficult to kill, and carbapenems are the usual treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Selection pressure may enrich such strains, but the defining feature is the enzyme it produces.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Destruction of carbapenems as well defines carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae, not an ESBL producer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: ESBL production is a property of gram-negative organisms, and the mechanism is enzymatic drug destruction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Intrinsic vancomycin resistance in gram-negatives reflects drug size, not an acquired plasmid gene.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: Extended-spectrum beta-lactamases are characteristically produced by which group of organisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acid-fast bacilli

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gram-negative bacteria

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gram-positive cocci in chains

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gram-positive cocci in clusters

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spore-forming anaerobic rods

explanation.summary: ESBLs are produced by gram-negative bacteria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Extended-spectrum beta-lactamases are beta-lactamases produced by some gram-negative bacteria, and they break down all penicillins and some cephalosporins. Recognizing the gram-negative association is what points toward carbapenem therapy for these isolates.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acid-fast organisms are not the group associated with extended-spectrum beta-lactamase production.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Streptococci and enterococci are gram-positive; Enterococcus does not produce beta-lactamases.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Staphylococci are gram-positive and are not the organisms described as ESBL producers.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Anaerobic spore-forming rods are not described as the source of these enzymes.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: Two gram-negative isolates are recovered in an intensive care unit. Isolate 1 is killed by meropenem but by no penicillin or cephalosporin tested. Isolate 2 is killed by neither meropenem nor any penicillin or cephalosporin tested. Which statement best describes these isolates?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both isolates are carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both isolates are ordinary beta-lactamase producers treatable with an inhibitor combination

choices.label: C
choices.text: Isolate 1 is a carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae and isolate 2 is an ESBL producer

choices.label: D
choices.text: Isolate 1 is an ESBL producer and isolate 2 is a carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Isolate 1 is intrinsically beta-lactam resistant and isolate 2 reflects selection pressure

explanation.summary: ESBL producers are still killed by carbapenems, whereas carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae destroy carbapenems as well.
explanation.whyCorrect: ESBLs break down all penicillins and some cephalosporins, and carbapenems are the usual treatment, which matches isolate 1. Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae are multidrug-resistant gram-negative organisms whose enzymes break down penicillins, most cephalosporins, and carbapenems, which matches isolate 2.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Isolate 1 remains carbapenem susceptible, so it cannot be a carbapenem-resistant organism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ordinary beta-lactamase producers regain susceptibility with an inhibitor; neither isolate fits that pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This reverses the two isolates; the carbapenem-susceptible one is the ESBL producer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Intrinsic resistance and selection pressure do not explain enzyme-defined beta-lactam susceptibility patterns.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: An intensive care unit patient's blood culture grows a gram-negative rod reported as carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae. Which of the following best explains why this organism is called multidrug resistant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It becomes resistant only when a beta-lactamase inhibitor is given at the same time

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a gram-positive organism that requires ceftaroline for any adequate coverage

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is intrinsically impermeable to antibiotics because of unusually large membrane pores

choices.label: D
choices.text: It produces enzymes that break down penicillins, most cephalosporins, and carbapenems

choices.label: E
choices.text: It replaced susceptible flora after selection pressure from prior oral vancomycin use

explanation.summary: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae produce enzymes that destroy penicillins, most cephalosporins, and carbapenems.
explanation.whyCorrect: CRE are multidrug-resistant gram-negative organisms that produce enzymes capable of breaking down penicillins, most cephalosporins, and carbapenems. Because carbapenems are the fallback for ESBL producers, losing them is what makes these isolates so difficult to treat.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Beta-lactamase inhibitors are given to protect beta-lactams, and they do not create resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CRE are gram-negative; ceftaroline is noted for activity against resistant gram-positive organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The described mechanism is enzymatic destruction of beta-lactams, not a permeability property.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Selection pressure with vancomycin is the mechanism used to explain emergence of VRE in gut flora.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: Compared with community-acquired infections, hospital-acquired infections more often involve multidrug-resistant organisms and require broader-spectrum antibiotics. Which of the following best explains this difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Community-acquired pathogens are intrinsically resistant to more antibiotic classes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Heavy antibiotic use in hospitals drives selection pressure and acquired resistance

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hospital laboratories cannot perform susceptibility testing on most clinical isolates

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hospitalized patients absorb oral antibiotics far more rapidly than outpatients do

choices.label: E
choices.text: Narrow-spectrum antibiotics are unavailable on most inpatient hospital formularies

explanation.summary: Consistent antibiotic exposure in hospitals, especially intravenous therapy, selects for resistant organisms and promotes acquired resistance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antibiotic use in the hospital setting, especially intravenous antibiotics, is much more prevalent than in the community. That consistent exposure allows bacteria in healthcare settings to gain resistance through selection pressure and through acquired resistance, which is why hospital-acquired infections often need broader coverage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The excess of resistant organisms is in the healthcare setting, not in community pathogens.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Susceptibility testing is a routine part of inpatient care and guides definitive therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Differences in oral absorption do not explain the higher prevalence of resistant organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Narrow-spectrum agents are available and are in fact preferred once the organism is known.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: An antimicrobial stewardship program lists its aims in a hospital charter. Which of the following is among the stated goals of such a program?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eliminating the need for microbiology cultures

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increasing total antibiotic days per patient

choices.label: C
choices.text: Minimizing the development of resistance

choices.label: D
choices.text: Replacing targeted therapy with empiric therapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Restricting all prescribing to pharmacists

explanation.summary: Antimicrobial stewardship programs aim to optimize patient outcomes, minimize resistance development, and minimize adverse drug events.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hospitals implement Antimicrobial Stewardship Programs precisely to optimize patient outcomes, minimize the development of resistance, and minimize adverse drug events. Every ASP intervention, from restriction to audit and feedback, serves those three goals.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cultures are central to stewardship because they allow empiric therapy to be narrowed.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Longer and broader antibiotic exposure increases resistance and adverse events.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stewardship moves therapy from empiric toward targeted treatment, not the reverse.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Stewardship teams are collaborative and advise prescribers rather than replacing them.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A hospital is assembling the collaborative team that will run its antimicrobial stewardship program. Which combination of personnel best reflects such a team?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An outside accrediting agency that reviews prescribing once each calendar year

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bedside nurses alone, who record antibiotic administration times for every patient

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hospital administrators, billing staff, and the pharmacy purchasing department

choices.label: D
choices.text: Infectious disease physicians and pharmacists, microbiology lab, and infection prevention

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surgical residents who select the perioperative antibiotic for each operative case

explanation.summary: Stewardship programs are run by collaborative teams of infectious disease physicians and pharmacists, microbiology laboratory staff, and infection prevention personnel.
explanation.whyCorrect: ASPs consist of collaborative teams that establish antibiotic guidance for their facility, conduct audits of prescribing habits, and provide education to optimize practice and improve care. The described membership spans prescribing expertise, laboratory data, and infection prevention.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An annual external review cannot provide the ongoing guidance, audit, and education described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nursing documentation alone cannot set facility guidance or audit prescribing decisions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Administrative and purchasing functions do not supply the clinical and laboratory expertise required.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A single specialty choosing its own antibiotics is the practice that stewardship audits, not the team.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: As part of a stewardship intervention, a pharmacist routinely measures serum drug concentrations for two antibiotic classes and adjusts dosing accordingly. Which of the following is most appropriately monitored in this way?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Carbapenems and fluoroquinolones

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cephalosporins and beta-lactamase inhibitors

choices.label: C
choices.text: Macrolides and fluoroquinolones

choices.label: D
choices.text: Penicillins and macrolides

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vancomycin and aminoglycosides

explanation.summary: Pharmacokinetic monitoring is a stewardship intervention applied to antibiotics such as vancomycin and aminoglycosides.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the listed ASP interventions is pharmacokinetic monitoring of some antibiotics, with vancomycin and aminoglycosides given as the examples. Monitoring levels keeps exposure effective while limiting adverse drug events, one of the three stewardship aims.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Carbapenems and fluoroquinolones are chosen by susceptibility, not managed by serum levels here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cephalosporins and beta-lactamase inhibitors are not the examples given for pharmacokinetic monitoring.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neither macrolides nor fluoroquinolones are the monitored classes described.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Penicillins and macrolides are not the agents named for routine level monitoring.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A stewardship program implements software that rapidly identifies pathogens from positive cultures and alerts the treating team. What is the principal benefit of this intervention?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It allows every patient to be treated with one single broad-spectrum agent

choices.label: B
choices.text: It guarantees that no patient receiving antibiotics will have an adverse event

choices.label: C
choices.text: It removes the need to obtain any cultures before starting antibiotic therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: It replaces the susceptibility panel performed by the microbiology laboratory

choices.label: E
choices.text: It shortens the time to starting effective treatment for the infected patient

explanation.summary: Clinical decision support software speeds pathogen identification and therefore shortens time to effective therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: One listed ASP intervention is the use of clinical decision support software to rapidly identify pathogens and shorten the time to starting effective treatment. Faster identification lets the team move from a best-guess empiric regimen to therapy that actually covers the organism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The point of faster identification is to narrow therapy, not to standardize broad coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Stewardship reduces adverse drug events but no intervention can guarantee their absence.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cultures remain essential; the software works on the culture results themselves.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Susceptibility testing is still performed and is what triggers definitive therapy.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: Ceftaroline is placed on a hospital's approval-required list so that it cannot be ordered without stewardship sign-off. Which stewardship intervention does this represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clinical decision support alerting

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intravenous to oral conversion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pharmacokinetic monitoring

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prospective audit and feedback

choices.label: E
choices.text: Restriction of select antibiotics

explanation.summary: Requiring approval before an agent can be used is restriction of a select antibiotic.
explanation.whyCorrect: Restriction of select antibiotics, with ceftaroline given as the example, is one of the listed ASP interventions. Restricting an agent reserves it for infections caused by the pathogens it uniquely covers, limiting exposure and preserving the drug.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Decision support software speeds pathogen identification rather than gating orders.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intravenous to oral conversion changes the route of an agent already in use.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pharmacokinetic monitoring adjusts dosing using measured serum drug levels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Audit and feedback reviews therapy already started and advises the prescriber afterward.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: Each week, a stewardship pharmacist reviews the charts of patients already receiving selected antibiotics and contacts the prescriber with recommendations to modify therapy. Which intervention is being described?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clinical decision support software used for rapid pathogen identification

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pharmacokinetic monitoring of measured serum drug concentrations

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prospective audit and feedback to the prescriber of the antibiotic

choices.label: D
choices.text: Restriction of a select antibiotic before the first dose is given

choices.label: E
choices.text: Timely transition from intravenous to oral antibiotic administration

explanation.summary: Reviewing ongoing therapy and giving recommendations back to the prescriber is prospective audit and feedback.
explanation.whyCorrect: Prospective audit and feedback to prescribers of selected antibiotics is one of the listed ASP interventions. It complements restriction: restriction acts before the drug is released, whereas audit and feedback acts on therapy that is already under way.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No software-based pathogen identification is described in this workflow.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pharmacokinetic monitoring involves measuring drug levels, which is not described here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Restriction blocks or gates the order before therapy starts rather than reviewing it later.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Route conversion is a specific recommendation, not the review process itself.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A patient with pneumonia has been afebrile for 24 hours, is tolerating a regular diet, and is improving on intravenous antibiotics. The stewardship team recommends switching him to an oral agent with equivalent coverage. This recommendation is an example of which intervention?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Empiric broadening of the antibiotic spectrum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pharmacokinetic monitoring of the antibiotic level

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prospective audit of the microbiology laboratory

choices.label: D
choices.text: Restriction of a select antibiotic

choices.label: E
choices.text: Timely transition from intravenous to oral therapy

explanation.summary: Moving an improving patient from intravenous to oral antibiotics is a standard stewardship intervention.
explanation.whyCorrect: Timely transition from intravenous to oral antibiotics is one of the listed ASP interventions. Since intravenous antibiotic use in hospitals is a major driver of resistance and of drug-related harm, converting to oral therapy when a patient is improving serves the stewardship goals.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Broadening therapy in an improving patient is the opposite of good stewardship.
whyWrongByChoice.B: No serum drug concentration is being measured or used to adjust the dose.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Audit and feedback targets prescribers of selected antibiotics, not the laboratory.
whyWrongByChoice.D: No agent is being reserved or gated behind approval in this scenario.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A restricted antibiotic on a hospital formulary is the only fifth-generation cephalosporin available. Which of the following best describes its spectrum of activity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It covers anaerobic organisms exclusively and is used for intra-abdominal infections

choices.label: B
choices.text: It covers extended-spectrum beta-lactamase producers better than carbapenems do

choices.label: C
choices.text: It covers many multidrug-resistant gram-positive organisms, including MRSA and VRE

choices.label: D
choices.text: It covers only gram-negative organisms, including carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae

choices.label: E
choices.text: It covers only susceptible streptococci and has no activity against staphylococci

explanation.summary: Ceftaroline, the only fifth-generation cephalosporin, is unique for its activity against multidrug-resistant gram-positive organisms including MRSA and VRE.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ceftaroline is given as the example of a restricted antibiotic. It is the only fifth-generation cephalosporin available and is unique because it has activity against a broad range of multidrug-resistant gram-positive organisms, including MRSA and VRE, which is exactly why it is worth preserving.

whyWrongByChoice.A: It is not described as an anaerobe-specific agent for intra-abdominal infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Carbapenems are the agents usually used for extended-spectrum beta-lactamase producers.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Its distinguishing feature is gram-positive coverage, not activity against resistant gram-negatives.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Coverage limited to susceptible streptococci would not justify restricting the drug.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A fifth-generation cephalosporin with activity against MRSA and VRE is reserved for infections known to be caused by those pathogens rather than being used broadly. What is the best rationale for this policy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It causes more adverse drug events than any other cephalosporin on the formulary

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is the only available antibiotic that can be administered by the oral route

choices.label: C
choices.text: Its serum concentrations cannot be measured, so its dose cannot be individualized

choices.label: D
choices.text: Limiting exposure limits resistance and preserves the drug's coverage for the future

choices.label: E
choices.text: The drug is inactive against gram-positive organisms unless combined with vancomycin

explanation.summary: Restricting a uniquely active agent limits bacterial exposure to it and preserves its usefulness.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ceftaroline is restricted, or reserved, for certain infections with known resistant pathogens in order to limit exposure, meaning bacterial resistance, and maintain coverage. The same selection-pressure logic that drives resistance in general is what justifies protecting a last-line agent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Toxicity is not the stated reason the drug is reserved for selected pathogens.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Route of administration has nothing to do with why the agent is restricted.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pharmacokinetic monitoring is applied to vancomycin and aminoglycosides, not used as the rationale here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: It is restricted because of its unusual gram-positive activity, not because it lacks activity.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: Why is a narrow-spectrum antibiotic preferred over a broad-spectrum antibiotic once the causative organism is known?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is always less expensive than every available broad-spectrum alternative

choices.label: B
choices.text: It kills a wider range of bacteria, including the beneficial organisms

choices.label: C
choices.text: It minimizes disruption of the normal microbiome and reduces resistance risk

choices.label: D
choices.text: It reaches a therapeutic serum concentration faster in every infected patient

choices.label: E
choices.text: It removes any need for culture and susceptibility testing in that patient

explanation.summary: Narrow-spectrum drugs target only the bacteria causing the infection, sparing the microbiome and lowering resistance risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: Narrow-spectrum drugs target only specific types of bacteria, which minimizes disruption to the normal gut microbiome and reduces the risk of developing antibiotic resistance by targeting only the bacteria causing the infection. Narrow-spectrum therapy is therefore preferred when the causative organism is known.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cost is considered when selecting definitive therapy, but it is not the reason narrow is preferred.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Killing a wider range of bacteria, including beneficial ones, describes broad-spectrum therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Speed of reaching drug levels is not the stated advantage of a narrower spectrum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cultures and susceptibilities are what make narrow-spectrum therapy possible in the first place.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A patient with a culture-proven infection caused by a fully susceptible organism is left on a broad-spectrum antibiotic despite the susceptibility report. Which consequence is most likely to result from this unnecessary broad-spectrum use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Beneficial bacteria will be killed and resistance development will increase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intrinsic resistance will develop within the isolated organism over 48 hours

choices.label: C
choices.text: The isolate will lose its resistance genes through ongoing selection pressure

choices.label: D
choices.text: The laboratory will be unable to report the final susceptibility results

choices.label: E
choices.text: The patient's antibiotic will need conversion from oral to intravenous dosing

explanation.summary: Broad-spectrum antibiotics kill beneficial bacteria along with pathogens and increase resistance development when used unnecessarily.
explanation.whyCorrect: Broad-spectrum antibiotics kill a wider range of bacteria, including beneficial ones, which can lead to increased resistance development when they are used unnecessarily. Once susceptibilities are known, staying broad provides no added benefit while carrying that cost.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Intrinsic resistance is a native species property and does not develop during a course of therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Selection pressure enriches resistant organisms rather than removing resistance genes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Continuing an antibiotic does not prevent the laboratory from reporting susceptibilities.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Stewardship moves therapy from intravenous toward oral, not the reverse.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: An attending compares two prescribing strategies by saying that one is like using a precision screwdriver to repair a delicate watch while the other is like using a hammer. Which pairing best fits this comparison?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Broad-spectrum therapy is the screwdriver and narrow-spectrum therapy is the hammer

choices.label: B
choices.text: Empiric therapy is the screwdriver and culture-directed therapy is the hammer

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibitor combinations are the screwdriver and carbapenem therapy is the hammer

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intravenous therapy is the screwdriver and oral step-down therapy is the hammer

choices.label: E
choices.text: Narrow-spectrum therapy is the screwdriver and broad-spectrum therapy is the hammer

explanation.summary: Narrow-spectrum therapy targets the pathogen precisely, while broad-spectrum therapy causes collateral damage to beneficial flora.
explanation.whyCorrect: A precision screwdriver targets specific screws without damaging the intricate mechanisms inside, just as narrow-spectrum antibiotics target specific bacteria without disrupting the beneficial ones. A hammer causes unnecessary damage, similar to how broad-spectrum antibiotics harm beneficial bacteria and increase resistance when used unnecessarily.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This reverses the analogy; the imprecise tool corresponds to broad-spectrum coverage.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Culture-directed therapy is the precise strategy, so this pairing is inverted.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The analogy contrasts narrow with broad coverage rather than specific drug classes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The comparison concerns spectrum of activity, not the route of administration.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: Escherichia coli cannot be treated with vancomycin under any circumstance, whereas Enterococcus in the gut is often vancomycin susceptible until a patient receives a course of vancomycin. Which statement best explains the difference between these two situations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both organisms illustrate acquired resistance transferred from dead bacterial fragments

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both organisms produce extended-spectrum beta-lactamases that degrade vancomycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: E. coli illustrates intrinsic resistance while Enterococcus illustrates selection pressure

choices.label: D
choices.text: E. coli illustrates selection pressure while Enterococcus illustrates intrinsic resistance

choices.label: E
choices.text: E. coli resistance is enzymatic while enterococcal resistance reflects underdosing

explanation.summary: E. coli is naturally vancomycin resistant, whereas VRE emerges only after vancomycin exposure removes susceptible enterococci.
explanation.whyCorrect: E. coli is intrinsically resistant to vancomycin because the antibiotic is too large to penetrate its cell wall, so no exposure is required. Enterococcus is the example of selection pressure: when antibiotics such as oral vancomycin eliminate susceptible enterococci, vancomycin-resistant enterococci become predominant.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neither example depends on uptake of resistance DNA from the environment.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Vancomycin has no beta-lactam ring, so beta-lactamases cannot explain either finding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This reverses the two mechanisms; exposure-independent resistance belongs to E. coli.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neither pattern is explained by enzymatic destruction of vancomycin or by inadequate dosing.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes empiric antibiotic therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A best-guess regimen started before the causative organism has been identified

choices.label: B
choices.text: A regimen selected solely on the basis of the acquisition cost of the drug

choices.label: C
choices.text: Antibiotics given to a healthy person in order to prevent a future infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Therapy chosen after culture and susceptibility results have already returned

choices.label: E
choices.text: Therapy given only to patients with a proven, fully identified bacterial pathogen

explanation.summary: Empiric therapy is the best guess at coverage for a proven or suspected infection before the organism is known.
explanation.whyCorrect: Empiric therapy is the best guess of antibiotic coverage for a patient with a proven or suspected infection where an organism has not yet been identified. Broad-spectrum agents can be warranted empirically and are narrowed later once the organism is identified.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cost is one consideration in selecting definitive therapy, not the definition of empiric therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Empiric therapy treats a proven or suspected infection rather than preventing one.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Therapy chosen after susceptibilities return is definitive, or targeted, therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Empiric therapy is used precisely when the pathogen has not yet been identified.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A patient with a severe infection of unknown source is started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. Two days later, cultures identify a single organism with a full susceptibility panel. According to stewardship principles, what should happen next?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a second broad-spectrum agent to keep resistance from emerging

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continue the original broad-spectrum regimen for the full planned course

choices.label: C
choices.text: Narrow therapy to a targeted agent active against the identified organism

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stop all antibiotics and repeat the cultures before treating any further

choices.label: E
choices.text: Substitute a restricted agent that is reserved for resistant pathogens

explanation.summary: Broad empiric coverage should be narrowed to targeted therapy once the organism and susceptibilities are known.
explanation.whyCorrect: Broad-spectrum antibiotics can be warranted for empiric therapy, and they can be narrowed later in order to minimize pathogen exposure, decreasing the chance for resistance, and to reduce adverse drug effects. After culture and sensitivity results are known, targeted treatment can begin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adding coverage broadens exposure further and is the opposite of stewardship.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Staying broad after susceptibilities return increases resistance risk and adverse drug events.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The organism and its susceptibilities are already known, so treatment should continue in targeted form.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Restricted agents are reserved for infections caused by the resistant pathogens they uniquely cover.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: Which of the following best characterizes definitive, or targeted, antibiotic therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Treatment based only on the patient's recent antibiotic exposures and risk factors

choices.label: B
choices.text: Treatment chosen by the microbiology laboratory rather than by the treating physician

choices.label: C
choices.text: Treatment selected after cultures and susceptibilities identify the causative organism

choices.label: D
choices.text: Treatment started immediately before any specimens have been collected for culture

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treatment that always employs the broadest antibiotic spectrum that is available

explanation.summary: Definitive, or targeted, therapy is given once culture and susceptibility results identify the organism and the drugs that will work.
explanation.whyCorrect: After culture and sensitivity results are known, the targeted, or definitive, treatment can begin. Unlike empiric therapy, with targeted therapy we know which organism we are treating and which antibiotics will work against it, which allows the regimen to be narrow, safe, effective, and cost effective.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Using recent exposures and likely pathogens to guess coverage describes empiric therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The laboratory supplies identification and susceptibilities; the physician selects the regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Treatment started before specimens are obtained is empiric, not definitive, therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Definitive therapy should be as narrow as the susceptibility data allow.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: Once an organism and its susceptibilities are known, several active agents are available. Which set of characteristics should guide the choice of definitive therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Broadest spectrum, intravenous route, longest duration, and highest tolerated dose

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lowest acquisition price regardless of activity against the identified isolate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Newest agent, restricted status, parenteral administration, and hospital supply

choices.label: D
choices.text: Safe, effective, narrow in spectrum, and cost effective for the treated patient

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whichever antibiotic the patient happened to receive during a prior admission

explanation.summary: Good stewardship selects definitive therapy that is safe, effective, narrow in spectrum, and cost effective.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once the organism and susceptibilities are known, it is important to be prudent and a good antibiotic steward by choosing drugs that are safe, effective, narrow in spectrum, and cost effective. Narrow spectrum limits microbiome disruption and resistance, while safety limits adverse drug events.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Choosing the broadest, longest, highest-dose option maximizes exactly the harms stewardship avoids.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cost matters only among agents that are actually active and safe for the isolate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Novelty and restricted status are not selection criteria; restricted drugs are reserved, not preferred.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prior antibiotic exposure raises the risk of resistance rather than guiding definitive choice.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A febrile patient is suspected of having a serious bacterial infection. Following the standard approach to infectious diseases, at which point should empiric antibiotic therapy be started?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Before any specimens are collected, so that treatment is not delayed

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immediately after cultures have been obtained from the suspected sites

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only once the full susceptibility panel has returned for the isolate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only once the Gram stain result has been reported by the laboratory

choices.label: E
choices.text: Only once the organism has been identified to the species level

explanation.summary: Empiric therapy for likely pathogens begins once suspected sites have been cultured, before identification and susceptibilities return.
explanation.whyCorrect: The general approach runs from suspecting infection, to culturing the suspected sites, to Gram stain, to identification, to susceptibilities. Empiric therapy for likely pathogens is begun at the culturing step, since identification and susceptibilities take about 48 hours and treatment cannot wait that long.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Starting before cultures are drawn can obscure the organism and prevent later narrowing.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Susceptibility results mark the switch to definitive therapy, not the start of treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Waiting for the Gram stain delays treatment that should already be under way.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Identification takes roughly two days, far too long to withhold therapy in a sick patient.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: In the standard sequence of suspecting infection, culturing suspected sites, performing a Gram stain, identifying the organism, and obtaining susceptibilities, at which step is therapy switched to a patient-specific definitive regimen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: When specimens are collected for culture

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the Gram stain morphology is reported

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the infection is first clinically suspected

choices.label: D
choices.text: When the patient first becomes afebrile

choices.label: E
choices.text: When the susceptibility results become available

explanation.summary: Definitive therapy for the patient-specific pathogen begins when susceptibilities are known.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the general approach to infectious diseases, the switch to definitive therapy for the patient-specific pathogen occurs at the susceptibility step. Only then do we know both which organism is being treated and which antibiotics will work against it.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Culturing is the step at which empiric therapy is begun, not definitive therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A Gram stain narrows the possibilities but does not identify the drugs that will work.
whyWrongByChoice.C: At the point of suspicion nothing is known about the organism or its drug susceptibility.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clinical defervescence does not supply the organism-specific data definitive therapy requires.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease presents with fever, productive cough, and worsening shortness of breath over 48 hours. He is tachycardic and febrile to 101.3 F, with diminished breath sounds at the left base and left lower lobe consolidation on chest radiograph. One month ago he was hospitalized for a urinary tract infection and completed a 7-day course of ciprofloxacin. Which feature most increases the likelihood that his pneumonia is caused by a multidrug-resistant organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: His age of 72 years at the time of this presentation

choices.label: B
choices.text: His recent hospitalization with a 7-day course of ciprofloxacin

choices.label: C
choices.text: His temperature of 101.3 F with accompanying tachycardia

choices.label: D
choices.text: The diminished breath sounds over the left lower lung field

choices.label: E
choices.text: The lobar consolidation seen on his chest radiograph

explanation.summary: Recent hospitalization and recent antibiotic exposure are the features that predict a multidrug-resistant pathogen.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antibiotic use in the hospital setting is prevalent and drives resistance through selection pressure and acquired resistance, so a recent admission plus a recent course of ciprofloxacin makes a resistant organism far more likely. Empiric therapy is a best guess built on exactly these recent exposures and the common pathogens for the syndrome.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Age alone does not indicate that the infecting organism will be multidrug resistant.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fever and tachycardia reflect the severity of infection rather than its resistance profile.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Diminished breath sounds localize the consolidation and do not predict resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Consolidation confirms pneumonia but says nothing about the susceptibility of the pathogen.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A hospitalized patient with pneumonia asks how long it will take, after his sputum and blood samples reach the microbiology laboratory, to learn which organism is responsible and which antibiotics will kill it. Which is the most accurate answer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: About 2 hours

choices.label: B
choices.text: About 7 days

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 8 hours

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 14 days

choices.label: E
choices.text: About 48 hours

explanation.summary: Identification and susceptibility results generally take about 48 hours after samples reach the laboratory.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once samples are sent to the lab it takes about 48 hours to identify the organism and discover its susceptibilities. That delay is exactly why empiric therapy, the best guess based on recent exposures and common pathogens, is started while the cultures incubate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Two hours is far too short for culture growth, identification, and susceptibility testing.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A week-long wait would make targeted therapy impossible within a typical treatment course.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Results are not available the same day; empiric coverage bridges a roughly two-day gap.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Two weeks greatly overstates the turnaround for routine identification and susceptibilities.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: A hospitalized man with pneumonia has been receiving empiric therapy with a broad-spectrum beta-lactam plus a macrolide. Cultures now grow a multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae that is resistant to ciprofloxacin and to the empiric beta-lactam but susceptible to carbapenems. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add oral vancomycin to the regimen to cover resistant gut organisms as well

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continue the current empiric beta-lactam and macrolide regimen unchanged

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stop all antibiotics and observe the patient off therapy for the next 48 hours

choices.label: D
choices.text: Substitute ciprofloxacin, since he responded to that drug during a prior illness

choices.label: E
choices.text: Switch to targeted therapy with meropenem based on the susceptibility report

explanation.summary: Once susceptibilities show the empiric drug is inactive, therapy is switched to a targeted agent that the organism is susceptible to.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is the definitive therapy step: the organism is known, and the report shows it is resistant to the empiric beta-lactam but susceptible to carbapenems, so the patient is switched to a targeted regimen of meropenem. Carbapenems are also the usual choice for the difficult-to-kill resistant gram-negative organisms described in this brick.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Oral vancomycin does not treat gram-negative pneumonia and would select for resistant enterococci.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The isolate is resistant to the empiric beta-lactam, so continuing it leaves the infection untreated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Withholding therapy in a patient with proven multidrug-resistant pneumonia is unsafe.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The isolate is explicitly reported as resistant to ciprofloxacin, which he recently received.

questions.topicName: Antibiotic Stewardship

questions.stem: Besides limiting the development of resistance, narrowing a patient's antibiotic regimen once the pathogen has been identified accomplishes which additional goal of antibiotic stewardship?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It eliminates the requirement to obtain cultures during future admissions

choices.label: B
choices.text: It increases the total number of antibiotic days delivered to the patient

choices.label: C
choices.text: It reduces the patient's risk of experiencing adverse drug effects

choices.label: D
choices.text: It removes the need for pharmacokinetic monitoring in every treated patient

choices.label: E
choices.text: It shifts prescribing responsibility from the physician to the microbiology lab

explanation.summary: Narrowing therapy serves the stewardship goal of minimizing adverse drug events as well as limiting resistance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Broad-spectrum empiric agents are narrowed later in order to minimize pathogen exposure, decreasing the chance for resistance, and to reduce adverse drug effects. Minimizing adverse drug events is one of the three explicit aims of stewardship, alongside optimizing outcomes and limiting resistance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cultures remain the basis for identifying organisms and narrowing therapy in every episode.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Narrowing reduces unnecessary exposure rather than lengthening the antibiotic course.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Drug level monitoring is still applied to agents such as vancomycin and aminoglycosides.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The laboratory reports data; the prescriber still chooses and adjusts the regimen.
